<a id="dds-layer-domainparticipant-creation"></a>

<a id="creating-a-domainparticipant"></a>

# Creating a DomainParticipant

Creation of a [DomainParticipant](domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) is done with the [`create_participant()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory18create_participantE10DomainId_tRK20DomainParticipantQosP25DomainParticipantListenerRK10StatusMask)
member function on the
[DomainParticipantFactory](../domainParticipantFactory/domainParticipantFactory.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantfactory) singleton, that acts as a factory for the DomainParticipant.
Then, when the lifecycle of the participant finishes, every participant must be deleted with
[`delete_participant()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory18delete_participantEP17DomainParticipant).
Please refer to [Deleting a DomainParticipant](#dds-layer-domainparticipant-deletion) for further details on the deletion of a participant.

Mandatory arguments are:

* The `DomainId` that identifies the domain where the DomainParticipant will be created.
* The [DomainParticipantQos](domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantqos) describing the behavior of the DomainParticipant.
  If the provided value is `PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT`, the value of the DomainParticipantQos is used.

Alternatively, instead of the two mandatory arguments above, you can use:

* The [DomainParticipantExtendedQos](domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantextendedqos) which encompasses both the `DomainId` and
  the [DomainParticipantQos](domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantqos).

Optional arguments are:

* A Listener derived from [DomainParticipantListener](../domainParticipantListener/domainParticipantListener.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantlistener), implementing the callbacks
  that will be triggered in response to events and state changes on the DomainParticipant.
  By default empty callbacks are used.
* A [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) that activates or deactivates triggering of individual callbacks on the
  [DomainParticipantListener](../domainParticipantListener/domainParticipantListener.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantlistener).

#### WARNING
Following the [DDSI-RTPS V2.2](https://www.omg.org/spec/DDSI-RTPS/2.2/PDF) standard (Section 9.6.1.1), the default ports are calculated depending on the
`DomainId`, as it is explained in section [Well Known Ports](../../../transport/listening_locators.md#listening-locators-defaultports).
Thus, it is encouraged to use `DomainId` lower than 200
(over `DomainId` 233 default port assign will fail consistently).

[`create_participant()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory18create_participantE10DomainId_tRK20DomainParticipantQosP25DomainParticipantListenerRK10StatusMask)
will return a null pointer if there was an error during the operation, e.g.
if the provided QoS is not compatible or is not supported.
It is advisable to check that the returned value is a valid pointer.

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant with default DomainParticipantQos and no Listener
// The value PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT is used to denote the default QoS.
DomainParticipant* participant_with_default_attributes =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant_with_default_attributes)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// A custom DomainParticipantQos can be provided to the creation method
DomainParticipantQos custom_qos;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

DomainParticipant* participant_with_custom_qos =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, custom_qos);
if (nullptr == participant_with_custom_qos)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DomainParticipant with default QoS and a custom Listener.
// CustomDomainParticipantListener inherits from DomainParticipantListener.
// The value PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT is used to denote the default QoS.
CustomDomainParticipantListener custom_listener;
DomainParticipant* participant_with_default_qos_and_custom_listener =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT,
                &custom_listener);
if (nullptr == participant_with_default_qos_and_custom_listener)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-domainparticipant-creation-profile"></a>

<a id="profile-based-creation-of-a-domainparticipant"></a>

## Profile based creation of a DomainParticipant

Instead of using a DomainParticipantQos, the name of a profile
can be used to create a DomainParticipant with the [`create_participant_with_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory31create_participant_with_profileE10DomainId_tRKNSt6stringEP25DomainParticipantListenerRK10StatusMask)
member function on the [DomainParticipantFactory](../domainParticipantFactory/domainParticipantFactory.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantfactory) singleton.

Mandatory arguments are:

* The `DomainId` that identifies the domain where the DomainParticipant will be created.
  Do not use `DomainId` higher than 200 (see [Creating a DomainParticipant](#dds-layer-domainparticipant-creation)).
* The name of the profile to be applied to the DomainParticipant.

Optional arguments are:

* A Listener derived from [DomainParticipantListener](../domainParticipantListener/domainParticipantListener.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantlistener), implementing the callbacks
  that will be triggered in response to events and state changes on the DomainParticipant.
  By default empty callbacks are used.
* A [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) that activates or deactivates triggering of individual callbacks on the
  [DomainParticipantListener](../domainParticipantListener/domainParticipantListener.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantlistener).
  By default all events are enabled.

[`create_participant_with_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory31create_participant_with_profileE10DomainId_tRKNSt6stringEP25DomainParticipantListenerRK10StatusMask) will return a null pointer if there was an error during
the operation, e.g if the provided QoS is not compatible or is not supported.
It is advisable to check that the returned value is a valid pointer.

#### NOTE
XML profiles must have been loaded previously. See [Loading profiles from an XML file](../domainParticipantFactory/domainParticipantFactory.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantfactory-load-profiles).

```c++
// First load the XML with the profiles
DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->load_XML_profiles_file("profiles.xml");

// Create a DomainParticipant using a profile and no Listener
DomainParticipant* participant_with_profile =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant_with_profile(0, "participant_profile");
if (nullptr == participant_with_profile)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DomainParticipant using a profile and a custom Listener.
// CustomDomainParticipantListener inherits from DomainParticipantListener.
CustomDomainParticipantListener custom_listener;
DomainParticipant* participant_with_profile_and_custom_listener =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant_with_profile(0, "participant_profile",
                &custom_listener);
if (nullptr == participant_with_profile_and_custom_listener)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-domainparticipant-creation-default-profile"></a>

<a id="default-profile-domainparticipant-creation"></a>

## Default profile DomainParticipant creation

If there is a profile already exported in the environment (please refer to [XML profiles](../../../xml_configuration/xml_configuration.md#xml-profiles) for related
information), creating a DomainParticipant with the
[`create_participant_with_default_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory39create_participant_with_default_profileEv) member function on the
[DomainParticipantFactory](../domainParticipantFactory/domainParticipantFactory.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantfactory) singleton would use that settings to configure the participant.
If the profile has not been exported, the DomainParticipant will be created with the default values per
[DomainParticipantQos](domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantqos), and `0` as `DomainId`.

Optional arguments are:

* A Listener derived from [DomainParticipantListener](../domainParticipantListener/domainParticipantListener.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantlistener), implementing the callbacks
  that will be triggered in response to events and state changes on the DomainParticipant.
  By default empty callbacks are used.
* A [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) that activates or deactivates triggering of individual callbacks on the
  [DomainParticipantListener](../domainParticipantListener/domainParticipantListener.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantlistener).
  By default all events are enabled.

[`create_participant_with_default_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory39create_participant_with_default_profileEv) will return a null pointer if there was an
error during the operation.
It is advisable to check that the returned value is a valid pointer.

#### NOTE
XML profiles must have been loaded previously. See [XML profiles](../../../xml_configuration/xml_configuration.md#xml-profiles).

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant using the environment profile and no Listener
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant_with_default_profile();
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DomainParticipant using the environment profile and a custom Listener.
// CustomDomainParticipantListener inherits from DomainParticipantListener.
CustomDomainParticipantListener custom_listener;
DomainParticipant* participant_with_custom_listener =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant_with_default_profile(
    &custom_listener, StatusMask::none());
if (nullptr == participant_with_custom_listener)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-domainparticipant-deletion"></a>

<a id="deleting-a-domainparticipant"></a>

## Deleting a DomainParticipant

A DomainParticipant shall be deleted with the [`delete_participant()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory18delete_participantEP17DomainParticipant) member function on the
[DomainParticipantFactory](../domainParticipantFactory/domainParticipantFactory.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantfactory) singleton.

#### IMPORTANT
A DomainParticipant can only be deleted if all Entities belonging to the participant
(Publisher, Subscriber or Topic) have already been deleted.
Otherwise, the function will issue an error and the DomainParticipant will not be deleted.
This can be performed either by using the [`delete_contained_entities()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant25delete_contained_entitiesEv) member function of the
[DomainParticipant](domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) or manually deleting each entity with the corresponding *delete_* method from the
DomainParticipant e.g [`delete_publisher()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant16delete_publisherEPK9Publisher), [`delete_subscriber()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant17delete_subscriberEPK10Subscriber),
[`delete_topic()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant12delete_topicEPK5Topic), etc.

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Use the DomainParticipant to communicate
// (...)

// Delete entities created by the DomainParticipant
if (participant->delete_contained_entities() != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // DomainParticipant failed to delete the entities it created.
    return;
}

// Delete the DomainParticipant
if (DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->delete_participant(participant) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="partitions"></a>

<a id="id1"></a>

# Partitions

Partitions introduce a logical entity isolation level concept inside the physical isolation induced by a
[Domain](../domain.md#dds-layer-domain).
They represent another level to separate [Publishers](../../publisher/publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher) and
[Subscribers](../../subscriber/subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber) beyond Domain and
[Topic](../../topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic).
For a Publisher to communicate with a Subscriber,
they have to belong at least to one common partition.
In this sense, partitions represent a light mechanism to provide data separation among endpoints:

* Unlike Domain and Topic, Partitions can be changed dynamically
  during the life cycle of the endpoint with little cost.
  Specifically, no new threads are launched, no new memory is allocated, and the change history is not affected.
  Beware that modifying the Partition membership of endpoints will trigger the announcement
  of the new QoS configuration, and as a result, new endpoint matching may occur,
  depending on the new Partition configuration.
  Changes on the memory allocation and running threads may occur due to the matching of remote endpoints.
* Unlike Domain and Topic, an endpoint can belong to several Partitions
  at the same time.
  For certain data to be shared over different Topics, there must be a different
  Publisher for each Topic,
  each of them sharing its own history of changes.
  On the other hand, a single Publisher can share the same data over different Partitions
  using a single topic data change, thus reducing network overload.

The Partition membership of an endpoint can be configured on the [PartitionQosPolicy](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/partitionqospolicy.md#api-pim-partitionqospolicy)
data member of the [PublisherQos](../../publisher/publisher/publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisherqos) or [SubscriberQos](../../subscriber/subscriber/subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriberqos) objects.
This member holds a list of Partition name strings.
In DDS, the default Partition name is the empty string `""`.
Therefore, an empty list (`{}`) is equivalent to a list containing only the empty string (`{""}`).
As a result, a Publisher and a Subscriber that specify no Partition can still communicate through the default
Partition, and explicitly configuring `""` has the same behavior.
If `""` is included together with additional names, the endpoint belongs to the default Partition and to those
additional Partitions.

#### WARNING
Partitions are linked to the endpoint and not to the changes.
This means that the endpoint history is oblivious to modifications in the Partitions.
For example, if a Publisher switches Partitions and afterwards needs to resend some older change again,
it will deliver it to the new Partition set, regardless of which Partitions were defined
when the change was created.
This means that a late joiner Subscriber may receive changes that were created when another
set of Partitions was active.

<a id="wildcards-in-partitions"></a>

## Wildcards in Partitions

Partition name entries can have wildcards following the naming conventions defined by the
POSIX `fnmatch` API ([1003.2-1992 section B.6](https://standards.ieee.org/standard/1003_2-1992.html)).
Entries with wildcards can match several names, allowing an endpoint to easily be included in several Partitions.
Two Partition names with wildcards will match if either of them matches the other one according to `fnmatch`.
That is, the matching is checked both ways.
For example, consider the following configuration:

- A Publisher with Partition `part*`
- A Subscriber with Partition `partition*`

Even though `partition*` does not match `part*`, these Publisher and Subscriber
will communicate between them because `part*` matches `partition*`.

Note that a Partition with name `*` will match any other partition,
including the default Partition `""`.

<a id="full-example"></a>

## Full example

Given a system with the following Partition configuration:

| Participant_1   | Pub_11                | {“Partition_1”, “Partition_2”}   |
|-----------------|-----------------------|----------------------------------|
| Pub_12          | {“\*”}                |                                  |
| Participant_2   | Pub_21                | {default} ≡ {“”} ≡ {}            |
| Pub_22          | {“Partition\*”}       |                                  |
| Participant_3   | Subs_31               | {“Partition_1”}                  |
| Subs_32         | {“Partition_2”}       |                                  |
| Subs_33         | {“Partition_3”}       |                                  |
| Subs_34         | {default} ≡ {“”} ≡ {} |                                  |

The endpoints will finally match the Partitions depicted on the following table.

|             |        |        |        |         | Participant_1   | Participant_2   | Participant_3   |
|-------------|--------|--------|--------|---------|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| Pub_11      | Pub_12 | Pub_21 | Pub_22 | Subs_31 | Subs_32         | Subs_33         | Subs_34         |
| Partition_1 | ✓      | ✓      | ✕      | ✓       | ✓               | ✕               | ✕               |
| Partition_2 | ✓      | ✓      | ✕      | ✓       | ✕               | ✓               | ✕               |
| Partition_3 | ✕      | ✓      | ✕      | ✓       | ✕               | ✕               | ✓               |
| {default}   | ✕      | ✓      | ✓      | ✕       | ✕               | ✕               | ✕               |

The following table provides the communication matrix for the given example:

|               |         | Participant_1   | Participant_2   |
|---------------|---------|-----------------|-----------------|
| Pub_11        | Pub_12  | Pub_21          | Pub_22          |
| Participant_3 | Subs_31 | ✓               | ✓               |
| Subs_32       | ✓       | ✓               | ✕               |
| Subs_33       | ✕       | ✓               | ✕               |
| Subs_34       | ✕       | ✓               | ✓               |

The following piece of code shows the set of parameters needed for the use case depicted in this example.

### C++

```c++
PublisherQos pub_11_qos;
pub_11_qos.partition().push_back("Partition_1");
pub_11_qos.partition().push_back("Partition_2");

PublisherQos pub_12_qos;
pub_12_qos.partition().push_back("*");

PublisherQos pub_21_qos;
//No partitions defined for pub_21

PublisherQos pub_22_qos;
pub_22_qos.partition().push_back("Partition*");

SubscriberQos subs_31_qos;
subs_31_qos.partition().push_back("Partition_1");

SubscriberQos subs_32_qos;
subs_32_qos.partition().push_back("Partition_2");

SubscriberQos subs_33_qos;
subs_33_qos.partition().push_back("Partition_3");

SubscriberQos subs_34_qos;
//No partitions defined for subs_34
```

### XML

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<profiles xmlns="http://www.eprosima.com">
    <data_writer profile_name="pub_11">
        <qos>
            <partition>
                <names>
                    <name>Partition_1</name>
                    <name>Partition_2</name>
                </names>
            </partition>
        </qos>
    </data_writer>

    <data_writer profile_name="pub_12">
        <qos>
            <partition>
                <names>
                    <name>*</name>
                </names>
            </partition>
        </qos>
    </data_writer>

    <data_writer profile_name="pub_22">
        <qos>
            <partition>
                <names>
                    <name>Partition*</name>
                </names>
            </partition>
        </qos>
    </data_writer>

    <data_reader profile_name="subs_31">
        <qos>
            <partition>
                <names>
                    <name>Partition_1</name>
                </names>
            </partition>
        </qos>
    </data_reader>

    <data_reader profile_name="subs_32">
        <qos>
            <partition>
                <names>
                    <name>Partition_2</name>
                </names>
            </partition>
        </qos>
    </data_reader>

    <data_reader profile_name="subs_33">
        <qos>
            <partition>
                <names>
                    <name>Partition_3</name>
                </names>
            </partition>
        </qos>
    </data_reader>
</profiles>
```

<a id="dds-layer-publisher"></a>

<a id="publisher"></a>

# Publisher

A publication is defined by the association of a [DataWriter](dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter)
to a [Publisher](publisher/publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisher).
To start publishing the values of a data instance, the application creates a new
DataWriter in a Publisher.
This DataWriter will be bound to the [Topic](../topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic)
that describes the data type that is being transmitted.
Remote subscriptions that match with this
Topic will be able to receive the data value updates from the DataWriter.

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-publisher"></a>

<a id="publisher"></a>

# Publisher

The [Publisher](#dds-layer-publisher-publisher) acts on behalf of one or several [DataWriter](../dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter) objects
that belong to it.
It serves as a container that allows grouping different DataWriter objects under
a common configuration given by the [PublisherQos](#dds-layer-publisher-publisherqos) of the Publisher.

DataWriter objects that belong to the same Publisher do not have any other
relation among each other beyond the PublisherQos of the Publisher and act independently
otherwise.
Specifically, a Publisher can host DataWriter objects for different [Topics](../../topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic)
and data types.

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-publisherqos"></a>

<a id="publisherqos"></a>

## PublisherQos

[`PublisherQos`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds12PublisherQosE) controls the behavior of the [`Publisher`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9PublisherE).
Internally it contains the following [`QosPolicy`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/qospolicy.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9QosPolicyE) objects:

| QosPolicy class                                                                           | Accessor/Mutator                                                                                                                             | Mutable   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| [PresentationQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#presentationqospolicy)   | [`presentation()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherqos.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds12PublisherQos12presentationEv)     | Yes       |
| [PartitionQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#partitionqospolicy)         | [`partition()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherqos.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds12PublisherQos9partitionEv)            | Yes       |
| [GroupDataQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#groupqospolicy)             | [`group_data()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherqos.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds12PublisherQos10group_dataEv)         | Yes       |
| [EntityFactoryQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#entityfactoryqospolicy) | [`entity_factory()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherqos.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds12PublisherQos14entity_factoryEv) | Yes       |

Refer to the detailed description of each [`QosPolicy`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/qospolicy.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9QosPolicyE) class for more information about their usage and
default values.

The QoS value of a previously created Publisher can be modified using the
[`Publisher::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher7set_qosERK12PublisherQos) member function.

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Publisher with default PublisherQos
Publisher* publisher =
        participant->create_publisher(PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == publisher)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
PublisherQos qos = publisher->get_qos();

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Assign the new Qos to the object
publisher->set_qos(qos);
```

<a id="dds-layer-defaultpublisherqos"></a>

<a id="default-publisherqos"></a>

### Default PublisherQos

The default [PublisherQos](#dds-layer-publisher-publisherqos) refers to the value returned by the
[`get_default_publisher_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant25get_default_publisher_qosEv) member function on the DomainParticipant instance.
The special value `PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT` can be used as QoS argument on
[`create_publisher()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant16create_publisherERK12PublisherQosR12ReturnCode_tP17PublisherListenerRK10StatusMask) or [`Publisher::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher7set_qosERK12PublisherQos) member functions to indicate that the current
default PublisherQos should be used.

When the system starts, the default PublisherQos is equivalent to the default constructed
value [`PublisherQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds12PublisherQos12PublisherQosEv).
The default PublisherQos can be modified at any time using the
[`set_default_publisher_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant25set_default_publisher_qosERK12PublisherQos) member function on the [DomainParticipant](../../domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) instance.
Modifying the default PublisherQos will not affect already existing
[Publisher](#dds-layer-publisher-publisher) instances.

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
PublisherQos qos_type1 = participant->get_default_publisher_qos();

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Set as the new default PublisherQos
if (participant->set_default_publisher_qos(qos_type1) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Publisher with the new default PublisherQos.
Publisher* publisher_with_qos_type1 =
        participant->create_publisher(PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == publisher_with_qos_type1)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
PublisherQos qos_type2;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Set as the new default PublisherQos
if (participant->set_default_publisher_qos(qos_type2) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Publisher with the new default PublisherQos.
Publisher* publisher_with_qos_type2 =
        participant->create_publisher(PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == publisher_with_qos_type2)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Resetting the default PublisherQos to the original default constructed values
if (participant->set_default_publisher_qos(PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT)
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// The previous instruction is equivalent to the following
if (participant->set_default_publisher_qos(PublisherQos())
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

[`set_default_publisher_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant25set_default_publisher_qosERK12PublisherQos) member function also accepts the special value
`PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT` as input argument.
This will reset the current default PublisherQos to default constructed
value [`PublisherQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds12PublisherQos12PublisherQosEv).

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a custom PublisherQos
PublisherQos custom_qos;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Create a publisher with a custom PublisherQos
Publisher* publisher = participant->create_publisher(custom_qos);
if (nullptr == publisher)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Set the QoS on the publisher to the default
if (publisher->set_qos(PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// The previous instruction is equivalent to the following:
if (publisher->set_qos(participant->get_default_publisher_qos())
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

#### NOTE
The value `PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT` has different meaning depending on where it is used:

* On [`create_publisher()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant16create_publisherERK12PublisherQosR12ReturnCode_tP17PublisherListenerRK10StatusMask) and [`Publisher::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher7set_qosERK12PublisherQos) it refers to the default
  [PublisherQos](#dds-layer-publisher-publisherqos).
  as returned by [`get_default_publisher_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant25get_default_publisher_qosEv).
* On [`set_default_publisher_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant25set_default_publisher_qosERK12PublisherQos) it refers to the default constructed
  [`PublisherQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds12PublisherQos12PublisherQosEv).

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/dds_layer/publisher/publisherListener/publisherListener.md -->

<!-- {{{ X-Types API -->
<!-- }}} -->

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-publisherlistener"></a>

<a id="publisherlistener"></a>

# PublisherListener

[`PublisherListener`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17PublisherListenerE) is an abstract class defining the callbacks that will be triggered
in response to state changes on the [Publisher](../publisher/publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisher).
By default, all these callbacks are empty and do nothing.
The user should implement a specialization of this class overriding the callbacks
that are needed on the application.
Callbacks that are not overridden will maintain their empty implementation.

[`PublisherListener`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17PublisherListenerE) inherits from [DataWriterListener](../dataWriterListener/dataWriterListener.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriterlistener).
Therefore, it has the ability to react to all events that are reported to the
[DataWriter](../dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter).
Since events are always notified to the most specific Entity Listener that can handle the event,
callbacks that [`PublisherListener`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17PublisherListenerE) inherits from DataWriterListener
will only be called if the triggering DataWriter has
no Listener attached,
or if the callback is disabled by the [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) on the DataWriter.

[`PublisherListener`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisherlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17PublisherListenerE) does not add any new callback.
Please, refer to the [DataWriterListener](../dataWriterListener/dataWriterListener.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriterlistener) for the list of inherited callbacks
and override examples.

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/dds_layer/publisher/publisher/createPublisher.md -->

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-creation"></a>

<a id="creating-a-publisher"></a>

# Creating a Publisher

A [Publisher](publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisher) always belongs to a [DomainParticipant](../../domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant).
Creation of a Publisher is done with the [`create_publisher()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant16create_publisherERK12PublisherQosR12ReturnCode_tP17PublisherListenerRK10StatusMask) member function on the
DomainParticipant instance, that acts as a factory for the Publisher.

Mandatory arguments are:

* The [PublisherQos](publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisherqos) describing the behavior of the Publisher.
  If the provided value is `PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT`,
  the value of the [Default PublisherQos](publisher.md#dds-layer-defaultpublisherqos) is used.

Optional arguments are:

* A Listener derived from [PublisherListener](../publisherListener/publisherListener.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisherlistener), implementing the callbacks
  that will be triggered in response to events and state changes on the Publisher.
  By default empty callbacks are used.
* A [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) that activates or deactivates triggering of individual callbacks on the
  PublisherListener.
  By default all events are enabled.

[`create_publisher()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant16create_publisherERK12PublisherQosR12ReturnCode_tP17PublisherListenerRK10StatusMask) will return a null pointer if there was an error during the operation, e.g.
if the provided QoS is not compatible or is not supported.
It is advisable to check that the returned value is a valid pointer.

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Publisher with default PublisherQos and no Listener
// The value PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT is used to denote the default QoS.
Publisher* publisher_with_default_qos =
        participant->create_publisher(PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == publisher_with_default_qos)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// A custom PublisherQos can be provided to the creation method
PublisherQos custom_qos;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

Publisher* publisher_with_custom_qos =
        participant->create_publisher(custom_qos);
if (nullptr == publisher_with_custom_qos)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Publisher with default QoS and a custom Listener.
// CustomPublisherListener inherits from PublisherListener.
// The value PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT is used to denote the default QoS.
CustomPublisherListener custom_listener;
Publisher* publisher_with_default_qos_and_custom_listener =
        participant->create_publisher(PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT, &custom_listener);
if (nullptr == publisher_with_default_qos_and_custom_listener)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-creation-profile"></a>

<a id="profile-based-creation-of-a-publisher"></a>

## Profile based creation of a Publisher

Instead of using a [PublisherQos](publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisherqos), the name of a profile
can be used to create a Publisher with the [`create_publisher_with_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant29create_publisher_with_profileERKNSt6stringER12ReturnCode_tP17PublisherListenerRK10StatusMask)
member function on the DomainParticipant instance.

Mandatory arguments are:

* A string with the name that identifies the Publisher.

Optional arguments are:

* A Listener derived from [PublisherListener](../publisherListener/publisherListener.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisherlistener), implementing the callbacks
  that will be triggered in response to events and state changes on the Publisher.
  By default empty callbacks are used.
* A [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) that activates or deactivates triggering of individual callbacks on the
  PublisherListener.
  By default all events are enabled.

[`create_publisher_with_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant29create_publisher_with_profileERKNSt6stringER12ReturnCode_tP17PublisherListenerRK10StatusMask) will return a null pointer if there was an error during the
operation, e.g. if the provided QoS is not compatible or is not supported.
It is advisable to check that the returned value is a valid pointer.

#### NOTE
XML profiles must have been loaded previously. See [Loading profiles from an XML file](../../domain/domainParticipantFactory/domainParticipantFactory.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantfactory-load-profiles).

```c++
// First load the XML with the profiles
DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->load_XML_profiles_file("profiles.xml");

// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Publisher using a profile and no Listener
Publisher* publisher_with_profile =
        participant->create_publisher_with_profile("publisher_profile");
if (nullptr == publisher_with_profile)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Publisher using a profile and a custom Listener.
// CustomPublisherListener inherits from PublisherListener.
CustomPublisherListener custom_listener;
Publisher* publisher_with_profile_and_custom_listener =
        participant->create_publisher_with_profile("publisher_profile", &custom_listener);
if (nullptr == publisher_with_profile_and_custom_listener)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-deletion"></a>

<a id="deleting-a-publisher"></a>

## Deleting a Publisher

A Publisher can be deleted with the [`delete_publisher()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant16delete_publisherEPK9Publisher) member function on the
DomainParticipant instance where the Publisher was created.

#### NOTE
A Publisher can only be deleted if all Entities belonging to the Publisher
(DataWriters) have already been deleted.
Otherwise, the function will issue an error and the Publisher will not be deleted.
This can be performed by using the [`delete_contained_entities()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher25delete_contained_entitiesEv) member function of the
[Publisher](publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisher).

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Publisher
Publisher* publisher =
        participant->create_publisher(PUBLISHER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == publisher)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Use the Publisher to communicate
// (...)

// Delete the entities the Publisher created.
if (publisher->delete_contained_entities() != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Publisher failed to delete the entities it created.
    return;
}

// Delete the Publisher
if (participant->delete_publisher(publisher) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md -->

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-datawriter"></a>

<a id="datawriter"></a>

# DataWriter

A [`DataWriter`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriterE) is attached to exactly one [Publisher](../publisher/publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisher) that acts as a factory for it.
Additionally, each DataWriter is bound to a single [Topic](../../topic/topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic-topic) since its creation.
This Topic must exist prior to the creation of the DataWriter,
and must be bound to the data type that the DataWriter wants to publish.

The effect of creating a new DataWriter in a Publisher for a specific
Topic is to initiate a new publication with the name and data type described
by the Topic.

Once the DataWriter is created, the application can inform of changes in the data value using the
[`write()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter5writeEPCKv) member function on the DataWriter.
These changes will be transmitted to all subscriptions matched with this publication.

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-datawriterqos"></a>

<a id="datawriterqos"></a>

## DataWriterQos

[`DataWriterQos`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataWriterQosE) controls the behavior of the DataWriter.
Internally it contains the following [`QosPolicy`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/qospolicy.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9QosPolicyE) objects:

| [LivelinessQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#livelinessqospolicy)                   | [`liveliness()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataWriterQos10livelinessEv)                         | No        |

| [RTPSReliableWriterQos](../../core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#rtpsreliablewriterqos)                | [`reliable_writer_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataWriterQos19reliable_writer_qosEv)       | Yes (\*)  |

| [WriterResourceLimitsQos](../../core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#writerresourcelimitsqos)            | [`writer_resource_limits()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataWriterQos22writer_resource_limitsEv) | No        |
| [DataSharingQosPolicy](../../core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#datasharingqospolicy)                  | [`data_sharing()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataWriterQos12data_sharingEv)                     | No        |

The following non-consolidated property-assigned QoS apply to DataWriters:

| Property name     | Non-consolidated QoS                                                                                            |
|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| fastdds.push_mode | [DataWriter operating mode QoS Policy](../../../property_policies/non_consolidated_qos.md#push-mode-qos-policy) |
| partitions        | [Endpoint Partitions](../../../property_policies/non_consolidated_qos.md#property-policies-partitions)          |

Refer to the detailed description of each [`QosPolicy`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/qospolicy.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9QosPolicyE) class for more information about their usage and
default values.

#### NOTE
Reliability kind (whether the publication is reliable or best effort) is not mutable.
However, the `max_blocking_time` data member of [ReliabilityQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#reliabilityqospolicy) can be modified any time.

#### NOTE
Not all data members of RTPSReliableWriterQos are mutable, please refer to [RTPSReliableWriterQos](../../core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#rtpsreliablewriterqos)
for more information.

The QoS value of a previously created DataWriter can be modified using the
[`DataWriter::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter7set_qosERK13DataWriterQos) member function.

```c++
// Create a DataWriter with default DataWriterQos
DataWriter* data_writer =
        publisher->create_datawriter(topic, DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_writer)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
DataWriterQos qos = data_writer->get_qos();

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Assign the new Qos to the object
data_writer->set_qos(qos);
```

<a id="dds-layer-defaultdatawriterqos"></a>

<a id="default-datawriterqos"></a>

### Default DataWriterQos

The default [DataWriterQos](#dds-layer-publisher-datawriterqos) refers to the value returned by the
[`get_default_datawriter_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher26get_default_datawriter_qosEv) member function on the Publisher instance.
The special value `DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT` can be used as QoS argument on [`create_datawriter()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher17create_datawriterEP5TopicRK13DataWriterQosP18DataWriterListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE)
or [`DataWriter::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter7set_qosERK13DataWriterQos) member functions to indicate that the current default
DataWriterQos should be used.

When the system starts, the default DataWriterQos is equivalent to the default constructed
value [`DataWriterQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataWriterQos13DataWriterQosEv).
The default DataWriterQos can be modified at any time using the
[`set_default_datawriter_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher26set_default_datawriter_qosERK13DataWriterQos) member function on the Publisher instance.
Modifying the default DataWriterQos will not affect already existing
DataWriter instances.

```c++
// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
DataWriterQos qos_type1 = publisher->get_default_datawriter_qos();

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Set as the new default DataWriterQos
if (publisher->set_default_datawriter_qos(qos_type1) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DataWriter with the new default DataWriterQos.
DataWriter* data_writer_with_qos_type1 =
        publisher->create_datawriter(topic, DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_writer_with_qos_type1)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
DataWriterQos qos_type2;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Set as the new default DataWriterQos
if (publisher->set_default_datawriter_qos(qos_type2) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DataWriter with the new default DataWriterQos.
DataWriter* data_writer_with_qos_type2 =
        publisher->create_datawriter(topic, DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_writer_with_qos_type2)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Resetting the default DataWriterQos to the original default constructed values
if (publisher->set_default_datawriter_qos(DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT)
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// The previous instruction is equivalent to the following
if (publisher->set_default_datawriter_qos(DataWriterQos())
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

[`set_default_datawriter_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher26set_default_datawriter_qosERK13DataWriterQos) member function also accepts the special value
`DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT` as input argument.
This will reset the current default DataWriterQos to default constructed
value [`DataWriterQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataWriterQos13DataWriterQosEv).

```c++
// Create a custom DataWriterQos
DataWriterQos custom_qos;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Create a DataWriter with a custom DataWriterQos
DataWriter* data_writer = publisher->create_datawriter(topic, custom_qos);
if (nullptr == data_writer)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Set the QoS on the DataWriter to the default
if (data_writer->set_qos(DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// The previous instruction is equivalent to the following:
if (data_writer->set_qos(publisher->get_default_datawriter_qos())
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

#### NOTE
The value `DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT` has different meaning depending on where it is used:

* On [`create_datawriter()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher17create_datawriterEP5TopicRK13DataWriterQosP18DataWriterListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE) and [`DataWriter::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter7set_qosERK13DataWriterQos) it refers to the default DataWriterQos
  as returned by [`get_default_datawriter_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher26get_default_datawriter_qosEv).
* On [`set_default_datawriter_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher26set_default_datawriter_qosERK13DataWriterQos) it refers to the default constructed
  [`DataWriterQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataWriterQos13DataWriterQosEv).

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-datawriter-type-support-context"></a>

<a id="type-support-context"></a>

## Type support context

A DataWriter can be configured with a [type support context](../../topic/typeSupport/typeSupport.md#dds-layer-topic-type-support-context)
that is forwarded to the [`TopicDataType`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/topicdatatype.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13TopicDataTypeE) callbacks on every write operation.
This allows the type implementation to rely on per-writer information (e.g., bounded sizes)

The context must be set **before** enabling the DataWriter using
[`DataWriter::set_type_support_context()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter24set_type_support_contextERKNSt10shared_ptrIN13TopicDataType7ContextEEE).
Calling this method on an already-enabled DataWriter returns `RETCODE_ILLEGAL_OPERATION`.

```c++
// User-defined context struct carrying per-writer configuration.
struct MyContext : public TopicDataType::Context
{
    uint32_t string_max_length = 0;
    uint32_t sequence_max_length = 0;
};

// Create a DataWriter (initially disabled, e.g. via participant QoS).
DataWriterQos writer_qos = DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT;
DataWriter* writer = publisher->create_datawriter(topic, writer_qos);

// Create a context carrying per-writer configuration.
auto context = std::make_shared<MyContext>();
context->string_max_length = 512;
context->sequence_max_length = 1024;

// Set it before enabling the DataWriter.
ReturnCode_t ret = writer->set_type_support_context(context);
assert(ret == RETCODE_OK);

// Then enable the writer (e.g., by enabling its DomainParticipant).
```

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-datawriterlistener"></a>

<a id="datawriterlistener"></a>

# DataWriterListener

[`DataWriterListener`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataWriterListenerE) is an abstract class defining the callbacks that will be triggered
in response to state changes on the [DataWriter](../dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter).
By default, all these callbacks are empty and do nothing.
The user should implement a specialization of this class overriding the callbacks
that are needed on the application.
Callbacks that are not overridden will maintain their empty implementation.

[`DataWriterListener`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataWriterListenerE) defines the following callbacks:

* [`on_publication_matched()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataWriterListener22on_publication_matchedEP10DataWriterRK24PublicationMatchedStatus): The DataWriter has found a
  [DataReader](../../subscriber/dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader) that matches the [Topic](../../topic/topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic-topic) and has
  a common partition and a compatible QoS, or has ceased to be matched with a
  DataReader that was previously considered to be matched.
* [`on_offered_deadline_missed()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataWriterListener26on_offered_deadline_missedEP10DataWriterRK27OfferedDeadlineMissedStatus): The DataWriter failed to provide
  data within the deadline period configured on its [DataWriterQos](../dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriterqos).
  It will be called for each deadline period and data instance for which the
  DataWriter failed to provide data.
* [`on_offered_incompatible_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataWriterListener27on_offered_incompatible_qosEP10DataWriterRK28OfferedIncompatibleQosStatus): The DataWriter has found a
  DataReader that matches the Topic and has
  a common partition, but with a requested QoS that is incompatible with the one defined on the
  DataWriter.
* [`on_liveliness_lost()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataWriterListener18on_liveliness_lostEP10DataWriterRK20LivelinessLostStatus): The DataWriter did not respect the
  liveliness configuration on its DataWriterQos, and therefore,
  DataReader entities will consider the DataWriter
  as no longer *active*.
* [`on_unacknowledged_sample_removed()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataWriterListener32on_unacknowledged_sample_removedEP10DataWriterRK16InstanceHandle_t): The Datawriter has removed a sample that has not been
  acknowledged by every matched DataReader.

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-datawriterlistener-on-unack-sample-removed"></a>

<a id="on-unacknowledged-sample-removed-callback"></a>

## on_unacknowledged_sample_removed callback

[`on_unacknowledged_sample_removed()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataWriterListener32on_unacknowledged_sample_removedEP10DataWriterRK16InstanceHandle_t) non-standard callback notifies the user when a sample has
been removed without being sent/received by the matched DataReaders.
This could happen in constrained networks or if the publication throughput is too demanding.
This callback can be used to detect these situations so the publishing application can apply some solution to ease this
issue like reducing the publication rate.

The criteria to consider that a sample has been removed without being acknowledged depends on the
[ReliabilityQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#reliabilityqospolicy):

* [`BEST_EFFORT_RELIABILITY_QOS`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/reliabilityqospolicykind.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24ReliabilityQosPolicyKind27BEST_EFFORT_RELIABILITY_QOSE) DataWriters will notify that a sample has been removed while unacknowledged if the
  sample has not been sent through the transport.
* [`RELIABLE_RELIABILITY_QOS`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/reliabilityqospolicykind.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24ReliabilityQosPolicyKind24RELIABLE_RELIABILITY_QOSE) DataWriters consider samples to have been removed unacknowledged if not every matched
  DataReader has confirmed its reception by sending the corresponding meta-traffic `ACK` message.
  Consequently, a sample that is notified as removed unacknowledged might be received by one or more DataReaders, but
  not by every matched one, or at least, the `ACK` message has not been received at the moment of sample removal.
  A race condition is inevitable in this case, because when the sample is removed, the `ACK` from some matched
  DataReader is missing, but that means that it might have been lost in the transmission or that the message is still
  coming through and it will be received after the sample removal.
  Thus, this criteria may include false positives, but from the user’s point of view, it is more meaningful to know when
  the sample has not been acknowledged by every matched DataReader even if some samples are erroneously notified.

A specific case must be considered for reliable DataWriters with [DisablePositiveACKsQosPolicy](../../core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#disablepositiveacksqospolicy) enabled.
This policy disables the sending of positive `ACK` messages, unless the sample has been lost in which case the matched
DataReader notifies the loss with a negative `NACK` message.
If no `NACK` has been received in the time defined in the QoS policy, the sample is considered to be received.
Again, this is prone to race conditions because the `NACK` message might be on its way or have been lost in the
network.
For this specific case, where `ACK` messages are not going to be received, the reliable DataWriter uses the same
criteria as the best effort DataWriter.

```c++
class CustomDataWriterListener : public DataWriterListener
{

public:

    CustomDataWriterListener()
        : DataWriterListener()
    {
    }

    virtual ~CustomDataWriterListener()
    {
    }

    void on_publication_matched(
            DataWriter* writer,
            const PublicationMatchedStatus& info) override
    {
        static_cast<void>(writer);
        if (info.current_count_change == 1)
        {
            std::cout << "Matched a remote Subscriber for one of our Topics" << std::endl;
        }
        else if (info.current_count_change == -1)
        {
            std::cout << "Unmatched a remote Subscriber" << std::endl;
        }
    }

    void on_offered_deadline_missed(
            DataWriter* writer,
            const OfferedDeadlineMissedStatus& status) override
    {
        static_cast<void>(writer);
        static_cast<void>(status);
        std::cout << "Some data could not be delivered on time" << std::endl;
    }

    void on_offered_incompatible_qos(
            DataWriter* writer,
            const OfferedIncompatibleQosStatus& status) override
    {
        std::cout << "Found a remote Topic with incompatible QoS (QoS ID: " << status.last_policy_id
                  << ")" << std::endl;
    }

    void on_liveliness_lost(
            DataWriter* writer,
            const LivelinessLostStatus& status) override
    {
        static_cast<void>(writer);
        static_cast<void>(status);
        std::cout << "Liveliness lost. Matched Subscribers will consider us offline" << std::endl;
    }

    void on_unacknowledged_sample_removed(
            DataWriter* writer,
            const InstanceHandle_t& instance) override
    {
        static_cast<void>(writer);
        static_cast<void>(instance);
        std::cout << "Sample removed unacknowledged" << std::endl;
    }

};
```

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/createDataWriter.md -->
