<a id="dds-layer-publisher-datawriter-creation"></a>

<a id="creating-a-datawriter"></a>

# Creating a DataWriter

A [DataWriter](dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter) always belongs to a [Publisher](../publisher/publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisher).
Creation of a DataWriter is done with the [`create_datawriter()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher17create_datawriterEP5TopicRK13DataWriterQosP18DataWriterListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE) member function on the
Publisher instance, that acts as a factory for the DataWriter.

Mandatory arguments are:

* A [Topic](../../topic/topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic-topic) bound to the data type that will be transmitted.
* The [DataWriterQos](dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriterqos) describing the behavior of the DataWriter.
  If the provided value is `DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT`,
  the value of the [Default DataWriterQos](dataWriter.md#dds-layer-defaultdatawriterqos) is used.
  If the provided value is `DATAWRITER_QOS_USE_TOPIC_QOS`,
  the values of the default QoS and the provided TopicQoS are used, whereby any policy
  that is set on the TopicQoS overrides the corresponding policy on the default QoS.

Optional arguments are:

* A Listener derived from [DataWriterListener](../dataWriterListener/dataWriterListener.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriterlistener), implementing the callbacks
  that will be triggered in response to events and state changes on the DataWriter.
  By default empty callbacks are used.
* A [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) that activates or deactivates triggering of individual callbacks on the
  DataWriterListener.
  By default all events are enabled.

[`create_datawriter()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher17create_datawriterEP5TopicRK13DataWriterQosP18DataWriterListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE) will return a null pointer if there was an error during the operation, e.g.
if the provided QoS is not compatible or is not supported.
It is advisable to check that the returned value is a valid pointer.

```c++
// Create a DataWriter with default DataWriterQos and no Listener
// The value DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT is used to denote the default QoS.
DataWriter* data_writer_with_default_qos =
        publisher->create_datawriter(topic, DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_writer_with_default_qos)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// A custom DataWriterQos can be provided to the creation method
DataWriterQos custom_qos;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

DataWriter* data_writer_with_custom_qos =
        publisher->create_datawriter(topic, custom_qos);
if (nullptr == data_writer_with_custom_qos)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DataWriter with default QoS and a custom Listener.
// CustomDataWriterListener inherits from DataWriterListener.
// The value DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT is used to denote the default QoS.
CustomDataWriterListener custom_listener;
DataWriter* data_writer_with_default_qos_and_custom_listener =
        publisher->create_datawriter(topic, DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT, &custom_listener);
if (nullptr == data_writer_with_default_qos_and_custom_listener)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DataWriter with default QoS and a custom TopicQos.
// The value DATAWRITER_QOS_USE_TOPIC_QOS is used to denote the default QoS
// and to override the TopicQos.
Topic* topic =
        participant->create_topic("", "", TOPIC_QOS_DEFAULT);
DataWriter* data_writer_with_default_qos_and_custom_topic_qos =
        publisher->create_datawriter(topic, DATAWRITER_QOS_USE_TOPIC_QOS);
if (nullptr == data_writer_with_default_qos_and_custom_topic_qos)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-datawriter-creation-profile"></a>

<a id="profile-based-creation-of-a-datawriter"></a>

## Profile based creation of a DataWriter

Instead of using a DataWriterQos, the name of a profile
can be used to create a DataWriter with the [`create_datawriter_with_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher30create_datawriter_with_profileEP5TopicRKNSt6stringEP18DataWriterListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE)
member function on the Publisher instance.

Mandatory arguments are:

* A Topic bound to the data type that will be transmitted.
* A string with the name that identifies the DataWriter.

Optional arguments are:

* A Listener derived from DataWriterListener, implementing the callbacks
  that will be triggered in response to events and state changes on the DataWriter.
  By default empty callbacks are used.
* A [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) that activates or deactivates triggering of individual callbacks on the
  DataWriterListener.
  By default all events are enabled.

[`create_datawriter_with_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher30create_datawriter_with_profileEP5TopicRKNSt6stringEP18DataWriterListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE) will return a null pointer if there was an error during the
operation, e.g. if the provided QoS is not compatible or is not supported.
It is advisable to check that the returned value is a valid pointer.

#### NOTE
XML profiles must have been loaded previously. See [Loading profiles from an XML file](../../domain/domainParticipantFactory/domainParticipantFactory.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantfactory-load-profiles).

```c++
// First load the XML with the profiles
DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->load_XML_profiles_file("profiles.xml");

// Create a DataWriter using a profile and no Listener
DataWriter* data_writer_with_profile =
        publisher->create_datawriter_with_profile(topic, "data_writer_profile");
if (nullptr == data_writer_with_profile)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DataWriter using a profile and a custom Listener.
// CustomDataWriterListener inherits from DataWriterListener.
CustomDataWriterListener custom_listener;
DataWriter* data_writer_with_profile_and_custom_listener =
        publisher->create_datawriter_with_profile(topic, "data_writer_profile", &custom_listener);
if (nullptr == data_writer_with_profile_and_custom_listener)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-datawriter-with-payload-pool-creation"></a>

<a id="creating-a-datawriter-with-a-custom-payloadpool"></a>

## Creating a DataWriter with a custom PayloadPool

A custom [PayloadPool](../../../rtps_layer/rtps_layer.md#rtps-layer-custom-payload-pool) can be passed as an argument during the creation of a
[DataWriter](dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter).
This allows for customizing the management of the information exchanged between DataWriters and DataReaders.
The same configuration can be set in the
[opposite endpoint](../../subscriber/dataReader/createDataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader-with-payload-pool-creation).

```c++
// A DataWriterQos must be provided to the creation method
DataWriterQos qos;

// Create PayloadPool
std::shared_ptr<eprosima::fastdds::rtps::IPayloadPool> payload_pool =
        std::dynamic_pointer_cast<eprosima::fastdds::rtps::IPayloadPool>(std::make_shared<CustomPayloadPool>());

DataWriter* data_writer = publisher->create_datawriter(topic, qos, nullptr, StatusMask::all(), payload_pool);
if (nullptr == data_writer)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

This configuration can be performed also in the [RTPS layer](../../../rtps_layer/rtps_layer.md#rtps-layer-custom-payload-pool).
The [customization example](../../../rtps_layer/rtps_layer.md#rtps-layer-payload-pool-example) applies both layers.

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-datawriter-deletion"></a>

<a id="deleting-a-datawriter"></a>

## Deleting a DataWriter

A DataWriter can be deleted with the [`delete_datawriter()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/publisher_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9Publisher17delete_datawriterEPK10DataWriter) member function on the
[Publisher](../publisher/publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisher) instance where the DataWriter was created.

```c++
// Create a DataWriter
DataWriter* data_writer =
        publisher->create_datawriter(topic, DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_writer)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Use the DataWriter to communicate
// (...)

// Delete the DataWriter
if (publisher->delete_datawriter(data_writer) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/publishingData.md -->

<!-- {{{ X-Types API -->
<!-- }}} -->

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-write"></a>

<a id="publishing-data"></a>

# Publishing data

The user informs of a change in the value of a data instance with the [`write()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter5writeEPCKv) member function on the
[DataWriter](dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter). This change will then be communicated to every
[DataReader](../../subscriber/dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader) matched with the DataWriter.
As a side effect, this operation asserts liveliness on the DataWriter itself,
the [Publisher](../publisher/publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher-publisher) and the [DomainParticipant](../../domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant).

The function takes two arguments:

* A pointer to the data instance with the new values.
* The handler to the instance.

An empty (i.e., default constructed [`InstanceHandle_t`](../../../api_reference/rtps/common/InstanceHandle/InstanceHandle_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps16InstanceHandle_tE)) instance handler can be used for the argument handle.
This indicates that the identity of the instance should be automatically deduced from the key of the
instance data.
Alternatively, the member function [`write()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter5writeEPCKv) is overloaded to take only the pointer to the data instance,
which will always deduced the identity from the key of the instance data.

If the handle is not empty, then it must correspond to the value obtained with the `getKey()` of the
[`TypeSupport`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/typesupport.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds11TypeSupportE) instance.
Otherwise the write function will fail with `RETCODE_PRECONDITION_NOT_MET`.

```c++
// Register the data type in the DomainParticipant.
TypeSupport custom_type_support(new CustomDataType());
custom_type_support.register_type(participant, custom_type_support.get_type_name());

// Create a Topic with the registered type.
Topic* custom_topic =
        participant->create_topic("topic_name", custom_type_support.get_type_name(), TOPIC_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == custom_topic)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DataWriter
DataWriter* data_writer =
        publisher->create_datawriter(custom_topic, DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_writer)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Get a data instance
void* data = custom_type_support->create_data();

// Fill the data values
// (...)

// Publish the new value, deduce the instance handle
if (data_writer->write(data, eprosima::fastdds::rtps::InstanceHandle_t()) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// The data instance can be reused to publish new values,
// but delete it at the end to avoid leaks
custom_type_support->delete_data(data);
```

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-write-blocking"></a>

<a id="blocking-of-the-write-operation"></a>

## Blocking of the write operation

If the reliability kind is set to `RELIABLE` on the [DataWriterQos](dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriterqos),
the [`write()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter5writeEPCKv) operation may block.
Specifically, if the limits specified in the configured resource limits have been reached, the
[`write()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter5writeEPCKv) operation will block waiting for space to become available.
Under these circumstances, the reliability `max_blocking_time` configures the maximum time
the write operation may block waiting.
If `max_blocking_time` elapses before the DataWriter is able to store
the modification without exceeding the limits, the write operation will fail and return `TIMEOUT`.

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-write-loans"></a>

<a id="borrowing-a-data-buffer"></a>

## Borrowing a data buffer

When the user calls [`write()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter5writeEPCKv) with a new sample value,
the data is copied from the given sample to the DataWriter’s memory.
For large data types this copy can consume significant time and memory resources.
Instead, the DataWriter can loan a sample from its memory to the user,
and the user can fill this sample with the required values.
When [`write()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter5writeEPCKv) is called with such a loaned sample,
the DataWriter does not copy its contents, as it already owns the buffer.

To use loaned data samples in publications, perform the following steps:

1. Get a reference to a loaned sample using [`loan_sample()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter11loan_sampleERPv22LoanInitializationKind).
2. Use the reference to build the data sample.
3. Write the sample using [`write()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter5writeEPCKv).

Once [`write()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter5writeEPCKv) has been called with a loaned sample,
the loan is considered returned, and it is not safe to make any
changes on the contents of the sample.

If function [`loan_sample()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter11loan_sampleERPv22LoanInitializationKind) is called but the sample is never written,
the loan must be returned to the DataWriter using [`discard_loan()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter12discard_loanERPv).
Otherwise the DataWriter may run out of samples.

```c++
    // Borrow a data instance
    void* data = nullptr;
    if (RETCODE_OK == data_writer->loan_sample(data))
    {
        bool error = false;

        // Fill the data values
        // (...)

        if (error)
        {
            // Return the loan without publishing
            data_writer->discard_loan(data);
            return;
        }

        // Publish the new value
        if (data_writer->write(data, eprosima::fastdds::rtps::InstanceHandle_t()) != RETCODE_OK)
        {
            // Error
            return;
        }
    }
```

<a id="dds-layer-publisher-prefiltering"></a>

<a id="prefiltering-out-datareaders"></a>

## Prefiltering out DataReaders

The user can use an overload of the [`write()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter5writeEPCKv) method that allows providing a [`WriteParams`](../../../api_reference/rtps/common/WriteParams/WriteParams.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps11WriteParamsE) structure.
One of the members of this latter structure is the [`UserWriteData`](../../../api_reference/rtps/common/WriteParams/WriteParams.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps11WriteParams13UserWriteDataE) in which the user
can store extra information to be used by the prefiltering mechanism and it can be set using the
[`user_write_data()`](../../../api_reference/rtps/common/WriteParams/WriteParams.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds4rtps11WriteParams15user_write_dataEv).

By implementing the [`IContentFilter`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/icontentfilter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds14IContentFilterE) and passing it to the DataWriter with [`DataWriter::set_sample_prefilter()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriter20set_sample_prefilterENSt10shared_ptrI14IContentFilterEE),
user can prevent the DataWriter from sending samples to the matched DataReaders based on both
the content of the sample ([`SerializedPayload_t`](../../../api_reference/rtps/common/SerializedPayload/SerializedPayload_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps19SerializedPayload_tE)) and/or the `user_write_data` within
`FilteredSampleInfo`.
If the return value of [`evaluate()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/icontentfilter.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds14IContentFilter8evaluateERK17SerializedPayloadRK16FilterSampleInfoRK6GUID_t) is `false`, the sample will not be sent to the DataReader
identified by its [`Guid_t`](../../../api_reference/rtps/common/Guid/GUID_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps6GUID_tE) in the method’s input argument.
It is strongly recommended that the [`evaluate()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/icontentfilter.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds14IContentFilter8evaluateERK17SerializedPayloadRK16FilterSampleInfoRK6GUID_t) implementation neither performs any blocking
operation nor uses the DataWriter, as this may lead to deadlocks or undesired behavior.

#### WARNING
Prefiltering is currently incompatible with [DataSharingQosPolicy](../../core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#datasharingqospolicy).
Hence, ensure that the [`kind()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/datasharingqospolicy.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds20DataSharingQosPolicy4kindEv) is set to `OFF` or
if `AUTO` is used, [constraints](../../../transport/datasharing.md#datasharing-delivery-constraints) are not met.

Next is an example of how to use the prefiltering mechanism:

```c++
struct CustomUserWriteData : public eprosima::fastdds::rtps::WriteParams::UserWriteData
{
    CustomUserWriteData(
            const eprosima::fastdds::rtps::GuidPrefix_t& prefix)
        : filtered_out_prefix(prefix)
    {
    }

    eprosima::fastdds::rtps::GuidPrefix_t filtered_out_prefix;
};

struct CustomPreFilter : public eprosima::fastdds::dds::IContentFilter
{
    // Custom evaluation
    bool evaluate(
            const SerializedPayload& payload,
            const FilterSampleInfo& filter_sample_info,
            const eprosima::fastdds::rtps::GUID_t& reader_guid) const override
    {
        static_cast<void>(payload);
        static_cast<void>(filter_sample_info);

        bool sample_should_be_sent = true;

        auto custom_write_data =
                std::static_pointer_cast<CustomUserWriteData>(
            filter_sample_info.user_write_data);

        // If the reader is the one to filter out, do not send the sample
        if (custom_write_data->filtered_out_prefix == reader_guid.guidPrefix)
        {
            sample_should_be_sent = false;
        }
        return sample_should_be_sent;
    }

};

// Create a DataWriter
DataWriter* data_writer =
        publisher->create_datawriter(topic, DATAWRITER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_writer)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Set a prefilter on the filtered reader
eprosima::fastdds::dds::ReturnCode_t ret = data_writer->set_sample_prefilter(
    std::make_shared<CustomPreFilter>());

if (ret != eprosima::fastdds::dds::RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a custom user write data
eprosima::fastdds::rtps::GuidPrefix_t filtered_out_prefix;
std::istringstream("44.53.00.5f.45.60.52.4f.53.49.7c.41") >> filtered_out_prefix;

std::shared_ptr<CustomUserWriteData> custom_write_data =
        std::make_shared<CustomUserWriteData>(filtered_out_prefix);

// Set the custom user write data
eprosima::fastdds::rtps::WriteParams write_params;
write_params.user_write_data(custom_write_data);

HelloWorld sample;     //Auto-generated container class for topic data from Fast DDS-Gen
sample.msg("Hello there!");     // Add contents to the message

// Write a sample with the custom user write data
data_writer->write(&sample, write_params);

```

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/dds_layer/subscriber/subscriber.md -->

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber"></a>

<a id="subscriber"></a>

# Subscriber

A subscription is defined by the association of a [DataReader](dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader)
to a [Subscriber](subscriber/subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriber).
To start receiving updates of a publication, the application creates a new
DataReader in a Subscriber.
This DataReader will be bound to the [Topic](../topic/topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic-topic)
that describes the data type that is going to be received.
The DataReader will then start receiving data value updates from
remote publications that match this Topic.

When the Subscriber receives data, it informs the application that new data is available.
Then, the application can use the DataReader to get the received data.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-subscriber"></a>

<a id="subscriber"></a>

# Subscriber

The [`Subscriber`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SubscriberE) acts on behalf of one or several [DataReader](../dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader) objects
that belong to it.
It serves as a container that allows grouping different DataReader objects under
a common configuration given by the [SubscriberQos](#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriberqos) of the Subscriber.

DataReader objects that belong to the same Subscriber
do not have any other relation among each other beyond the [`SubscriberQos`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriberqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13SubscriberQosE) of the Subscriber
and act independently otherwise.
Specifically, a Subscriber can host DataReader objects
for different topics and data types.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-subscriberqos"></a>

<a id="subscriberqos"></a>

## SubscriberQos

[`SubscriberQos`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriberqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13SubscriberQosE) controls the behavior of the [Subscriber](#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriber).
Internally it contains the following [`QosPolicy`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/qospolicy.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9QosPolicyE) objects:

| QosPolicy class                                                                           | Accessor/Mutator                                                                                                                                | Mutable   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------|
| [PresentationQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#presentationqospolicy)   | [`presentation()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriberqos.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds13SubscriberQos12presentationEv)     | Yes       |
| [PartitionQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#partitionqospolicy)         | [`partition()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriberqos.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds13SubscriberQos9partitionEv)            | Yes       |
| [GroupDataQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#groupqospolicy)             | [`group_data()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriberqos.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds13SubscriberQos10group_dataEv)         | Yes       |
| [EntityFactoryQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#entityfactoryqospolicy) | [`entity_factory()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriberqos.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds13SubscriberQos14entity_factoryEv) | Yes       |

Refer to the detailed description of each [`QosPolicy`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/qospolicy.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds9QosPolicyE) class for more information about their usage and
default values.

The QoS value of a previously created Subscriber can be modified using the
[`Subscriber::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber7set_qosERK13SubscriberQos) member function.

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Subscriber with default SubscriberQos
Subscriber* subscriber =
        participant->create_subscriber(SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == subscriber)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
SubscriberQos qos = subscriber->get_qos();

// Modify QoS attributes
qos.entity_factory().autoenable_created_entities = false;

// Assign the new Qos to the object
subscriber->set_qos(qos);
```

<a id="dds-layer-defaultsubscriberqos"></a>

<a id="default-subscriberqos"></a>

### Default SubscriberQos

The default [SubscriberQos](#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriberqos) refers to the value returned by the
[`get_default_subscriber_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant26get_default_subscriber_qosEv) member function
on the [DomainParticipant](../../domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) instance.
The special value `SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT` can be used as QoS argument on
[`create_subscriber()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant17create_subscriberERK13SubscriberQosR12ReturnCode_tP18SubscriberListenerRK10StatusMask) or [`Subscriber::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber7set_qosERK13SubscriberQos)
member functions to indicate that the current default SubscriberQos
should be used.

When the system starts, the default SubscriberQos is equivalent to the default constructed
value [`SubscriberQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriberqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13SubscriberQos13SubscriberQosEv).
The default SubscriberQos can be modified at any time using the
[`set_default_subscriber_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant26set_default_subscriber_qosERK13SubscriberQos) member function on the
DomainParticipant instance.
Modifying the default SubscriberQos will not affect already existing
Subscriber instances.

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
SubscriberQos qos_type1 = participant->get_default_subscriber_qos();

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Set as the new default SubscriberQos
if (participant->set_default_subscriber_qos(qos_type1) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Subscriber with the new default SubscriberQos.
Subscriber* subscriber_with_qos_type1 =
        participant->create_subscriber(SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == subscriber_with_qos_type1)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
SubscriberQos qos_type2;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Set as the new default SubscriberQos
if (participant->set_default_subscriber_qos(qos_type2) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Subscriber with the new default SubscriberQos.
Subscriber* subscriber_with_qos_type2 =
        participant->create_subscriber(SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == subscriber_with_qos_type2)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Resetting the default SubscriberQos to the original default constructed values
if (participant->set_default_subscriber_qos(SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT)
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// The previous instruction is equivalent to the following
if (participant->set_default_subscriber_qos(SubscriberQos())
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

[`set_default_subscriber_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant26set_default_subscriber_qosERK13SubscriberQos) member function also accepts
the special value `SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT` as input argument.
This will reset the current default SubscriberQos to default constructed
value [`SubscriberQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriberqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13SubscriberQos13SubscriberQosEv).

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a custom SubscriberQos
SubscriberQos custom_qos;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Create a subscriber with a custom SubscriberQos
Subscriber* subscriber = participant->create_subscriber(custom_qos);
if (nullptr == subscriber)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Set the QoS on the subscriber to the default
if (subscriber->set_qos(SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// The previous instruction is equivalent to the following:
if (subscriber->set_qos(participant->get_default_subscriber_qos())
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

#### NOTE
The value `SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT` has different meaning depending on where it is used:

* On [`create_subscriber()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant17create_subscriberERK13SubscriberQosR12ReturnCode_tP18SubscriberListenerRK10StatusMask) and [`Subscriber::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber7set_qosERK13SubscriberQos) it refers to the default
  SubscriberQos as returned by [`get_default_subscriber_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant26get_default_subscriber_qosEv).
* On [`set_default_subscriber_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant26set_default_subscriber_qosERK13SubscriberQos) it refers to the default constructed
  [`SubscriberQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriberqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13SubscriberQos13SubscriberQosEv).

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/dds_layer/subscriber/subscriberListener/subscriberListener.md -->

<!-- {{{ X-Types API -->
<!-- }}} -->

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-subscriberlistener"></a>

<a id="subscriberlistener"></a>

# SubscriberListener

[`SubscriberListener`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriberlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18SubscriberListenerE) is an abstract class defining the
callbacks that will be triggered in response to state changes on the
[Subscriber](../subscriber/subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriber).
By default, all these callbacks are empty and do nothing.
The user should implement a specialization of this class overriding the callbacks
that are needed on the application.
Callbacks that are not overridden will maintain their empty implementation.

SubscriberListener inherits from [DataReaderListener](../dataReaderListener/dataReaderListener.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareaderlistener).
Therefore, it has the ability to react to all events that are reported to the
[DataReader](../dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader).
Since events are always notified to the most specific Entity Listener that can handle the event,
callbacks that SubscriberListener inherits from
DataReaderListener will only be called if the triggering DataReader has no Listener attached,
or if the callback is disabled by the [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) on the DataReader.

Additionally, SubscriberListener adds the following callback:

* [`on_data_on_readers()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriberlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18SubscriberListener18on_data_on_readersEP10Subscriber):
  New data is available on any DataReader
  belonging to this Subscriber.
  There is no queuing of invocations to this callback, meaning that if several new data changes are received
  at once, only one callback invocation may be issued for all of them, instead of one per change.
  If the application is retrieving the received data on this callback, it must keep
  [reading data](../dataReader/readingData.md#dds-layer-subscriber-accessreceived) until no new changes are left.

#### IMPORTANT
For more information about callbacks and its hierarchy, please refer to
[Listener](../../core/entity/entity.md#dds-layer-core-entity-commonchars-listener).

```c++
class CustomSubscriberListener : public SubscriberListener
{

public:

    CustomSubscriberListener()
        : SubscriberListener()
    {
    }

    virtual ~CustomSubscriberListener()
    {
    }

    virtual void on_data_on_readers(
            Subscriber* sub)
    {
        static_cast<void>(sub);
        std::cout << "New data available" << std::endl;
    }

};
```

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/dds_layer/subscriber/subscriber/createSubscriber.md -->

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-creation"></a>

<a id="creating-a-subscriber"></a>

# Creating a Subscriber

A [Subscriber](subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriber) always belongs to a [DomainParticipant](../../domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant).
Creation of a Subscriber is done with the [`create_subscriber()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant17create_subscriberERK13SubscriberQosR12ReturnCode_tP18SubscriberListenerRK10StatusMask) member function on the
DomainParticipant instance, that acts as a factory for the Subscriber.

Mandatory arguments are:

* The [SubscriberQos](subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriberqos) describing the behavior of the Subscriber.
  If the provided value is `SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT`,
  the value of the [Default SubscriberQos](subscriber.md#dds-layer-defaultsubscriberqos) is used.

Optional arguments are:

* A Listener derived from [SubscriberListener](../subscriberListener/subscriberListener.md#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriberlistener), implementing the callbacks
  that will be triggered in response to events and state changes on the Subscriber.
  By default empty callbacks are used.
* A [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) that activates or deactivates triggering of individual callbacks on the
  SubscriberListener.
  By default all events are enabled.

[`create_subscriber()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant17create_subscriberERK13SubscriberQosR12ReturnCode_tP18SubscriberListenerRK10StatusMask) will return a null pointer if there was an error during the operation, e.g.
if the provided QoS is not compatible or is not supported.
It is advisable to check that the returned value is a valid pointer.

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Subscriber with default SubscriberQos and no Listener
// The value SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT is used to denote the default QoS.
Subscriber* subscriber_with_default_qos =
        participant->create_subscriber(SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == subscriber_with_default_qos)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// A custom SubscriberQos can be provided to the creation method
SubscriberQos custom_qos;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

Subscriber* subscriber_with_custom_qos =
        participant->create_subscriber(custom_qos);
if (nullptr == subscriber_with_custom_qos)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Subscriber with default QoS and a custom Listener.
// CustomSubscriberListener inherits from SubscriberListener.
// The value SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT is used to denote the default QoS.
CustomSubscriberListener custom_listener;
Subscriber* subscriber_with_default_qos_and_custom_listener =
        participant->create_subscriber(SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT, &custom_listener);
if (nullptr == subscriber_with_default_qos_and_custom_listener)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-creation-profile"></a>

<a id="profile-based-creation-of-a-subscriber"></a>

## Profile based creation of a Subscriber

Instead of using a SubscriberQos, the name of a profile
can be used to create a Subscriber with the [`create_subscriber_with_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant30create_subscriber_with_profileERKNSt6stringER12ReturnCode_tP18SubscriberListenerRK10StatusMask)
member function on the DomainParticipant instance.

Mandatory arguments are:

* A string with the name that identifies the Subscriber.

Optional arguments are:

* A Listener derived from SubscriberListener, implementing the callbacks
  that will be triggered in response to events and state changes on the Subscriber.
  By default empty callbacks are used.
* A [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) that activates or deactivates triggering of individual callbacks on the
  SubscriberListener.
  By default all events are enabled.

[`create_subscriber_with_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant30create_subscriber_with_profileERKNSt6stringER12ReturnCode_tP18SubscriberListenerRK10StatusMask) will return a null pointer if there was an error during
the operation, e.g. if the provided QoS is not compatible or is not supported.
It is advisable to check that the returned value is a valid pointer.

#### NOTE
XML profiles must have been loaded previously. See [Loading profiles from an XML file](../../domain/domainParticipantFactory/domainParticipantFactory.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantfactory-load-profiles).

```c++
// First load the XML with the profiles
DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->load_XML_profiles_file("profiles.xml");

// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Subscriber using a profile and no Listener
Subscriber* subscriber_with_profile =
        participant->create_subscriber_with_profile("subscriber_profile");
if (nullptr == subscriber_with_profile)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Subscriber using a profile and a custom Listener.
// CustomSubscriberListener inherits from SubscriberListener.
CustomSubscriberListener custom_listener;
Subscriber* subscriber_with_profile_and_custom_listener =
        participant->create_subscriber_with_profile("subscriber_profile", &custom_listener);
if (nullptr == subscriber_with_profile_and_custom_listener)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-deletion"></a>

<a id="deleting-a-subscriber"></a>

## Deleting a Subscriber

A Subscriber can be deleted with the [`delete_subscriber()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant17delete_subscriberEPK10Subscriber) member function on the
DomainParticipant instance where the Subscriber was created.

#### NOTE
A Subscriber can only be deleted if all Entities belonging to the Subscriber
(DataReaders) have already been deleted.
Otherwise, the function will issue an error and the Subscriber will not be deleted.
This can be performed by using the [`delete_contained_entities()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber25delete_contained_entitiesEv) member function of the
[Subscriber](subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriber).

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a Subscriber
Subscriber* subscriber =
        participant->create_subscriber(SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == subscriber)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Use the Subscriber to communicate
// (...)

// Delete the entities the subscriber created
if (subscriber->delete_contained_entities() != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Subscriber failed to delete the entities it created
    return;
}

// Delete the Subscriber
if (participant->delete_subscriber(subscriber) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-datareader"></a>

<a id="datareader"></a>

# DataReader

A [`DataReader`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataReaderE) is attached to exactly one
[Subscriber](../subscriber/subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriber) that acts as a factory for it.
Additionally, each DataReader is bound to a single
[Topic](../../topic/topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic-topic) since its creation.
This Topic must exist prior to the creation of the
DataReader,
and must be bound to the data type that the DataReader wants to publish.

The effect of creating a new DataReader in a
Subscriber for a specific
Topic is to initiate a new subscription with the name and data type described
by the Topic.

Once the DataReader is created, the application will be informed
when changes in the data value are received from remote publications.
These changes can then be retrieved using the [`DataReader::read_next_sample()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataReader16read_next_sampleEPvP10SampleInfo) or [`DataReader::take_next_sample()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataReader16take_next_sampleEPvP10SampleInfo)
member functions of the DataReader.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-datareaderqos"></a>

<a id="datareaderqos"></a>

default values.

#### NOTE
Reliability kind (whether the publication is reliable or best effort) is not mutable.
However, the [`max_blocking_time`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/reliabilityqospolicy.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds20ReliabilityQosPolicy17max_blocking_timeE) data member of [`ReliabilityQosPolicy`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/reliabilityqospolicy.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds20ReliabilityQosPolicyE) can be modified
any time.

Not all data members of RTPSReliableReaderQos are mutable, please refer to [RTPSReliableReaderQos](../../core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#rtpsreliablereaderqos)
for more information.

The QoS value of a previously created DataReader can be modified using the
[`DataReader::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataReader7set_qosERK13DataReaderQos) member function.

```c++
// Create a DataReader with default DataReaderQos
DataReader* data_reader =
        subscriber->create_datareader(topic, DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_reader)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
DataReaderQos qos = data_reader->get_qos();

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Assign the new Qos to the object
data_reader->set_qos(qos);
```

<a id="dds-layer-defaultdatareaderqos"></a>

<a id="default-datareaderqos"></a>

### Default DataReaderQos

The default DataReaderQos refers to the value returned by the
[`get_default_datareader_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber26get_default_datareader_qosEv) member function on the
[Subscriber](../subscriber/subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriber) instance.
The special value `DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT` can be used as QoS argument on
[`create_datareader()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber17create_datareaderEP16TopicDescriptionRK13DataReaderQosP18DataReaderListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE) or
[`DataReader::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataReader7set_qosERK13DataReaderQos) member functions to indicate that the current default
DataReaderQos should be used.

When the system starts, the default DataReaderQos is equivalent to
the default constructed value [`DataReaderQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareaderqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataReaderQos13DataReaderQosEv).
The default DataReaderQos can be modified at any time using the
[`set_default_datareader_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber26set_default_datareader_qosERK13DataReaderQos) member function on the
Subscriber instance.
Modifying the default DataReaderQos will not affect already existing
[DataReader](#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader) instances.

```c++
// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
DataReaderQos qos_type1 = subscriber->get_default_datareader_qos();

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Set as the new default DataReaderQos
if (subscriber->set_default_datareader_qos(qos_type1) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DataReader with the new default DataReaderQos.
DataReader* data_reader_with_qos_type1 =
        subscriber->create_datareader(topic, DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_reader_with_qos_type1)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Get the current QoS or create a new one from scratch
DataReaderQos qos_type2;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Set as the new default DataReaderQos
if (subscriber->set_default_datareader_qos(qos_type2) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DataReader with the new default DataReaderQos.
DataReader* data_reader_with_qos_type2 =
        subscriber->create_datareader(topic, DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_reader_with_qos_type2)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Resetting the default DataReaderQos to the original default constructed values
if (subscriber->set_default_datareader_qos(DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT)
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// The previous instruction is equivalent to the following
if (subscriber->set_default_datareader_qos(DataReaderQos())
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

[`set_default_datareader_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber26set_default_datareader_qosERK13DataReaderQos) member function also accepts
the special value `DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT` as input argument.
This will reset the current default DataReaderQos to default constructed
value [`DataReaderQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareaderqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataReaderQos13DataReaderQosEv).

```c++
// Create a custom DataReaderQos
DataReaderQos custom_qos;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

// Create a DataWriter with a custom DataReaderQos
DataReader* data_reader = subscriber->create_datareader(topic, custom_qos);
if (nullptr == data_reader)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Set the QoS on the DataWriter to the default
if (data_reader->set_qos(DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// The previous instruction is equivalent to the following:
if (data_reader->set_qos(subscriber->get_default_datareader_qos())
        != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

#### NOTE
The value `DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT` has different meaning depending on where it is used:

* On [`create_datareader()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber17create_datareaderEP16TopicDescriptionRK13DataReaderQosP18DataReaderListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE)
  and [`DataReader::set_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataReader7set_qosERK13DataReaderQos) it refers to the default
  DataReaderQos as returned by
  [`get_default_datareader_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber26get_default_datareader_qosEv).
* On [`set_default_datareader_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber26set_default_datareader_qosERK13DataReaderQos) it refers
  to the default constructed [`DataReaderQos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareaderqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataReaderQos13DataReaderQosEv).

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-datareader-type-support-context"></a>

<a id="type-support-context"></a>

## Type support context

A DataReader can be configured with a [type support context](../../topic/typeSupport/typeSupport.md#dds-layer-topic-type-support-context)
that is forwarded to the [`TopicDataType`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/topicdatatype.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13TopicDataTypeE) callbacks on every read operation.
This allows the type implementation to rely on per-reader information (e.g., bounded sizes) without
resorting to global state.

The context must be set **before** enabling the DataReader using
[`DataReader::set_type_support_context()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataReader24set_type_support_contextERKNSt10shared_ptrIN13TopicDataType7ContextEEE).
Calling this method on an already-enabled DataReader returns `RETCODE_ILLEGAL_OPERATION`.

```c++
// User-defined context struct carrying per-reader configuration.
struct MyContext : public TopicDataType::Context
{
    uint32_t string_max_length = 0;
    uint32_t sequence_max_length = 0;
};

// Create a DataReader (initially disabled, e.g. via participant QoS).
DataReaderQos reader_qos = DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT;
DataReader* reader = subscriber->create_datareader(topic, reader_qos);

// Create a context carrying per-reader configuration.
auto context = std::make_shared<MyContext>();
context->string_max_length = 512;
context->sequence_max_length = 1024;

// Set it before enabling the DataReader.
ReturnCode_t ret = reader->set_type_support_context(context);
assert(ret == RETCODE_OK);

// Then enable the reader (e.g., by enabling its DomainParticipant).
```

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/dds_layer/subscriber/dataReaderListener/dataReaderListener.md -->

<!-- {{{ X-Types API -->
<!-- }}} -->

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-datareaderlistener"></a>

<a id="datareaderlistener"></a>

# DataReaderListener

[`DataReaderListener`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareaderlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataReaderListenerE) is an abstract class defining the callbacks
that will be triggered in response to state changes on the [DataReader](../dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader).
By default, all these callbacks are empty and do nothing.
The user should implement a specialization of this class overriding the callbacks
that are needed on the application.
Callbacks that are not overridden will maintain their empty implementation.

DataReaderListener defines the following callbacks:

* [`on_data_available()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareaderlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataReaderListener17on_data_availableEP10DataReader):
  There is new data available for the application on the DataReader.
  There is no queuing of invocations to this callback, meaning that if several new data changes are received
  at once, only one callback invocation may be issued for all of them, instead of one per change.
  If the application is retrieving the received data on this callback, it must keep
  [reading data](../dataReader/readingData.md#dds-layer-subscriber-accessreceived) until no new changes are left.
* [`on_subscription_matched()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareaderlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataReaderListener23on_subscription_matchedEP10DataReaderRKN7fastdds3dds25SubscriptionMatchedStatusE):
  The DataReader has found a
  [DataWriter](../../publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter) that matches the [Topic](../../topic/topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic-topic) and has
  a common partition and a compatible QoS, or has ceased to be matched with a
  DataWriter that was previously considered to be matched.
  It is also triggered when a matched DataWriter has changed its
  [DataWriterQos](../../publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriterqos).
* [`on_requested_deadline_missed()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareaderlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataReaderListener28on_requested_deadline_missedEP10DataReaderRK29RequestedDeadlineMissedStatus):
  The DataReader did not receive
  data within the deadline period configured on its [DataReaderQos](../dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareaderqos).
  It will be called for each deadline period and data instance for which the
  DataReader missed data.
* [`on_requested_incompatible_qos()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareaderlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataReaderListener29on_requested_incompatible_qosEP10DataReaderRK30RequestedIncompatibleQosStatus):
  The DataReader has found a
  DataWriter that matches the Topic and has
  a common partition, but with a QoS that is incompatible with the one defined on the
  DataReader.
* [`on_liveliness_changed()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareaderlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataReaderListener21on_liveliness_changedEP10DataReaderRK23LivelinessChangedStatus):
  The liveliness status of a matched DataWriter has changed.
  Either a DataWriter that was *inactive* has become *active* or the other
  way around.
* [`on_sample_rejected()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareaderlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataReaderListener18on_sample_rejectedEP10DataReaderRK20SampleRejectedStatus):
  A received data sample was rejected.
  See [SampleRejectedStatus](../../core/status/status.md#dds-layer-core-status-samplerejectedstatus) for further information.
* [`on_sample_lost()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareaderlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DataReaderListener14on_sample_lostEP10DataReaderRK16SampleLostStatus):
  A data sample was lost and will never be received.
  See [SampleLostStatus](../../core/status/status.md#dds-layer-core-status-sampleloststatus) for further information.

#### IMPORTANT
For more information about callbacks and its hierarchy, please refer to
[Listener](../../core/entity/entity.md#dds-layer-core-entity-commonchars-listener).

```c++
class CustomDataReaderListener : public DataReaderListener
{

public:

    CustomDataReaderListener()
        : DataReaderListener()
    {
    }

    virtual ~CustomDataReaderListener()
    {
    }

    void on_data_available(
            DataReader* reader) override
    {
        static_cast<void>(reader);
        std::cout << "Received new data message" << std::endl;
    }

    void on_subscription_matched(
            DataReader* reader,
            const SubscriptionMatchedStatus& info) override
    {
        static_cast<void>(reader);
        if (info.current_count_change == 1)
        {
            std::cout << "Matched a remote DataWriter" << std::endl;
        }
        else if (info.current_count_change == -1)
        {
            std::cout << "Unmatched a remote DataWriter" << std::endl;
        }
    }

    void on_requested_deadline_missed(
            DataReader* reader,
            const RequestedDeadlineMissedStatus& info) override
    {
        static_cast<void>(reader);
        static_cast<void>(info);
        std::cout << "Some data was not received on time" << std::endl;
    }

    void on_liveliness_changed(
            DataReader* reader,
            const LivelinessChangedStatus& info) override
    {
        static_cast<void>(reader);
        if (info.alive_count_change == 1)
        {
            std::cout << "A matched DataWriter has become active" << std::endl;
        }
        else if (info.not_alive_count_change == 1)
        {
            std::cout << "A matched DataWriter has become inactive" << std::endl;
        }
    }

    void on_sample_rejected(
            DataReader* reader,
            const SampleRejectedStatus& info) override
    {
        static_cast<void>(reader);
        static_cast<void>(info);
        std::cout << "A received data sample was rejected" << std::endl;
    }

    void on_requested_incompatible_qos(
            DataReader* reader,
            const RequestedIncompatibleQosStatus& info) override
    {
        std::cout << "Found a remote Topic with incompatible QoS (QoS ID: " << info.last_policy_id
                  << ")" << std::endl;
    }

    void on_sample_lost(
            DataReader* reader,
            const SampleLostStatus& info) override
    {
        static_cast<void>(reader);
        static_cast<void>(info);
        std::cout << "A data sample was lost and will not be received" << std::endl;
    }

};
```

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-datareader-creation"></a>

<a id="creating-a-datareader"></a>

# Creating a DataReader

A [DataReader](dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader) always belongs to a [Subscriber](../subscriber/subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriber).
Creation of a DataReader is done with the [`create_datareader()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber17create_datareaderEP16TopicDescriptionRK13DataReaderQosP18DataReaderListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE) member function on the
Subscriber instance, that acts as a factory for the DataReader.

Mandatory arguments are:

* A [Topic](../../topic/topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic-topic) bound to the data type that will be transmitted.
* The [DataReaderQos](dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareaderqos) describing the behavior of the DataReader.
  If the provided value is `DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT`,
  the value of the [Default DataReaderQos](dataReader.md#dds-layer-defaultdatareaderqos) is used.
  If the provided value is `DATAREADER_QOS_USE_TOPIC_QOS`,
  the values of the default QoS and the provided TopicQoS are used, whereby any policy
  that is set on the TopicQoS overrides the corresponding policy on the default QoS.

Optional arguments are:

* A Listener derived from [DataReaderListener](../dataReaderListener/dataReaderListener.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareaderlistener), implementing the callbacks
  that will be triggered in response to events and state changes on the DataReader.
  By default empty callbacks are used.
* A [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) that activates or deactivates triggering of individual callbacks on the
  DataReaderListener.
  By default all events are enabled.

[`create_datareader()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber17create_datareaderEP16TopicDescriptionRK13DataReaderQosP18DataReaderListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE) will return a null pointer if there was an error during the operation, e.g.
if the provided QoS is not compatible or is not supported.
It is advisable to check that the returned value is a valid pointer.

```c++
// Create a DataReader with default DataReaderQos and no Listener
// The value DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT is used to denote the default QoS.
DataReader* data_reader_with_default_qos =
        subscriber->create_datareader(topic, DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_reader_with_default_qos)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// A custom DataReaderQos can be provided to the creation method
DataReaderQos custom_qos;

// Modify QoS attributes
// (...)

DataReader* data_reader_with_custom_qos =
        subscriber->create_datareader(topic, custom_qos);
if (nullptr == data_reader_with_custom_qos)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DataReader with default QoS and a custom Listener.
// CustomDataReaderListener inherits from DataReaderListener.
// The value DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT is used to denote the default QoS.
CustomDataReaderListener custom_listener;
DataReader* data_reader_with_default_qos_and_custom_listener =
        subscriber->create_datareader(topic, DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT, &custom_listener);
if (nullptr == data_reader_with_default_qos_and_custom_listener)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DataReader with default QoS and a custom TopicQos.
// The value DATAREADER_QOS_USE_TOPIC_QOS is used to denote the default QoS
// and to override the TopicQos.
Topic* topic =
        participant->create_topic("", "", TOPIC_QOS_DEFAULT);
DataReader* data_reader_with_default_qos_and_custom_topic_qos =
        subscriber->create_datareader(topic, DATAREADER_QOS_USE_TOPIC_QOS);
if (nullptr == data_reader_with_default_qos_and_custom_topic_qos)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-datareader-creation-profile"></a>

<a id="profile-based-creation-of-a-datareader"></a>

## Profile based creation of a DataReader

Instead of using a DataReaderQos, the name of a profile
can be used to create a DataReader with the [`create_datareader_with_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber30create_datareader_with_profileEP16TopicDescriptionRKNSt6stringEP18DataReaderListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE)
member function on the Subscriber instance.

Mandatory arguments are:

* A Topic bound to the data type that will be transmitted.
* A string with the name that identifies the DataReader.

Optional arguments are:

* A Listener derived from DataReaderListener, implementing the callbacks
  that will be triggered in response to events and state changes on the DataReader.
  By default empty callbacks are used.
* A [`StatusMask`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/status/statusmask.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10StatusMaskE) that activates or deactivates triggering of individual callbacks on the
  DataReaderListener.
  By default all events are enabled.

[`create_datareader_with_profile()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber30create_datareader_with_profileEP16TopicDescriptionRKNSt6stringEP18DataReaderListenerRK10StatusMaskNSt10shared_ptrIN7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolEEE) will return a null pointer if there was an error during the operation,
e.g. if the provided QoS is not compatible or is not supported.
It is advisable to check that the returned value is a valid pointer.

#### NOTE
XML profiles must have been loaded previously. See [Loading profiles from an XML file](../../domain/domainParticipantFactory/domainParticipantFactory.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantfactory-load-profiles).

```c++
// First load the XML with the profiles
DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->load_XML_profiles_file("profiles.xml");

// Create a DataReader using a profile and no Listener
DataReader* data_reader_with_profile =
        subscriber->create_datareader_with_profile(topic, "data_reader_profile");
if (nullptr == data_reader_with_profile)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a DataReader using a profile and a custom Listener.
// CustomDataReaderListener inherits from DataReaderListener.
CustomDataReaderListener custom_listener;
DataReader* data_reader_with_profile_and_custom_listener =
        subscriber->create_datareader_with_profile(topic, "data_reader_profile", &custom_listener);
if (nullptr == data_reader_with_profile_and_custom_listener)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-datareader-with-payload-pool-creation"></a>

<a id="creating-a-datawriter-with-a-custom-payloadpool"></a>

## Creating a DataWriter with a custom PayloadPool

A custom [PayloadPool](../../../rtps_layer/rtps_layer.md#rtps-layer-custom-payload-pool) can be passed as an argument during the creation of a
[DataReader](dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader).
This allows for customizing the management of the information exchanged between DataWriters and DataReaders.
The same configuration can be set in the
[opposite endpoint](../../publisher/dataWriter/createDataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter-with-payload-pool-creation).

```c++
// A DataReaderQos must be provided to the creation method
DataReaderQos qos;

// Create PayloadPool
std::shared_ptr<CustomPayloadPool> payload_pool = std::make_shared<CustomPayloadPool>();

DataReader* data_reader = subscriber->create_datareader(topic, qos, nullptr, StatusMask::all(), payload_pool);
if (nullptr == data_reader)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

This configuration can be performed also in the [RTPS layer](../../../rtps_layer/rtps_layer.md#rtps-layer-custom-payload-pool).
The [customization example](../../../rtps_layer/rtps_layer.md#rtps-layer-payload-pool-example) applies both layers.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-datareader-deletion"></a>

<a id="deleting-a-datareader"></a>

## Deleting a DataReader

A DataReader can be deleted with the [`delete_datareader()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/subscriber_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10Subscriber17delete_datareaderEPK10DataReader) member function on the
[Subscriber](../subscriber/subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber-subscriber) instance where the DataReader was created.

#### NOTE
A DataReader can only be deleted if all Entities belonging to the DataReader
(QueryConditions) have already been deleted.
Otherwise, the function will issue an error and the DataReader will not be deleted.
This can be performed by using the [`delete_contained_entities()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataReader25delete_contained_entitiesEv) member function of the
[DataReader](dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader).

```c++
// Create a DataReader
DataReader* data_reader =
        subscriber->create_datareader(topic, DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == data_reader)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Use the DataReader to communicate
// (...)

// Delete the entities the DataReader created
if (data_reader->delete_contained_entities() != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // DataReader failed to delete the entities it created.
    return;
}

// Delete the DataReader
if (subscriber->delete_datareader(data_reader) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo"></a>

<a id="sampleinfo"></a>

# SampleInfo

When a sample is retrieved from the [DataReader](../dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader), in addition to the sample data,
a [`SampleInfo`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfoE) instance is returned.
This object contains additional information that complements the returned data value and helps on its interpretation.
For example, if the [valid_data](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-validdata) value is `false`, the
DataReader is not informing the application about a new value in the data instance,
but a change on its status, and the returned data value must be discarded.

Please, refer to the section [Accessing received data](../dataReader/readingData.md#dds-layer-subscriber-accessreceived) for more information regarding how received
data can be accessed on the DataReader.

The following sections describe the data members of [`SampleInfo`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfoE)
and the meaning of each one in relation to the returned sample data.

* [sample_state](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-samplestate)
* [view_state](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-viewstate)
* [instance_state](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-instancestate)
* [disposed_generation_count](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-disposedgenerationcount)
* [no_writers_generation_count](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-nowritersgenerationcount)
* [sample_rank](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-samplerank)
* [generation_rank](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-generationrank)
* [absolute_generation_rank](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-absolutegenerationrank)
* [source_timestamp](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-sourcetimestamp)
* [instance_handle](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-instancehandle)
* [publication_handle](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-publicationhandle)
* [valid_data](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-validdata)
* [sample_identity](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-sampleidentity)
* [related_sample_identity](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-relatedsampleidentity)

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-samplestate"></a>

<a id="sample-state"></a>

## sample_state

[`sample_state`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo12sample_stateE) indicates whether or not the corresponding data sample has already
been read previously.
It can take one of these values:

* **READ**: The data sample has already been *read* or *taken* previously.
* **NOT_READ**: This is the first time this data sample has been retrieved.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-viewstate"></a>

<a id="view-state"></a>

## view_state

[`view_state`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo10view_stateE) indicates whether or not this is the very first sample
of this data instance that the DataReader retrieves.
It can take one of these values:

* **NEW**: This is the first time a sample of this instance is retrieved.
* **NOT_NEW**: Other samples of this instance have been retrieved previously.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-instancestate"></a>

<a id="instance-state"></a>

## instance_state

[`instance_state`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo14instance_stateE) indicates whether the instance is currently in existence
or it has been disposed.
In the latter case, it also provides information about the reason for the disposal.
It can take one of these values:

* **ALIVE**: The instance is currently in existence.
* **NOT_ALIVE_DISPOSED**: A remote [DataWriter](../../publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter) disposed the instance.
* **NOT_ALIVE_NO_WRITERS**: The DataReader disposed the instance because no remote
  DataWriter that was publishing the instance is *alive*.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-disposedgenerationcount"></a>

<a id="disposed-generation-count"></a>

## disposed_generation_count

[`disposed_generation_count`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo25disposed_generation_countE) indicates the number of times the instance had become alive after it was
disposed.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-nowritersgenerationcount"></a>

<a id="no-writers-generation-count"></a>

## no_writers_generation_count

[`no_writers_generation_count`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo27no_writers_generation_countE) indicates the number of times the instance had become alive after it was
disposed as `NOT_ALIVE_NO_WRITERS`.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-samplerank"></a>

<a id="sample-rank"></a>

## sample_rank

[`sample_rank`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo11sample_rankE) indicates the number of samples of the same instance that have been received after
this one.
For example, a value of `5` means that there are 5 newer samples available on the DataReader.

#### NOTE
Currently the [`sample_rank`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo11sample_rankE) is not implemented, and its value is always set to `0`.
It will be implemented on a future release of *Fast DDS*.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-generationrank"></a>

<a id="generation-rank"></a>

## generation_rank

[`generation_rank`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo15generation_rankE) indicates the number of times the instance was disposed and become alive again
between the time the sample was received and the time the most recent sample of the same instance
that is still held in the collection was received.

#### NOTE
Currently the [`generation_rank`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo15generation_rankE) is not implemented, and its value is always set to `0`.
It will be implemented on a future release of *Fast DDS*.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-absolutegenerationrank"></a>

<a id="absolute-generation-rank"></a>

## absolute_generation_rank

`absolute_generation_rank` indicates the number of times the instance was disposed and become alive
again between the time the sample was received and the time the most recent sample of the same instance
(which may not be in the collection) was received.

#### NOTE
Currently the `absolute_generation_rank` is not implemented, and its value is always set to `0`.
It will be implemented on a future release of *Fast DDS*.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-sourcetimestamp"></a>

<a id="source-timestamp"></a>

## source_timestamp

[`source_timestamp`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo16source_timestampE) holds the time stamp provided by the DataWriter when
the sample was published.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-instancehandle"></a>

<a id="instance-handle"></a>

## instance_handle

[`instance_handle`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo15instance_handleE) handles of the local instance.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-publicationhandle"></a>

<a id="publication-handle"></a>

## publication_handle

[`publication_handle`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo18publication_handleE) handles of the DataWriter that published the data change.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-validdata"></a>

<a id="valid-data"></a>

## valid_data

[`valid_data`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo10valid_dataE) is a boolean that indicates whether the data sample contains a change in the value or not.
Samples with this value set to false are used to communicate a change in the instance status, e.g.,
a change in the liveliness of the instance.
In this case, the data sample should be dismissed as all the relevant information is in the
data members of SampleInfo.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-sampleidentity"></a>

<a id="sample-identity"></a>

## sample_identity

[`sample_identity`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo15sample_identityE) is an extension for requester-replier configuration.
It contains the DataWriter and the sequence number of the current message, and it is used
by the replier to fill the [related_sample_identity](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-relatedsampleidentity) when it sends the reply.

<a id="dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-relatedsampleidentity"></a>

<a id="related-sample-identity"></a>

## related_sample_identity

[`related_sample_identity`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/sampleinfo.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10SampleInfo23related_sample_identityE) is an extension for requester-replier configuration.
On reply messages, it contains the [sample_identity](#dds-layer-subscriber-sampleinfo-sampleidentity) of the related request message.
It is used by the requester to be able to link each reply to the appropriate request.

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/dds_layer/subscriber/dataReader/readingData.md -->
