<a id="dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic-default-filter"></a>

<a id="the-default-sql-like-filter"></a>

# The default SQL-like filter

Filter expressions used by [ContentFilteredTopic](contentFilteredTopic.md#dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic) API may use a subset of SQL syntax, extended with
the possibility to use program variables in the SQL expression.
This section shows this default SQL-like syntax and how to use it.
Apart from the syntax described in this section, certain restrictions apply to the allowed SQL expressions.
These restrictions can be relaxed or tightened by the user, as explained in
[SQL Filter Expression limits](../../../property_policies/non_consolidated_qos.md#properties-sql-filter-expression-limits).

* [Grammar](#default-sql-filter-grammar)
* [Like condition](#default-sql-filter-like)
* [Match condition](#default-sql-filter-match)
* [Type comparisons](#default-sql-filter-type-comparisons)
* [Example](#default-sql-filter-example)

<a id="default-sql-filter-grammar"></a>

<a id="grammar"></a>

## Grammar

The allowed SQL expressions are defined with the BNF-grammar below.

The following conventions are made:

- “Terminals” are quoted.
- `TOKENS` are typeset in code block with black font color.

```
 FilterExpression

 Condition

 Predicate |

 Condition "AND" Condition |

 Condition "OR" Condition |

 "NOT" Condition |

 "(" Condition ")"

 ComparisonPredicate |

 BetweenPredicate

 FIELDNAME RelOp Parameter |

 Parameter RelOp FIELDNAME |

 FIELDNAME RelOp FIELDNAME

 FIELDNAME "BETWEEN" Range |

 FIELDNAME "NOT BETWEEN" Range

 "=" | ">" | ">=" | "<" | "<=" |

 "<>" | "!=" | like | match

 Parameter "AND" Parameter

 BOOLEANVALUE |

 INTEGERVALUE |

 CHARVALUE |

 FLOATVALUE |

 STRINGVALUE |

 ENUMERATEDVALUE |

 PARAMETER
```

“Terminals” and `TOKENS` are case sensitive but both uppercase and lowercase are supported.

The syntax and meaning of the tokens used in the SQL grammar is described as follows:

- **FIELDNAME**: is a reference to a field in the data-structure.
  The dot `.` is used to navigate through nested structures.
  The number of dots that may be used in a FIELDNAME is unlimited.
  The FIELDNAME can refer to fields at any depth in the data structure.
  The names of the field are those specified in the IDL definition of the corresponding structure.
  ```
   FieldNamePart ( "." FieldNamePart )*

   Identifier ( "[" Integer "]" )?
  ```

  An example of FIELDNAMEs:

  ### Filter expression

  ```default
  "points[0] = 0 AND color.red < 100"
  ```

  ### Associated IDL

  ```IDL
  struct Color
  {
      octet red;
      octet green;
      octet blue;
  };

  struct Shape
  {
      long points[4];
      Color color;
  };
  ```
- **BOOLEANVALUE**: Can either be true of false, case sensitive.
  ```
   ["TRUE", "true", "FALSE", "false"]
  ```
- **INTEGERVALUE**: Any series of digits, optionally preceded by a plus or minus sign, representing a decimal integer
  value within the range of the system.
  A hexadecimal number is preceded by `0x` and must be a valid hexadecimal expression.
  ```
   (["+","-"])? Integer

   (["0"-"9"])+ | ["0x","0X"](["0"-"9", "A"-"F", "a"-"f"])+
  ```

  An example of INTEGERVALUE:
  ```default
  value = -10
  ```
- **CHARVALUE**: A single character enclosed between single quotes.
  ```
   "'" Character "'"

   ~["\n"]
  ```

  An example of CHARVALUE:
  ```default
  value = 'c'
  ```
- **FLOATVALUE**: Any series of digits, optionally preceded by a plus or minus sign and optionally including a floating
  point (`.`).
  A power-of-ten expression may be postfixed, which has the syntax e:sup:n, where `n` is a number, optionally
  preceded by a plus or minus sign.
  ```
   (["+"], "-"])? (Integer Exponent | Integer Fractional | Integer Fractional Exponent)

   "." Integer

   ["e","E"] (["+"], "-"])? Integer
  ```

  An example of FLOATVALUE:
  ```default
  value = 10.1e-10
  ```
- **STRINGVALUE**: Any series of characters encapsulated in single quotes, except a new-line character or a right quote.
  A string starts with a left or right quote, but ends with a right quote.
  ```
   ["'"] ~["'", "\r", "\n"] ["'"]
  ```

  An example of STRINGVALUE:
  ```default
  value = 'This is a string'
  ```
- **ENUMERATEDVALUE**: An enumerated value is a reference to a value declared within an enumeration.
  Enumerated values consist of the name of the enumeration label enclosed in single quotes.
  The name used for the enumeration label must correspond to the label names specified in the IDL definition of the
  enumeration.
  ```
   ["'"] ~["'", "\r", "\n"] ["'"]
  ```

  An example of ENUMERATEDVALUE:

  ### Filter expression

  ```default
  value = 'ENUM_VALUE_1'
  ```

  ### Associated IDL

  ```default
  enum MyEnum
  {
      ENUM_VALUE_1,
      ENUM_VALUE_2,
      ENUM_VALUE_3
  };

  struct Enumerators
  {
      MyEnum value;
  };
  ```
- **PARAMETER**: A parameter is of the form `%n`, where `n` represents a natural number (zero included) smaller than
  100.
  It refers to the `n + 1 th` argument in the given context.
  ```
   ["%"] ["0"-"9"] (["0"-"9"])?
  ```

  An example of PARAMETER:
  ```default
  value = %1
  ```

<a id="default-sql-filter-like"></a>

<a id="like-condition"></a>

## Like condition

The [like](https://www.w3schools.com/sql/sql_like.asp) operator is similar as the one defined by SQL.
This operator can only be used with strings.
There are two wildcards that could be used in conjunction with this operator

- The percent sign `%` (or its alias `*`) represents zero, one, or multiple characters.
- The underscore sign `_` (or its alias `?`) represents one single character.

All wildcards can also be used in combinations.

An example of `like` operator

### Filter expression

```default
"str like '%bird%'"
```

### Associated IDL

```IDL
struct Like
{
    string str;
};
```

where string `There are birds flying` will return `true`.

<a id="default-sql-filter-match"></a>

<a id="match-condition"></a>

## Match condition

The `match` operator performs a full-text search using a regular expression.
This operator can only be used with strings.
It uses the [Basic Regular Expression (BRE) defined by POSIX](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/V1_chap09.html#tag_09_03).

An example of `match` operator

### Filter expression

```default
"str match '^The'"
```

### Associated IDL

```IDL
struct Like
{
    string str;
};
```

where string `There are birds flying` will return `true`.

<a id="default-sql-filter-type-comparisons"></a>

<a id="type-comparisons"></a>

## Type comparisons

For the supported operators in the grammar, next table shows the type compatibility.

| Operator1 | Operator2   | BOOLEAN   | INTEGER   | FLOAT   | CHAR   | STRING   | ENUM   |
|-------------------------|-----------|-----------|---------|--------|----------|--------|
| BOOLEAN                 | ✅         | ✅         | ❌       | ❌      | ❌        | ❌      |
| INTEGER                 | ✅         | ✅         | ✅       | ❌      | ❌        | ❌      |
| FLOAT                   | ❌         | ✅         | ✅       | ❌      | ❌        | ❌      |
| CHAR                    | ❌         | ❌         | ❌       | ✅      | ✅        | ❌      |
| STRING                  | ❌         | ❌         | ❌       | ✅      | ✅        | ❌      |
| ENUM                    | ❌         | ✅         | ❌       | ❌      | ❌        | ✅ \*   |

**(\*)** Only for the same enumerated type.

<a id="default-sql-filter-example"></a>

<a id="example"></a>

## Example

Assuming Topic `Shape` has next IDL definition.

```IDL
struct Shape
{
    long x,
    long y,
    long z,
    long width,
    long height
};
```

An example of filter expression would be:

```default
"x < 23 AND y > 50 AND width BETWEEN %0 AND %1"
```

A [ContentFilteredTopic](contentFilteredTopic.md#dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic) may be created using this filter expression as explained in section
[Creating a ContentFilteredTopic](createContentFilteredTopic.md#dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic-creation).

```c++
ContentFilteredTopic* sql_filter_topic =
        participant->create_contentfilteredtopic("Shape", topic,
                "x < 23 AND y > 50 AND width BETWEEN %0 AND %1",
                {"10", "20"});
```

In this example parameters are used.
Internally the [ContentFilteredTopic](contentFilteredTopic.md#dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic) will be created with the filter expression below, after
setting the provided parameters.

```default
"x < 23 AND y > 50 AND width BETWEEN 10 AND 20"
```

<a id="dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic-custom-filters"></a>

<a id="using-custom-filters"></a>

# Using custom filters

Fast DDS API supports the creation and later registration of user’s custom filters to be used in the creation of a
[`ContentFilteredTopic`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/contentfilteredtopic.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds20ContentFilteredTopicE).
Required steps for using a Custom Filter are:

- [Creating the Custom Filter](#dds-layer-topic-customfilter-creation)
- [Creating the Factory for the Custom Filter](#dds-layer-topic-customfilter-factory)
- [Registering the Factory](#dds-layer-topic-customfilter-register)
- [Creating a ContentFilteredTopic using the Custom Filter](#dds-layer-topic-customfilter-create-topic)

<a id="dds-layer-topic-customfilter-creation"></a>

<a id="creating-the-custom-filter"></a>

## Creating the Custom Filter

A custom filter must be implemented by a class which inherits from [`IContentFilter`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/icontentfilter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds14IContentFilterE).
Only one function must be implemented, overriding [`evaluate()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/icontentfilter.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds14IContentFilter8evaluateERK17SerializedPayloadRK16FilterSampleInfoRK6GUID_t).
Each time a sample is received by a [`DataReader`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataReaderE), this function is called with next arguments.

- `payload` - The serialized payload of the sample which the custom filter has to evaluate.
- `sample_info` - The extra information which accompanies the sample.
- `reader_guid` - The GUID of the reader for which the filter is being evaluated.

The function returns a boolean where `true` implies the sample is accepted and `false` rejects the sample.

Next snippet code shows an example of Custom Filter which deserialize the `index` field from a serialized sample and
rejects samples where `index` > `low_mark_` and `index` < `high_mark_`.

```c++
class MyCustomFilter : public IContentFilter
{
public:

    MyCustomFilter(
            int low_mark,
            int high_mark)
        : low_mark_(low_mark)
        , high_mark_(high_mark)
    {
    }

    bool evaluate(
            const SerializedPayload& payload,
            const FilterSampleInfo& sample_info,
            const GUID_t& reader_guid) const override
    {
        // Deserialize the `index` field from the serialized sample.
        /* IDL
         *
         * struct HelloWorld
         * {
         *     long index;
         *     string message;
         * }
         */
        eprosima::fastcdr::FastBuffer fastbuffer(reinterpret_cast<char*>(payload.data), payload.length);
        eprosima::fastcdr::Cdr deser(fastbuffer);
        // Deserialize encapsulation.
        deser.read_encapsulation();
        int index = 0;

        // Deserialize `index` field.
        try
        {
            deser >> index;
        }
        catch (eprosima::fastcdr::exception::NotEnoughMemoryException& exception)
        {
            return false;
        }

        // Custom filter: reject samples where index > low_mark_ and index < high_mark_.
        if (index > low_mark_ && index < high_mark_)
        {
            return false;
        }

        return true;
    }

private:

    int low_mark_ = 0;
    int high_mark_ = 0;

};
```

<a id="dds-layer-topic-customfilter-factory"></a>

<a id="creating-the-factory-for-the-custom-filter"></a>

## Creating the Factory for the Custom Filter

Fast DDS creates filters through a factory.
Therefore a factory which provides instantiating of a Custom Filter must be implemented.

A Custom Filter’s factory has to inherit from [`IContentFilterFactory`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/icontentfilterfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds21IContentFilterFactoryE).
This interface requires two functions to be implemented.

Each time a Custom Filter has to be created or updated, [`create_contentfilteredtopic()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant27create_contentfilteredtopicERKNSt6stringEP5TopicRKNSt6stringERKNSt6vectorINSt6stringEEER12ReturnCode_t) calls
internally [`create_content_filter()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/icontentfilterfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds21IContentFilterFactory21create_content_filterEPKcPKcPK13TopicDataTypePKcRK12ParameterSeqRP14IContentFilter) with these arguments:

- `filter_class_name` - Filter class name for which the factory is being called.
  It allows using the same factory for different filter classes.
- `type_name` - Type name of the topic being filtered.
- `data_type` - Type support object of the topic being filtered.
- `filter_expression` - Custom filter expression.
- `filter_parameters` - Values to set for the filter parameters (where custom filter expression has its pattern to
  substitute them).
- `filter_instance` - When a filter is being created, it will be `nullptr` on input, and will have the pointer to
  the created filter instance on output.
  When a filter is being updated, it will have a previously returned pointer on input.

This function should return the result of the operation.

When a Custom Filter should be removed, [`delete_contentfilteredtopic()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant27delete_contentfilteredtopicEPK20ContentFilteredTopic) calls internally
[`delete_content_filter()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/icontentfilterfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds21IContentFilterFactory21delete_content_filterEPKcP14IContentFilter).
The factory must remove the provided Custom Filter’s instance.

Next snippet code shows an example of Custom Filter’s factory which manages instances of the Custom Filter implemented
in the previous section.

```c++
class MyCustomFilterFactory : public IContentFilterFactory
{
public:

    ReturnCode_t create_content_filter(
            const char* filter_class_name, // My custom filter class name is 'MY_CUSTOM_FILTER'.
            const char* type_name, // This custom filter only supports one type: 'HelloWorld'.
            const TopicDataType* /*data_type*/, // Not used in this implementation.
            const char* filter_expression, // This Custom Filter doesn't implement a filter expression.
            const ParameterSeq& filter_parameters, // Always need two parameters to be set: low_mark and high_mark.
            IContentFilter*& filter_instance) override
    {
        // Check the ContentFilteredTopic should be created by my factory.
        if (0 != strcmp(filter_class_name, "MY_CUSTOM_FILTER"))
        {
            return RETCODE_BAD_PARAMETER;
        }

        // Check the ContentFilteredTopic is created for the unique type this Custom Filter supports.
        if (0 != strcmp(type_name, "HelloWorld"))
        {
            return RETCODE_BAD_PARAMETER;
        }

        // Check that the two mandatory filter parameters are set.
        if (2 != filter_parameters.length())
        {
            return RETCODE_BAD_PARAMETER;
        }

        // If there is an update, delete previous instance.
        if (nullptr != filter_instance)
        {
            delete(dynamic_cast<MyCustomFilter*>(filter_instance));
        }

        // Instantiation of the Custom Filter.
        filter_instance = new MyCustomFilter(std::stoi(filter_parameters[0]), std::stoi(filter_parameters[1]));

        return RETCODE_OK;
    }

    ReturnCode_t delete_content_filter(
            const char* filter_class_name,
            IContentFilter* filter_instance) override
    {
        // Check the ContentFilteredTopic should be created by my factory.
        if (0 != strcmp(filter_class_name, "MY_CUSTOM_FILTER"))
        {
            return RETCODE_BAD_PARAMETER;
        }

        // Deletion of the Custom Filter.
        delete(dynamic_cast<MyCustomFilter*>(filter_instance));

        return RETCODE_OK;
    }

};
```

<a id="dds-layer-topic-customfilter-register"></a>

<a id="registering-the-factory"></a>

## Registering the Factory

To be able to use the Custom Filter in an application, the Custom Filter’s factory must be registered in the
[`DomainParticipant`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipantE).
Next snippet code shows how to register a factory through API function
[`register_content_filter_factory()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant31register_content_filter_factoryEPKcPC21IContentFilterFactory).

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create Custom Filter Factory
MyCustomFilterFactory* factory = new MyCustomFilterFactory();


// Registration of the factory
if (RETCODE_OK !=
        participant->register_content_filter_factory("MY_CUSTOM_FILTER", factory))
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="dds-layer-topic-customfilter-create-topic"></a>

<a id="creating-a-contentfilteredtopic-using-the-custom-filter"></a>

## Creating a ContentFilteredTopic using the Custom Filter

[Creating a ContentFilteredTopic](createContentFilteredTopic.md#dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic-creation) explains how to create a [`ContentFilteredTopic`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/contentfilteredtopic.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds20ContentFilteredTopicE).
In the case of using a Custom Filter, [`create_contentfilteredtopic()`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant27create_contentfilteredtopicERKNSt6stringEP5TopicRKNSt6stringERKNSt6vectorINSt6stringEEER12ReturnCode_t) has an overload adding an
argument to select the Custom Filter.

Next snippet code shows how to create a [`ContentFilteredTopic`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/contentfilteredtopic.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds20ContentFilteredTopicE) using the Custom Filter.

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant in the desired domain
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create the Topic.
Topic* topic =
        participant->create_topic("HelloWorldTopic", "HelloWorld", TOPIC_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == topic)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Create a ContentFilteredTopic selecting the Custom Filter and using no expression with two parameters
// Filter expression cannot be an empty one even when it is not used by the custom filter, as that effectively
// disables any filtering
std::string expression = " ";
std::vector<std::string> parameters;
parameters.push_back("10"); // Parameter for low_mark
parameters.push_back("20"); // Parameter for low_mark
ContentFilteredTopic* filter_topic =
        participant->create_contentfilteredtopic("HelloWorldFilteredTopic1", topic, expression, parameters,
                "MY_CUSTOM_FILTER");
if (nullptr == filter_topic)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// The ContentFilteredTopic instances can then be used to create DataReader objects.
Subscriber* subscriber =
        participant->create_subscriber(SUBSCRIBER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == subscriber)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

DataReader* reader_on_filter = subscriber->create_datareader(filter_topic, DATAREADER_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == reader_on_filter)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

#### IMPORTANT
Even though this specific custom filtering example is not using the filter expression, mind that the expression
cannot be an empty string as that disables filtering as explained in
[Creating a ContentFilteredTopic](createContentFilteredTopic.md#dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic-creation).

#### NOTE
Deleting a ContentFilteredTopic which uses a Custom Filter is done exactly in the same manner explained in
[Deleting a ContentFilteredTopic](createContentFilteredTopic.md#dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic-deletion).

<a id="dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic-writer-side"></a>

<a id="where-is-filtering-applied-writer-vs-reader-side"></a>

# Where is filtering applied: writer vs reader side

[Content filters](contentFilteredTopic.md#dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic) may be evaluated on either side, as the DataWriter obtains
the filter expression from the DataReader during discovery.
Filtering on the writer side can save network bandwidth at the cost of increasing CPU usage on the writer.

<a id="dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic-writer-restrictions"></a>

<a id="conditions-for-writer-side-filtering"></a>

## Conditions for writer side filtering

A DataWriter will perform filter evaluation in the DataReader stead whenever all of the following conditions are met;
filtering will otherwise be performed by the DataReader.

- The DataWriter has infinite liveliness.
  See [LivelinessQosPolicy](../../core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#livelinessqospolicy).
- Communication with the DataReader is neither [intra-process](../../../transport/intraprocess.md#intraprocess-delivery) nor
  [data-sharing](../../../transport/datasharing.md#datasharing-delivery).
- The DataReader is not using multicast.
- The DataWriter is filtering for no more DataReaders than the maximum value set on
  [`reader_filters_allocation`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/writerresourcelimitsqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds23WriterResourceLimitsQos25reader_filters_allocationE).
  - There is a [resource-limit policy](../../core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#writerresourcelimitsqos) on [DataWriterQos](../../publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriterqos) that controls the allocation
    behavior of writer-side filtering resources.
    Setting a maximum value of 0 disables filter evaluation on the writer side.
    A maximum value of 32 (the default value) means the writer will perform filter evaluation for up to 32 readers.
  - If the DataWriter is evaluating filters for `writer_resource_limits.reader_filters_allocation.maximum`
    DataReaders, and a new filtered DataReader is created, then the filter for the newly created DataReader
    will be evaluated on the reader side.

<a id="dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic-writer-race-condition"></a>

<a id="discovery-race-condition"></a>

## Discovery race condition

On applications where the filter expression and/or the expression parameters are updated, there may be a
situation where the DataWriter will apply the old version of the filter until it receives updated information
through discovery.
This may imply that a publication made a short time after the DataReader updated the filter, but before the
updated discovery information is received by the DataWriter, may not be sent to the DataReader, even if the
new filter would have told otherwise.
Publications made after the updated discovery information is received will use the updated filter.

If some critical application considers this race condition issue unbearable, filtering on the writer side
can be disabled by setting the maximum value on [`reader_filters_allocation`](../../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/writerresourcelimitsqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds23WriterResourceLimitsQos25reader_filters_allocationE) to 0.

<a id="dds-layer-topic-contentfilteredtopic-writer-side-late-joiners"></a>

<a id="writer-side-filtering-on-late-joiners-pro"></a>

## Writer side filtering on late joiners **[Pro]**

By default, when a late joiner DataReader is discovered (non-volatile durability scenario), the DataWriter will not
apply the filter for that DataReader on historical samples.
This means that the late joiner DataReader will receive all historical samples, even those that would not match its
filter, which could cause performance degradation on resource-limited systems.

It is possible however to configure a DataWriter to perform writer-side filtering on late joiners by setting the
[DataWriterQos](../../publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriterqos) property `fastdds.content_filtering_on_late_joiners` to `true`.

| PropertyPolicyQos name                        | PropertyPolicyQos value   | Default value   |
|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------------|-----------------|
| `"fastdds.content_filtering_on_late_joiners"` | `bool`                    | `false`         |

### C++

```c++
DataWriterQos wqos;

// Enable content filtering on late joiners for this DataWriter
wqos.properties().properties().emplace_back(
    "fastdds.content_filtering_on_late_joiners",
    "true");
```

### XML

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<dds>
    <profiles xmlns="http://www.eprosima.com">
        <data_writer profile_name="cft_on_late_joiners_xml_profile">
            <propertiesPolicy>
                <properties>
                    <!-- Enable content filtering on late joiners -->
                    <property>
                        <name>fastdds.content_filtering_on_late_joiners</name>
                        <value>true</value>
                    </property>
                </properties>
            </propertiesPolicy>
        </data_writer>
    </profiles>
</dds>
```

<a id="dds-layer-topic-fastddsgen"></a>

<a id="fast-dds-gen-for-data-types-source-code-generation"></a>

# Fast DDS-Gen for data types source code generation

*eProsima Fast DDS* comes with a built-in source code generation tool, *Fast DDS-Gen*, which eases the process of
translating an IDL specification of a data type to a functional implementation.
Thus, this tool automatically generates the source code of a data type defined using IDL.
A basic use of the tool is described below.
To learn about all the features that *Fast DDS* offers, please refer to [Fast DDS-Gen](../../../../fastddsgen/introduction/introduction.md#fastddsgen-intro) section.

<a id="basic-usage"></a>

## Basic usage

*Fast DDS* can be executed by calling *fastddsgen* on Linux or *fastddsgen.bat* on Windows.
The IDL file containing the data type definition is given with the `<IDLfile>` argument.

| **Linux**                                                                |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ```bash<br/>fastddsgen [<options>] <IDLfile> [<IDLfile> ...]<br/>```     |
| **Windows**                                                              |
| ```bash<br/>fastddsgen.bat [<options>] <IDLfile> [<IDLfile> ...]<br/>``` |

Among the available arguments defined in [Usage](../../../../fastddsgen/usage/usage.md#fastddsgen-usage), the main *Fast DDS-Gen* options for data type source
code generation are the following:

* `-replace`: It replaces existing files in case the data type files have been previously generated.
* `-help`: It lists the currently supported platforms and Visual Studio versions.
* `-no-typeobjectsupport`: It disables the automatic generation of the [TypeObject representation](../../../xtypes/discovery_matching.md#xtypes-discovery-matching) registration code.
* `-example`: It generates a basic example of a DDS application and the files to build it for
  the given `platform`.
  Thus, *Fast DDS-Gen* tool can generate a sample application using the provided data type, together with a
  Makefile, to compile it on Linux distributions, and a Visual Studio project for Windows.
  To see an example of this please refer to tutorial [Building a publish/subscribe application](../../../../fastddsgen/pubsub_app/pubsub_app.md#fastddsgen-pubsub-app).

<a id="output-files"></a>

## Output files

*Fast DDS-Gen* outputs several files.
Assuming the IDL file had the name  *“Mytype”*, and none of the above options have been defined, these files are:

* MyType.hpp: Type definition.
* MyTypePubSubType.cxx/.hpp: Serialization and deserialization source code for the data type.
  It also defines the `getKey()` member function of the `MyTypePubSubType` class in case the
  topic implements keys (see [Data types with a key](../typeSupport/typeSupport.md#dds-layer-topic-keyed-data-types)).
* MyTypeCdrAux.hpp/.ipp: Auxiliary methods required by Fast CDR for type encoding and decoding.
* MyTypeTypeObjectSupport.cxx/.hpp: Auxiliary code required for [TypeObject representation](../../../xtypes/discovery_matching.md#xtypes-discovery-matching) generation and registration.

<a id="rtps-layer"></a>

<a id="id1"></a>

# RTPS Layer

The lower level RTPS Layer of *eprosima Fast DDS* serves an implementation of the protocol defined in the
[RTPS standard](https://www.omg.org/spec/DDSI-RTPS/2.2).
This layer provides more control over the internals of the communication protocol than the [DDS Layer](../dds_layer/dds_layer.md#dds-layer), so advanced
users have finer control over the library’s functionalities.

<a id="relation-to-the-dds-layer"></a>

## Relation to the DDS Layer

Elements of this layer map one-to-one with elements from the [DDS Layer](../dds_layer/dds_layer.md#dds-layer), with a few additions.
This correspondence is shown in the following table:

| [DDS Layer](../dds_layer/dds_layer.md#dds-layer)                                                            | [RTPS Layer](#rtps-layer)   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| [Domain](../dds_layer/domain/domain.md#dds-layer-domain)                                                    | RTPSDomain                  |
| [DomainParticipant](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) | RTPSParticipant             |
| [DataWriter](../dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter)                | RTPSWriter                  |
| [DataReader](../dds_layer/subscriber/dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader)              | RTPSReader                  |

<a id="how-to-use-the-rtps-layer"></a>

## How to use the RTPS Layer

We will now go over the use of the RTPS Layer like we did with the [DDS Layer](../dds_layer/dds_layer.md#dds-layer) one,
explaining the new features it presents.

We recommend you to look at the example describing how to use the RTPS layer that come with the distribution
while reading this section.
It is located in
[examples/cpp/rtps](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/tree/master/examples/cpp/rtps).

<a id="managing-the-participant"></a>

### Managing the Participant

Creating a [`RTPSParticipant`](../api_reference/rtps/participant/RTPSParticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps15RTPSParticipantE) is done with [`RTPSDomain::createParticipant()`](../api_reference/rtps/RTPSDomain.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps10RTPSDomain17createParticipantENSt8uint32_tERK25RTPSParticipantAttributesP23RTPSParticipantListener).
[`RTPSParticipantAttributes`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/RTPSParticipantAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25RTPSParticipantAttributesE) structure is used to configure the `RTPSParticipant` upon creation.

```c++
RTPSParticipantAttributes participant_attr;
participant_attr.setName("participant");
RTPSParticipant* participant = RTPSDomain::createParticipant(0, participant_attr);
```

<a id="managing-the-writers-and-readers"></a>

### Managing the Writers and Readers

As the RTPS standard specifies, [`RTPSWriters`](../api_reference/rtps/writer/RTPSWriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps10RTPSWriterE) and [`RTPSReaders`](../api_reference/rtps/reader/RTPSReader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps10RTPSReaderE) are always associated
with a [`History`](../api_reference/rtps/history/History_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps7HistoryE) element.
In the [DDS Layer](../dds_layer/dds_layer.md#dds-layer), its creation and management is hidden,
but in the [RTPS Layer](#rtps-layer), you have full control over its creation and configuration.

Writers are created with [`RTPSDomain::createRTPSWriter()`](../api_reference/rtps/RTPSDomain.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps10RTPSDomain16createRTPSWriterEP15RTPSParticipantR16WriterAttributesP13WriterHistoryP14WriterListener) and configured with a [`WriterAttributes`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/WriterAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps16WriterAttributesE) structure.
They also need a [`WriterHistory`](../api_reference/rtps/history/WriterHistory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps13WriterHistoryE) which is configured with a [`HistoryAttributes`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/HistoryAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17HistoryAttributesE) structure.

```c++
HistoryAttributes history_attr;
WriterHistory* history = new WriterHistory(history_attr);
WriterAttributes writer_attr;
RTPSWriter* writer = RTPSDomain::createRTPSWriter(participant, writer_attr, history);
```

Similar to the creation of Writers, Readers are created with [`RTPSDomain::createRTPSReader()`](../api_reference/rtps/RTPSDomain.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps10RTPSDomain16createRTPSReaderEP15RTPSParticipantR16ReaderAttributesP13ReaderHistoryP14ReaderListener)
and configured with a [`ReaderAttributes`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/ReaderAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps16ReaderAttributesE) structure.
A [`HistoryAttributes`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/HistoryAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17HistoryAttributesE) structure is used to configure the required [`ReaderHistory`](../api_reference/rtps/history/ReaderHistory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps13ReaderHistoryE).
Note that in this case, you can provide a specialization of [`ReaderListener`](../api_reference/rtps/reader/ReaderListener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps14ReaderListenerE) class that implements your
callbacks:

```c++
class MyReaderListener : public ReaderListener
{
    // Callbacks override
};
MyReaderListener listener;
HistoryAttributes history_attr;
ReaderHistory* history = new ReaderHistory(history_attr);
ReaderAttributes reader_attr;
RTPSReader* reader = RTPSDomain::createRTPSReader(participant, reader_attr, history, &listener);
```

<a id="using-the-history-to-send-and-receive-data"></a>

### Using the History to Send and Receive Data

In the RTPS Protocol, Readers and Writers save the data about a topic in their associated Histories.
Each piece of data is represented by a Change, which *eprosima Fast DDS* implements as [`CacheChange_t`](../api_reference/rtps/common/CacheChange/CacheChange_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps13CacheChange_tE).
Changes are always managed by the History.

You can add a new `CacheChange_t` to the History of the Writer to send data.
The procedure is as follows:

1. Request a `CacheChange_t` from the Writer History with `WriterHistory::create_change()`.
   In order to allocate enough memory,
   you need to provide as argument the maximum number of bytes in the payload.
2. Fill the `CacheChange_t` with the data.
3. Add it to the History with [`WriterHistory::add_change()`](../api_reference/rtps/history/WriterHistory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps13WriterHistory10add_changeEP13CacheChange_t).

The Writer will take care of everything to communicate the data to the Readers.

```c++
// Request a change from the history
CacheChange_t* change = history->create_change(255, ALIVE);
// Write serialized data into the change
change->serializedPayload.length = sprintf((char*) change->serializedPayload.data, "My example string %d", 2) + 1;
// Insert change into the history. The Writer takes care of the rest.
history->add_change(change);
```

If your topic data type has several fields, you will have to provide functions to serialize and deserialize
your data in and out of the `CacheChange_t`.
*Fast DDS-Gen* does this for you.

You can receive data from within the `ReaderListener::onNewCacheChangeAdded` callback,
as we did in the [DDS Layer](../dds_layer/dds_layer.md#dds-layer):

1. The callback receives a `CacheChange_t` parameter containing the received data.
2. Process the data within the received `CacheChange_t`.
3. Inform the Reader’s History that the change is not needed anymore.

```c++
class MyReaderListener : public ReaderListener
{
public:

    MyReaderListener()
    {
    }

    ~MyReaderListener()
    {
    }

    void onNewCacheChangeAdded(
            RTPSReader* reader,
            const CacheChange_t* const change)
    {
        // The incoming message is enclosed within the `change` in the function parameters
        printf("%s\n", change->serializedPayload.data);
        // Once done, remove the change
        reader->get_history()->remove_change((CacheChange_t*)change);
    }

};
```

<a id="rtps-layer-builtin-transports"></a>

<a id="managing-the-builtin-transports"></a>

### Managing the Builtin Transports

DDS uses the [Transport Layer](../transport/transport.md#comm-transports-configuration) to allow communication between DDS entities. *eProsima Fast DDS* comes
with five transports already implemented. However, these transports are not always exclusive between them
and in some cases they can be used simultaneously.

You can choose what transports you want to use by disabling the use of builtin transports and manually
adding them (see [TransportConfigQos](../dds_layer/core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#transportconfigqos)) or using the default builtin transports behavior and selecting
one of the configuration options listed below. Each option modifies the kind of transports that will be
instantiated.

| Builtin Transports Options   | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `NONE`                       | No transport will be instantiated. Hence, the user must manually add<br/>the desired  transports. Otherwise, the participant creation will fail.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `DEFAULT`                    | UDPv4 and SHM transports will be instantiated. SHM transport has priority<br/>over the UDPv4  transport. Meaning that SHM will always be used<br/>when possible.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `DEFAULTv6`                  | UDPv6 and SHM transports will be instantiated. SHM transport has priority<br/>over the UDPv6 transport. Meaning that SHM will always be used<br/>when possible.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `SHM`                        | Only a SHM transport will be instantiated.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `UDPv4`                      | Only a UDPv4 transport will be instantiated.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `UDPv6`                      | Only a UDPv6 transport will be instantiated.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `LARGE_DATA`                 | UDPv4, TCPv4, and SHM transports will be instantiated. However, UDP will<br/>only be used  for multicast announcements during the participant<br/>discovery phase (see [Discovery phases](../discovery/discovery.md#disc-phases))  while the participant<br/>liveliness and the application data delivery occurs over TCP or SHM.<br/>This configuration is useful when working with large data.(See<br/>[Large Data mode and Fast DDS over TCP](../use_cases/tcp/tcp_use_case.md#use-case-tcp)). |
```c++
RTPSParticipantAttributes participant_attr;
participant_attr.setup_transports(eprosima::fastdds::rtps::BuiltinTransports::LARGE_DATA);
RTPSParticipant* participant = RTPSDomain::createParticipant(0, participant_attr);
```

The same result can also be obtained using the [`setup_transports()`](../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds20DomainParticipantQos16setup_transportsEN4rtps17BuiltinTransportsERKN4rtps24BuiltinTransportsOptionsE) wrapper
function of the [DomainParticipantQos](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantqos), XML profiles (see [RTPS element type](../xml_configuration/domainparticipant.md#rtps)) or the
`FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS` environment variable (see [FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS](../env_vars/env_vars.md#env-vars-builtin-transports)).

#### NOTE
TCPv4 transport is initialized with the following configuration:

* [`calculate_crc`](../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor13calculate_crcE), [`check_crc`](../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor9check_crcE) and
  [`apply_security`](../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor14apply_securityE) are set to false.
* [`enable_tcp_nodelay`](../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor18enable_tcp_nodelayE) is set to true.
* [`keep_alive_thread`](../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor17keep_alive_threadE) and
  [`accept_thread`](../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor13accept_threadE) use the default configuration.

#### WARNING
To obtain a better performance when working with large data messages it is extremely recommended to use the
builtin transports configuration options to adjust the transport to the specific needs of the application.
Please refer to [Large Data with configuration options](../use_cases/tcp/tcp_large_data_with_options.md#use-case-large-data-options) for more information about how to configure it.

<a id="configuring-readers-and-writers"></a>

## Configuring Readers and Writers

One of the benefits of using the [RTPS Layer](#rtps-layer) is that it provides new configuration possibilities while
maintaining the options from the DDS layer.
For example, you can set a Writer or a Reader as a Reliable or Best-Effort endpoint as previously:

```c++
writer_attr.endpoint.reliabilityKind = BEST_EFFORT;
```

<a id="settingdatadurability"></a>

<a id="setting-the-data-durability-kind"></a>

### Setting the data durability kind

The Durability parameter defines the behavior of the Writer regarding samples already sent when a new Reader matches.
*eProsima Fast DDS* offers three Durability options:

* VOLATILE (default): Messages are discarded as they are sent.
  If a new Reader matches after message *n*, it will start received from message *n+1*.
* TRANSIENT_LOCAL: The Writer saves a record of the last *k* messages it has sent.
  If a new reader matches after message *n*, it will start receiving from message *n-k*
* TRANSIENT: As TRANSIENT_LOCAL, but the record of messages will be saved to persistent storage, so it will be available
  if the writer is destroyed and recreated, or in case of an application crash.

To choose your preferred option:

```c++
writer_attr.endpoint.durabilityKind = TRANSIENT_LOCAL;
```

Because in the [RTPS Layer](#rtps-layer) you have control over the History, in TRANSIENT_LOCAL and TRANSIENT modes the Writer
sends all changes you have not explicitly released from the History.

<a id="configuring-the-history"></a>

## Configuring the History

The History has its own configuration structure, the [`HistoryAttributes`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/HistoryAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17HistoryAttributesE).

<a id="changing-the-maximum-size-of-the-payload"></a>

### Changing the maximum size of the payload

You can choose the maximum size of the Payload that can go into a `CacheChange_t`.
Be sure to choose a size that allows it to hold the biggest possible piece of data:

```c++
history_attr.payloadMaxSize  = 250; // Defaults to 500 bytes
```

<a id="changing-the-size-of-the-history"></a>

### Changing the size of the History

You can specify a maximum amount of changes for the History to hold and an initial amount of allocated changes:

```c++
history_attr.initialReservedCaches = 250; // Defaults to 500
history_attr.maximumReservedCaches = 500; // Defaults to 0 = Unlimited Changes
```

When the initial amount of reserved changes is lower than the maximum, the History will allocate more changes as they
are needed until it reaches the maximum size.

<a id="rtps-layer-custom-payload-pool"></a>

<a id="using-a-custom-payload-pool"></a>

## Using a custom Payload Pool

A *Payload* is defined as the data the user wants to transmit between a Writer and a Reader.
RTPS needs to add some metadata to this Payload in order to manage the communication between the endpoints.
Therefore, this Payload is encapsulated inside the `SerializedPayload_t` field
of the `CacheChange_t`,
while the rest of the fields of the `CacheChange_t` provide the required metadata.

[`WriterHistory`](../api_reference/rtps/history/WriterHistory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps13WriterHistoryE) and [`ReaderHistory`](../api_reference/rtps/history/ReaderHistory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps13ReaderHistoryE) provide an interface for the user to interact with these changes:
Changes to be transmitted by the Writer are added to its WriterHistory,
and changes already processed on the Reader can be removed from the ReaderHistory.
In this sense, the History acts as a buffer for changes that are not fully processed yet.

During a normal execution, new changes are added to the History and old ones are removed from it.
In order to manage the lifecycle of the Payloads contained in these changes,
Readers and Writers use a pool object,
an implementation of the [`IPayloadPool`](../api_reference/rtps/history/IPayloadPool.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPoolE) interface.
Different pool implementations allow for different optimizations.
For example, Payloads of different size could be retrieved from different preallocated memory chunks.

Writers and Readers can automatically select a default Payload pool implementation that best suits
the configuration given in [`HistoryAttributes`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/HistoryAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17HistoryAttributesE).
However, a custom Payload pool can be given to [`RTPSDomain::createRTPSWriter()`](../api_reference/rtps/RTPSDomain.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps10RTPSDomain16createRTPSWriterEP15RTPSParticipantR16WriterAttributesP13WriterHistoryP14WriterListener) and
[`RTPSDomain::createRTPSReader()`](../api_reference/rtps/RTPSDomain.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps10RTPSDomain16createRTPSReaderEP15RTPSParticipantR16ReaderAttributesP13ReaderHistoryP14ReaderListener) functions.
Writers and Readers will use the provided pool when a new `CacheChange_t` is requested
or released.

<a id="rtps-layer-ipayload-pool-interface"></a>

<a id="ipayloadpool-interface"></a>

### IPayloadPool interface

* [`IPayloadPool::get_payload`](../api_reference/rtps/history/IPayloadPool.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPool11get_payloadENSt8uint32_tER19SerializedPayload_t) overload with size parameter:

  Ties an empty Payload of the requested size to a `CacheChange_t` instance.
  The Payload can then be filled with the required data.
* [`IPayloadPool::get_payload`](../api_reference/rtps/history/IPayloadPool.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPool11get_payloadENSt8uint32_tER19SerializedPayload_t) overload with SerializadPayload parameter:

  Copies the given Payload data to a new Payload from the pool.
  Each `SerializedPayload_t` contains a pointer to the pool that allocated its data.
  This allows certain certain optimizations, like sharing the Payload if the original one comes from this same pool,
  therefore avoiding the copy operation.
* [`IPayloadPool::release_payload`](../api_reference/rtps/history/IPayloadPool.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPool15release_payloadER19SerializedPayload_t):

  Returns the Payload tied to a `CacheChange_t` to the pool, and breaks the tie.

#### IMPORTANT
When implementing a custom Payload pool, make sure that the allocated Payloads
fulfill the requirements of standard RTPS serialization.
Specifically, the Payloads must be large enough to accommodate the serialized user data plus the 4 octets
of the SerializedPayloadHeader as specified in section 10.2 of the [RTPS standard](https://www.omg.org/spec/DDSI-RTPS/2.2).

For example, if we know the upper bound of the serialized user data,
we may consider implementing a pool that always allocates Payloads of a fixed size,
large enough to hold any of this data.
If the serialized user data has at most N octets,
then the allocated Payloads must have at least N+4 octets.

Note that the size requested to [`IPayloadPool::get_payload`](../api_reference/rtps/history/IPayloadPool.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPool11get_payloadENSt8uint32_tER19SerializedPayload_t) already considers this 4 octet header.

<a id="default-payload-pool-implementation"></a>

### Default Payload pool implementation

If no custom Payload pool is provided to the Writer or Reader, *Fast DDS* will automatically use the
default implementation that best matches the [`memoryPolicy`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/HistoryAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17HistoryAttributes12memoryPolicyE) configuration of the History.

**PREALLOCATED_MEMORY_MODE**

All payloads will have a data buffer of fixed size,
equal to the value of [`payloadMaxSize`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/HistoryAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17HistoryAttributes14payloadMaxSizeE),
regardless of the size requested to [`IPayloadPool::get_payload`](../api_reference/rtps/history/IPayloadPool.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps12IPayloadPool11get_payloadENSt8uint32_tER19SerializedPayload_t).
Released Payloads can be reused for another `CacheChange_t`.
This reduces memory allocation operations at the cost of higher memory usage.

During the initialization of the History, [`initialReservedCaches`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/HistoryAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17HistoryAttributes21initialReservedCachesE)
Payloads are preallocated for the initially allocated `CacheChange_t`.

**PREALLOCATED_WITH_REALLOC_MEMORY_MODE**

Payloads are guaranteed to have a data buffer at least as large as the
maximum between the requested size and [`payloadMaxSize`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/HistoryAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17HistoryAttributes14payloadMaxSizeE).
Released Payloads can be reused for another `CacheChange_t`.
If there is at least one free Payload with a buffer size equal or larger to the requested one,
no memory allocation is done.

During the initialization of the History, [`initialReservedCaches`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/HistoryAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17HistoryAttributes21initialReservedCachesE)
Payloads are preallocated for the initially allocated `CacheChange_t`.

**DYNAMIC_RESERVE_MEMORY_MODE**

Every time a Payload is requested, a new one is allocated in memory with the appropriate size.
[`payloadMaxSize`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/HistoryAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17HistoryAttributes14payloadMaxSizeE) is ignored.
The memory of released Payloads is always deallocated, so there are never free Payloads in the pool.
This reduces memory usage at the cost of frequent memory allocations.

No preallocation of Payloads is done in the initialization of the History,

**DYNAMIC_REUSABLE_MEMORY_MODE**

Payloads are guaranteed to have a data buffer at least as large as the requested size.
[`payloadMaxSize`](../api_reference/rtps/attributes/HistoryAttributes.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17HistoryAttributes14payloadMaxSizeE) is ignored.

Released Payloads can be reused for another `CacheChange_t`.
If there is at least one free Payload with a buffer size equal or larger to the requested one,
no memory allocation is done.

<a id="rtps-layer-payload-pool-example"></a>

<a id="example-using-a-custom-payload-pool"></a>

### Example using a custom Payload pool

```c++
// A simple payload pool that reserves and frees memory each time
class CustomPayloadPool : public IPayloadPool
{
    bool get_payload(
            uint32_t size,
            SerializedPayload_t& payload) override
    {
        // Reserve new memory for the payload buffer
        octet* payload_buff = new octet[size];

        // Assign the payload buffer to the CacheChange and update sizes
        payload.data = payload_buff;
        payload.length = size;
        payload.max_size = size;

        // Tell the CacheChange who needs to release its payload
        payload.payload_owner = this;

        return true;
    }

    bool get_payload(
            const SerializedPayload_t& data,
            SerializedPayload_t& payload)
    {
        // Reserve new memory for the payload buffer
        octet* payload_buff = new octet[data.length];

        // Copy the data
        memcpy(payload_buff, data.data, data.length);

        // Tell the CacheChange who needs to release its payload
        payload.payload_owner = this;

        // Assign the payload buffer to the CacheChange and update sizes
        payload.data = payload_buff;
        payload.length = data.length;
        payload.max_size = data.length;

        return true;
    }

    bool release_payload(
            SerializedPayload_t& payload) override
    {
        // Ensure precondition
        if (this != payload.payload_owner)
        {
            std::cerr << "Trying to release a payload buffer allocated by a different PayloadPool." << std::endl;
            return false;
        }

        // Dealloc the buffer of the payload
        delete[] payload.data;

        // Reset sizes and pointers
        payload.data = nullptr;
        payload.length = 0;
        payload.max_size = 0;

        // Reset the owner of the payload
        payload.payload_owner = nullptr;

        return true;
    }

};

std::shared_ptr<CustomPayloadPool> payload_pool = std::make_shared<CustomPayloadPool>();

// A writer using the custom payload pool
HistoryAttributes writer_history_attr;
WriterHistory* writer_history = new WriterHistory(writer_history_attr, payload_pool);
WriterAttributes writer_attr;
RTPSWriter* writer = RTPSDomain::createRTPSWriter(participant, writer_attr, writer_history);

// A reader using the same instance of the custom payload pool
HistoryAttributes reader_history_attr;
ReaderHistory* reader_history = new ReaderHistory(reader_history_attr);
ReaderAttributes reader_attr;
RTPSReader* reader = RTPSDomain::createRTPSReader(participant, reader_attr, payload_pool, reader_history);

// Write and Read operations work as usual, but take the Payloads from the pool.
// Requesting a change to the Writer will provide one with an empty Payload taken from the pool
CacheChange_t* change = writer_history->create_change(255, ALIVE);

// Write serialized data into the change and add it to the history
change->serializedPayload.length = sprintf((char*) change->serializedPayload.data, "My example string %d", 2) + 1;
writer_history->add_change(change);
```

<a id="discovery"></a>

<a id="id1"></a>

# Discovery

Fast DDS, as a Data Distribution Service ([DDS](https://www.omg.org/spec/DDS/1.4)) implementation, provides discovery
mechanisms that allow for automatically finding and matching [DataWriters](../dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter) and [DataReaders](../dds_layer/subscriber/dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader) across [DomainParticipants](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant)
so they can start sharing data.
This discovery is performed, for all the mechanisms, in two phases.

<a id="disc-phases"></a>

<a id="discovery-phases"></a>

## Discovery phases

1. **Participant Discovery Phase (PDP)**:
   During this phase the [`DomainParticipants`](../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipantE) acknowledge each other’s existence.
   To do that, each DomainParticipant sends periodic announcement messages, which specify, among other things, unicast
   addresses (IP and port) where the DomainParticipant is listening for incoming meta and user data traffic.
   Two given DomainParticipants will match when they exist in the same DDS Domain.
   By default, the announcement messages are sent using well-known multicast addresses and ports (calculated using the
   `DomainId`).
   Furthermore, it is possible to specify a list of addresses to send
   announcements using unicast (see in [Initial peers](simple.md#simple-initial-peers)).
   Moreover, it is also possible to configure the periodicity of such announcements (see
   [Discovery Configuration](../xml_configuration/domainparticipant.md#dconf)).
2. **Endpoint Discovery Phase (EDP)**:
   During this phase, the [`DataWriters`](../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriterE) and [`DataReaders`](../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataReaderE) acknowledge each other.
   To do that, the DomainParticipants share information about their DataWriters and DataReaders with each other,
   using the communication channels established during the PDP.
   This information contains, among other things, the [`Topic`](../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/topic_class.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds5TopicE) and data type (see [Topic](../dds_layer/topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic)).
   For two endpoints to match, their topic and data type must coincide.
   Once DataWriter and DataReader have matched, they are ready for sending/receiving user data traffic.

#### IMPORTANT
It is possible to use the PDP phase to transmit information about the host, user, and process (physical information)
in which the [`DomainParticipant`](../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipantE) is running.
Please refer to [Physical Data in Discovery Information](../property_policies/non_consolidated_qos.md#property-policies-physical-data) for more information about how to configure the transmitted
physical data.

<a id="disc-mechanisms"></a>

<a id="discovery-mechanisms"></a>

## Discovery mechanisms

Fast DDS provides the following discovery mechanisms:

- [Simple Discovery](simple.md#simple-disc-settings): This is the default mechanism.
  It upholds the [RTPS standard](https://www.omg.org/spec/DDSI-RTPS/2.2/PDF) for both PDP and EDP, and therefore
  provides compatibility with any other DDS and RTPS implementations.
- [Static Discovery](static.md#static-edp): This mechanisms uses the Simple Participant Discovery Protocol (SPDP) for the
  PDP phase (as specified by the [RTPS standard](https://www.omg.org/spec/DDSI-RTPS/2.2/PDF)), but allows for skipping
  the Simple Endpoint Discovery Protocol (SEDP) phase when all the DataWriters’ and DataReaders’ IPs and ports,
  data types, and Topics are known beforehand.
- [Discovery Server](discovery_server.md#discovery-server): This discovery mechanism uses a centralized discovery architecture,
  where a DomainParticipant, referred as Server, acts as a hub for meta traffic discovery.
- [PDP Relay](pdp_relay.md#pdp-relay) **[Pro]**: This discovery mechanism keeps the DomainParticipants using
  Simple Discovery, and uses a dedicated DomainParticipant that only re-distributes the participant
  announcements it receives, so that they can discover each other without multicast.
- **Manual Discovery**: This mechanism is only compatible with the RTPS layer.
  It disables the PDP, letting the user to manually match and unmatch [`RTPSParticipants`](../api_reference/rtps/participant/RTPSParticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps15RTPSParticipantE), [`RTPSReaders`](../api_reference/rtps/reader/RTPSReader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps10RTPSReaderE), and
  [`RTPSWriters`](../api_reference/rtps/writer/RTPSWriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps10RTPSWriterE) using whatever external meta-information channel of its choice.
  Therefore, the user must access the RTPSParticipant implemented by the DomainParticipant and directly match the
  RTPS Entities.
