<a id="domainparticipant-discovery-callbacks"></a>

<a id="domainparticipantlistener-discovery-callbacks"></a>

# DomainParticipantListener Discovery Callbacks

As stated in [DomainParticipantListener](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipantListener/domainParticipantListener.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantlistener), the [`DomainParticipantListener`](../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds25DomainParticipantListenerE) is an abstract class
defining the callbacks that will be triggered in response to state changes on the DomainParticipant.
Fast DDS defines three callbacks attached to events that may occur during discovery:
[`on_participant_discovery()`](../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds25DomainParticipantListener24on_participant_discoveryEP17DomainParticipantN7fastdds4rtps26ParticipantDiscoveryStatusERK27ParticipantBuiltinTopicDataRb),
[`on_data_reader_discovery()`](../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds25DomainParticipantListener24on_data_reader_discoveryEP17DomainParticipantN4rtps21ReaderDiscoveryStatusERK28SubscriptionBuiltinTopicDataRb),
[`on_data_writer_discovery()`](../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantlistener.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds25DomainParticipantListener24on_data_writer_discoveryEP17DomainParticipantN4rtps21WriterDiscoveryStatusERK27PublicationBuiltinTopicDataRb).
Further information about the DomainParticipantListener is provided in the [DomainParticipantListener](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipantListener/domainParticipantListener.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantlistener)
section.
The following is an example of the implementation of DomainParticipantListener discovery callbacks.

```c++
class DiscoveryDomainParticipantListener : public DomainParticipantListener
{
    /* Custom Callback on_participant_discovery */
    void on_participant_discovery(
            DomainParticipant* participant,
            eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ParticipantDiscoveryStatus status,
            const ParticipantBuiltinTopicData& info,
            bool& should_be_ignored) override
    {
        should_be_ignored = false;
        static_cast<void>(participant);
        switch (status){
            case eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ParticipantDiscoveryStatus::DISCOVERED_PARTICIPANT:
            {
                /* Process the case when a new DomainParticipant was found in the domain */
                std::cout << "New DomainParticipant '" << info.participant_name
                          << "' with ID '" << info.guid.entityId << "' and GuidPrefix '"
                          << info.guid.guidPrefix << "' discovered." << std::endl;
                /* The following line can be substituted to evaluate whether the discovered participant should be ignored */
                bool ignoring_condition = false;
                if (ignoring_condition)
                {
                    should_be_ignored = true;     // Request the ignoring of the discovered participant
                }
            }
            break;
            case eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ParticipantDiscoveryStatus::CHANGED_QOS_PARTICIPANT:
                /* Process the case when a DomainParticipant changed its QOS */
                break;
            case eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ParticipantDiscoveryStatus::REMOVED_PARTICIPANT:
                /* Process the case when a DomainParticipant was removed from the domain */
                std::cout << "DomainParticipant '" << info.participant_name
                          << "' with ID '" << info.guid.entityId << "' and GuidPrefix '"
                          << info.guid.guidPrefix << "' left the domain." << std::endl;
                break;
        }
    }

    /* Custom Callback on_data_reader_discovery */
    void on_data_reader_discovery(
            DomainParticipant* participant,
            eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ReaderDiscoveryStatus reason,
            const eprosima::fastdds::rtps::SubscriptionBuiltinTopicData& info,
            bool& should_be_ignored) override
    {
        should_be_ignored = false;
        static_cast<void>(participant);
        switch (reason){
            case eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ReaderDiscoveryStatus::DISCOVERED_READER:
            {
                /* Process the case when a new datareader was found in the domain */
                std::cout << "New DataReader subscribed to topic '" << info.topic_name
                          << "' of type '" << info.type_name << "' discovered";
                /* The following line can be substituted to evaluate whether the discovered datareader should be ignored */
                bool ignoring_condition = false;
                if (ignoring_condition)
                {
                    should_be_ignored = true;     // Request the ignoring of the discovered datareader
                }
            }
            break;
            case eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ReaderDiscoveryStatus::CHANGED_QOS_READER:
                /* Process the case when a datareader changed its QOS */
                break;
            case eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ReaderDiscoveryStatus::REMOVED_READER:
                /* Process the case when a datareader was removed from the domain */
                std::cout << "DataReader subscribed to topic '" << info.topic_name
                          << "' of type '" << info.type_name << "' left the domain.";
                break;
        }
    }

    /* Custom Callback on_data_writer_discovery */
    void on_data_writer_discovery(
            DomainParticipant* participant,
            eprosima::fastdds::rtps::WriterDiscoveryStatus reason,
            const eprosima::fastdds::dds::PublicationBuiltinTopicData& info,
            bool& should_be_ignored) override
    {
        should_be_ignored = false;
        static_cast<void>(participant);
        switch (reason){
            case eprosima::fastdds::rtps::WriterDiscoveryStatus::DISCOVERED_WRITER:
            {
                /* Process the case when a new datawriter was found in the domain */
                std::cout << "New DataWriter publishing under topic '" << info.topic_name
                          << "' of type '" << info.type_name << "' discovered";
                /* The following line can be substituted to evaluate whether the discovered datawriter should be ignored */
                bool ignoring_condition = false;
                if (ignoring_condition)
                {
                    should_be_ignored = true;     // Request the ignoring of the discovered datawriter
                }
            }
            break;
            case eprosima::fastdds::rtps::WriterDiscoveryStatus::CHANGED_QOS_WRITER:
                /* Process the case when a datawriter changed its QOS */
                break;
            case eprosima::fastdds::rtps::WriterDiscoveryStatus::REMOVED_WRITER:
                /* Process the case when a datawriter was removed from the domain */
                std::cout << "DataWriter publishing under topic '" << info.topic_name
                          << "' of type '" << info.type_name << "' left the domain.";
                break;
        }
    }

};
```

To use the previously implemented discovery callbacks in `DiscoveryDomainParticipantListener` class, which
inherits from the DomainParticipantListener, an object of this class is created and registered as a listener
of the DomainParticipant.

```c++
// Create the participant QoS and configure values
DomainParticipantQos pqos;

// Create a custom user DomainParticipantListener
DiscoveryDomainParticipantListener* plistener = new DiscoveryDomainParticipantListener();
// Pass the listener on DomainParticipant creation.
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(
    0, pqos, plistener);
```

#### IMPORTANT
Read more about callbacks and its hierarchy [here](../dds_layer/core/entity/entity.md#dds-layer-core-entity-commonchars-listener)

<a id="comm-transports-configuration"></a>

<a id="transport-layer"></a>

# Transport Layer

The transport layer provides communication services between DDS entities,
being responsible of actually sending and receiving messages over a physical transport.
The DDS layer uses this service for both user data and discovery traffic communication.
However, the DDS layer itself is transport independent,
it defines a transport API and can run over any transport plugin that implements this API.
This way, it is not restricted to a specific transport, and applications
can choose the one that best suits their requirements, or create their own.

*eProsima Fast DDS* comes with five transports already implemented:

- **UDPv4**: UDP Datagram communication over IPv4.
  This transport is created by default on a new [DomainParticipant](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant)
  if no specific transport configuration is given
  (see [UDP Transport](udp/udp.md#transport-udp-udp)).
- **UDPv6**: UDP Datagram communication over IPv6
  (see [UDP Transport](udp/udp.md#transport-udp-udp)).
- **TCPv4**: TCP communication over IPv4
  (see [TCP Transport](tcp/tcp.md#transport-tcp-tcp)).
- **TCPv6**: TCP communication over IPv6
  (see [TCP Transport](tcp/tcp.md#transport-tcp-tcp)).
- **SHM**: Shared memory communication among entities running on the same host.
  This transport is created by default on a new [DomainParticipant](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant)
  if no specific transport configuration is given
  (see [Shared Memory Transport](shared_memory/shared_memory.md#transport-sharedmemory-sharedmemory)).

Although it is not part of the transport module,
[intraprocess data delivery](intraprocess.md#intraprocess-delivery) and [data sharing delivery](datasharing.md#datasharing-delivery)
are also available to send messages between entities on some settings.
The figure below shows a comparison between the different transports available in *Fast DDS*.

<a id="transport-transportapi"></a>

<a id="transport-api"></a>

# Transport API

The following diagram presents the classes defined on the transport API of *eProsima Fast DDS*.
It shows the abstract API interfaces, and the classes required to implement a transport.

```plantuml
hide empty members
interface TransportDescriptorInterface
{
    +uint32_t maxMessageSize
    +uint32_t maxInitialPeersRange
}
interface TransportInterface
{
    #int32_t transport_kind_
}
class Locator
{
    +int32_t kind
    +uint32_t port
    +octet[16] address
}
TransportDescriptorInterface <|-- CustomTransportDescriptor
TransportInterface <|-- CustomTransport
CustomTransport <--right CustomTransportDescriptor : create
Locator <--right TransportInterface
```

*Transport API diagram*

<a id="transport-transportapi-transportdescriptor"></a>

<a id="transportdescriptorinterface"></a>

## TransportDescriptorInterface

Any class that implements the [`TransportDescriptorInterface`](../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_descriptor_interface.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28TransportDescriptorInterfaceE) is known as a `TransportDescriptor`.
It acts as a *builder* for a given transport, meaning that is allows to configure the transport,
and then a new [Transport](#transport-transportapi-transport) can be built according to this configuration
using its [`create_transport`](../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_descriptor_interface.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28TransportDescriptorInterface16create_transportEv) factory member function.

<a id="data-members"></a>

### Data members

The TransportDescriptorInterface defines the following data members:

| Member                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Data type   | Description                                              |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| [`maxMessageSize`](../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_descriptor_interface.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28TransportDescriptorInterface14maxMessageSizeE)             | `uint32_t`  | Maximum size of a single message in the transport.       |
| [`maxInitialPeersRange`](../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_descriptor_interface.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28TransportDescriptorInterface20maxInitialPeersRangeE) | `uint32_t`  | Number of channels opened with each initial remote peer. |

Any implementation of [TransportDescriptorInterface](#transport-transportapi-transportdescriptor) should add as many
data members as required to full configure the transport it describes.

<a id="transport-transportapi-transport"></a>

<a id="transportinterface"></a>

## TransportInterface

A `Transport` is any class that implements the [`TransportInterface`](../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_interface.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps18TransportInterfaceE).
It is the object that actually performs the message distribution over a physical transport.

Each `Transport` class defines its own [`kind`](../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_interface.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds4rtps18TransportInterface4kindEv), a unique identifier that is used to
check the compatibility of a [Locator](#transport-transportapi-locator) with a Transport, i.e.,
determine whether a Locator refers to a Transport or not.

Applications do not create the `Transport` instance themselves.
Instead, applications use a `TransportDescriptor` instance to configure the desired transport, and add
this configured instance to the list of user-defined transports of the [DomainParticipant](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant).
The DomainParticipant will use the factory function on the `TransportDescriptor`
to create the `Transport` when required.

```c++
DomainParticipantQos qos;

// Create a descriptor for the new transport.
auto udp_transport = std::make_shared<UDPv4TransportDescriptor>();
udp_transport->sendBufferSize = 9216;
udp_transport->receiveBufferSize = 9216;
udp_transport->non_blocking_send = true;

// [OPTIONAL] ThreadSettings configuration
udp_transport->default_reception_threads(eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ThreadSettings{2, 2, 2, 2});
udp_transport->set_thread_config_for_port(12345, eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ThreadSettings{3, 3, 3, 3});

// Link the Transport Layer to the Participant.
qos.transport().user_transports.push_back(udp_transport);

// Avoid using the default transport
qos.transport().use_builtin_transports = false;
```

<a id="id1"></a>

### Data members

The TransportInterface defines the following data members:

<a id="transport-transportapi-kind"></a>

| Member            | Data type   | Description                              |
|-------------------|-------------|------------------------------------------|
| `transport_kind_` | `int32_t`   | Unique identifier of the transport type. |

#### NOTE
`transport_kind_` is a protected data member for internal use.
It cannot be accessed nor modified from the public API.
However, users that are implementing a custom Transport need to fill it with a unique constant value
in the new implementation.

Currently the following identifiers are used in *Fast DDS*:

| Identifier                                                                                         |   Value | Transport type                                                                                 |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`LOCATOR_KIND_RESERVED`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/defines.md#c.LOCATOR_KIND_RESERVED) |       0 | None. Reserved value for internal use.                                                         |
| [`LOCATOR_KIND_UDPv4`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/defines.md#c.LOCATOR_KIND_UDPv4)       |       1 | [UDP Transport](udp/udp.md#transport-udp-udp) over IPv4.                                       |
| [`LOCATOR_KIND_UDPv6`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/defines.md#c.LOCATOR_KIND_UDPv6)       |       2 | [UDP Transport](udp/udp.md#transport-udp-udp) over IPv6.                                       |
| [`LOCATOR_KIND_TCPv4`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/defines.md#c.LOCATOR_KIND_TCPv4)       |       4 | [TCP Transport](tcp/tcp.md#transport-tcp-tcp) over IPv4.                                       |
| [`LOCATOR_KIND_TCPv6`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/defines.md#c.LOCATOR_KIND_TCPv6)       |       8 | [TCP Transport](tcp/tcp.md#transport-tcp-tcp) over IPv6.                                       |
| [`LOCATOR_KIND_SHM`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/defines.md#c.LOCATOR_KIND_SHM)           |      16 | [Shared Memory Transport](shared_memory/shared_memory.md#transport-sharedmemory-sharedmemory). |

<a id="transport-transportapi-locator"></a>

<a id="locator"></a>

## Locator

A [`Locator_t`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/Locator_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps9Locator_tE) uniquely identifies a communication channel with a remote peer for a particular transport.
For example, on UDP transports, the Locator will contain the information of the IP address and port
of the remote peer.

The Locator class is not abstract, and no specializations are implemented for each transport type.
Instead, transports should map the data members of the Locator class to their own channel identification
concepts.
For example, on [Shared Memory Transport](shared_memory/shared_memory.md#transport-sharedmemory-sharedmemory) the [`address`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/Locator_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps9Locator_t7addressE) contains a unique ID
for the local host, and the [`port`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/Locator_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps9Locator_t4portE) represents the shared ring buffer used to communicate buffer
descriptors.

Please refer to [Listening Locators](listening_locators.md#listening-locators) for more information about how to configure
DomainParticipant to listen to incoming traffic.

<a id="id2"></a>

### Data members

The Locator defines the following data members:

| Member                                                                                                          | Data type   | Description                              |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|------------------------------------------|
| [`kind`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/Locator_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps9Locator_t4kindE)       | `int32_t`   | Unique identifier of the transport type. |
| [`port`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/Locator_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps9Locator_t4portE)       | `uint32_t`  | The channel *port*.                      |
| [`address`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/Locator_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps9Locator_t7addressE) | `octet[16]` | The channel *address*.                   |

In TCP, the port of the locator is divided into a physical and a logical port.

* The *physical port* is the port used by the network device, the real port that the operating system understands.
  It is stored in the two least significant bytes of the member [`port`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/Locator_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps9Locator_t4portE).
* The *logical port* is the RTPS port.
  It is used by the RTPS protocol to distinguish different entities.
  It is stored in the two most significant bytes of the member [`port`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/Locator_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps9Locator_t4portE).

In TCP, this distinction allows for several DDS applications using different RTPS ports (*logical ports*) to share the
same *physical port*, thus only requiring for a single port to be opened for all communications.
In UDP there is only the *physical port*, which is also the RTPS port, and is stored in the two least significant bytes
of the member [`port`](../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/Locator_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps9Locator_t4portE).

The locator address, represented in 16 bytes, is managed differently depending on whether the protocol used is IPv4 or
IPv6.

* The IPv6 address uses the 16 available bytes to represent the address, which can be a global unicast, a unique
  local, or a link-local address.
  **[Pro]** The locator does not carry the zone index of link-local addresses, as it only has meaning on the local host.
  The transport selects it when needed (see [TCPv6 Addresses and Interfaces](tcp/tcp.md#transport-tcp-ipv6-addresses)).
* The IPv4 address splits those 16 bytes in the following three sections, ordered from least to greatest significance:
  - 4 bytes LAN IP: Local subnet identification (UDP and TCP).
  - 4 bytes WAN IP: Public IP (TCP only).
  - 8 bytes unused.

```idl
                        Locator IPv4 address
+--------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------+
| Unused | WAN address (62.128.41.210) | LAN address (192.168.0.113) |
+--------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------+
 8 bytes       (TCP only) 4 bytes                 4 bytes


                        Locator IPv6 address
+--------------------------------------------------------------------+
|          Address (2001:0000:130F:0000:0000:09C0:876A:130B)         |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------+
                              16 bytes
```

Check how to manipulate the WAN address in the [TCP IPv4 transport descriptor api](../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcpv4_transport_descriptor.md#api-tcpv4-transport-descriptor)
section.

<a id="transport-transportapi-iplocator"></a>

<a id="configuring-ip-locators-with-iplocator"></a>

### Configuring IP locators with IPLocator

`IPLocator` is an auxiliary static class that offers methods to manipulate IP based locators.
It is convenient when setting up a new [UDP Transport](udp/udp.md#transport-udp-udp) or [TCP Transport](tcp/tcp.md#transport-tcp-tcp),
as it simplifies setting IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, or manipulating ports.

For example, normally users configure the physical port and do not need to worry about logical ports.
However, `IPLocator` allows to manage them if needed.

```c++
// We will configure a TCP locator with IPLocator
Locator_t locator;

// Get & set the physical port
uint16_t physical_port = IPLocator::getPhysicalPort(locator);
IPLocator::setPhysicalPort(locator, 5555);

// On TCP locators, we can get & set the logical port
uint16_t logical_port = IPLocator::getLogicalPort(locator);
IPLocator::setLogicalPort(locator, 7400);

// Set WAN address
IPLocator::setWan(locator, "80.88.75.55");
```

*Fast DDS* also allows to specify locator addresses using names.
When an address is specified by a name, *Fast DDS* will query the known hosts and available DNS servers to try to
resolve the IP address.
This address will in turn be used to create the listening locator in the case of *server*, or as the address of the
remote *server* in the case of *clients* (and *servers* that connect to other *servers*).

### C++

```c++
Locator_t locator;
auto response = eprosima::fastdds::rtps::IPLocator::resolveNameDNS("localhost");
// Get the first returned IPv4
if (response.first.size() > 0)
{
    IPLocator::setIPv4(locator, response.first.begin()->data());
    locator.port = 11811;
}
// Use the locator to create server or client
```

### XML

```xml
<locator>
    <udpv4>
        <port>11811</port>
        <address>localhost</address>
    </udpv4>
</locator>
```

#### NOTE
**[Pro]** For TCPv6 addresses, the zone index suffix (e.g. `fe80::1%eth0`) is accepted but ignored.
For more information, see [TCPv6 Addresses and Interfaces](tcp/tcp.md#transport-tcp-ipv6-addresses).

<a id="transport-transportapi-chaining"></a>

<a id="chaining-of-transports"></a>

## Chaining of transports

There are use cases where the user needs to pre-process out-coming information before being sent to network and also
the incoming information after being received.
*Transport API* offers two interfaces for implementing this kind of functionality: [`ChainingTransportDescriptor`](../api_reference/transport/chaining_transport/chaining_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps27ChainingTransportDescriptorE)
and [`ChainingTransport`](../api_reference/transport/chaining_transport/chaining_transport.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17ChainingTransportE).

```plantuml
hide empty members
interface TransportDescriptorInterface
{
    +uint32_t maxMessageSize
    +uint32_t maxInitialPeersRange
}
interface TransportInterface
{
    #int32_t transport_kind_
}
interface ChainingTransportDescriptor
{
    +std::shared_ptr<TransportDescriptorInterface> low_level_descriptor
}
interface ChainingTransport
{
    #std::unique_ptr<TransportInterface> low_level_transport_
    {abstract} bool send(...)
    {abstract} void receive(...)
}
TransportDescriptorInterface <|-- ChainingTransportDescriptor
TransportInterface <|-- ChainingTransport
ChainingTransportDescriptor <|-- CustomChainingTransportDescriptor
ChainingTransport <|-- CustomChainingTransport
CustomChainingTransport <-- CustomChainingTransportDescriptor : create
CustomChainingTransportDescriptor "1" *-- "1" TransportDescriptorInterface : contains
CustomChainingTransport "1" *-- "1" TransportInterface : contains
CustomChainingTransportDescriptor --- UDPv4TransportDescriptor : example
CustomChainingTransport ---  UDPv4Transport : example
```

These extensions allow to implement a new Transport which depends on another one (called here as
`low_level_transport_`).
The user can override the [`send()`](../api_reference/transport/chaining_transport/chaining_transport.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17ChainingTransport4sendEPN7fastdds4rtps14SenderResourceERKNSt6vectorI13NetworkBufferEENSt8uint32_tEPN7fastdds4rtps16LocatorsIteratorEPN7fastdds4rtps16LocatorsIteratorERKNSt6chrono12steady_clock10time_pointE) function, pre-processing the out-coming buffer before calling
the associated `low_level_transport_`.
Also, when a incoming buffer arrives to the `low_level_transport_`, this one calls the overridden
[`receive()`](../api_reference/transport/chaining_transport/chaining_transport.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17ChainingTransport7receiveEP26TransportReceiverInterfacePKN7fastdds4rtps5octetENSt8uint32_tERKN7fastdds4rtps9Locator_tERKN7fastdds4rtps9Locator_tE) function to allow to pre-process the buffer.

<a id="transport-transportapi-chaining-descriptor"></a>

<a id="chainingtransportdescriptor"></a>

### ChainingTransportDescriptor

Implementing [`ChainingTransportDescriptor`](../api_reference/transport/chaining_transport/chaining_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps27ChainingTransportDescriptorE) allows to configure the new Transport and set the
`low_level_transport_` on which it depends.
The associated `low_level_transport_` can be any transport which inherits from
[`TransportInterface`](../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_interface.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps18TransportInterfaceE) (including another [`ChainingTransport`](../api_reference/transport/chaining_transport/chaining_transport.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17ChainingTransportE)).

The [`ChainingTransportDescriptor`](../api_reference/transport/chaining_transport/chaining_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps27ChainingTransportDescriptorE) defines the following data members:

| Member                                                                                                                                                                                     | Data type                                       | Description                                         |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| [`low_level_descriptor`](../api_reference/transport/chaining_transport/chaining_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps27ChainingTransportDescriptor20low_level_descriptorE) | `std::shared_ptr<TransportDescriptorInterface>` | Transport descriptor of the `low_level_transport_`. |

User has to specify the `low_level_transport_` in the definition of its new custom transport.

```c++
DomainParticipantQos qos;

auto udp_transport = std::make_shared<UDPv4TransportDescriptor>();

// Create a descriptor for the new transport.
// The low level transport will be a UDPv4Transport.
auto custom_transport = std::make_shared<CustomChainingTransportDescriptor>(udp_transport);

// Link the Transport Layer to the Participant.
qos.transport().user_transports.push_back(custom_transport);

// Avoid using the default transport
qos.transport().use_builtin_transports = false;
```

<a id="chainingtransport"></a>

### ChainingTransport

This interface forces the user to implement [`send()`](../api_reference/transport/chaining_transport/chaining_transport.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17ChainingTransport4sendEPN7fastdds4rtps14SenderResourceERKNSt6vectorI13NetworkBufferEENSt8uint32_tEPN7fastdds4rtps16LocatorsIteratorEPN7fastdds4rtps16LocatorsIteratorERKNSt6chrono12steady_clock10time_pointE) and [`receive()`](../api_reference/transport/chaining_transport/chaining_transport.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps17ChainingTransport7receiveEP26TransportReceiverInterfacePKN7fastdds4rtps5octetENSt8uint32_tERKN7fastdds4rtps9Locator_tERKN7fastdds4rtps9Locator_tE)
functions.
The idea is to pre-process the buffer and after, call to the next level.

```c++
class CustomChainingTransport : public eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ChainingTransport
{

public:

    CustomChainingTransport(
            const CustomChainingTransportDescriptor& descriptor)
        : ChainingTransport(descriptor)
        , descriptor_(descriptor)
    {
    }

    eprosima::fastdds::rtps::TransportDescriptorInterface* get_configuration()
    {
        return &descriptor_;
    }

    bool send(
            eprosima::fastdds::rtps::SenderResource* low_sender_resource,
            const std::vector<eprosima::fastdds::rtps::NetworkBuffer>& buffers,
            uint32_t total_bytes,
            eprosima::fastdds::rtps::LocatorsIterator* destination_locators_begin,
            eprosima::fastdds::rtps::LocatorsIterator* destination_locators_end,
            const std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point& timeout) override
    {
        //
        // Preprocess outcoming buffer.
        //

        // Call low level transport
        return low_sender_resource->send(buffers, total_bytes, destination_locators_begin,
                       destination_locators_end, timeout, 0);
    }

    bool send_w_priority(
            eprosima::fastdds::rtps::SenderResource* low_sender_resource,
            const std::vector<eprosima::fastdds::rtps::NetworkBuffer>& buffers,
            uint32_t total_bytes,
            eprosima::fastdds::rtps::LocatorsIterator* destination_locators_begin,
            eprosima::fastdds::rtps::LocatorsIterator* destination_locators_end,
            const std::chrono::steady_clock::time_point& timeout,
            int32_t transport_priority) override
    {
        //
        // Preprocess outcoming buffer.
        //

        // Call low level transport
        return low_sender_resource->send(buffers, total_bytes, destination_locators_begin,
                       destination_locators_end, timeout, transport_priority);
    }

    void receive(
            eprosima::fastdds::rtps::TransportReceiverInterface* next_receiver,
            const eprosima::fastdds::rtps::octet* receive_buffer,
            uint32_t receive_buffer_size,
            const eprosima::fastdds::rtps::Locator_t& local_locator,
            const eprosima::fastdds::rtps::Locator_t& remote_locator) override
    {
        //
        // Preprocess incoming buffer.
        //

        // Call upper level
        next_receiver->OnDataReceived(receive_buffer, receive_buffer_size, local_locator, remote_locator);
    }

private:

    CustomChainingTransportDescriptor descriptor_;
};
```

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/transport/udp/udp.md -->

<a id="transport-udp-udp"></a>

<a id="udp-transport"></a>

# UDP Transport

UDP is a connectionless transport, where the receiving [DomainParticipant](../../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) must open a UDP port
listening for incoming messages, and the sending DomainParticipant sends messages to this port.

#### WARNING
This documentation assumes the reader has basic knowledge of UDP/IP concepts, since terms like
Time To Live (TTL), socket buffers, and port numbering are not explained in detail.
However, it is possible to configure a basic UDP transport on *Fast DDS* without this knowledge.

<a id="transport-udp-transportdescriptor"></a>

<a id="udptransportdescriptor"></a>

## UDPTransportDescriptor

*eProsima Fast DDS* implements UDP transport for both UDPv4 and UDPv6.
Each of these transports is independent from the other, and has its own [`TransportDescriptorInterface`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_descriptor_interface.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28TransportDescriptorInterfaceE).
However, all their [`TransportDescriptorInterface`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_descriptor_interface.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28TransportDescriptorInterfaceE) data members are common.

The following table describes the common data members for both UDPv4 and UDPv6.

| Member                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Data type                                                                             | Default      | Description                                                                                                                        |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`sendBufferSize`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor14sendBufferSizeE)                                | `uint32_t`                                                                            | 0            | Size of the sending buffer of the socket (octets).                                                                                 |
| [`receiveBufferSize`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor17receiveBufferSizeE)                          | `uint32_t`                                                                            | 0            | Size of the receiving buffer of the socket (octets).                                                                               |
| [`netmask_filter`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor14netmask_filterE)                                | `NetmaskFilterKind`                                                                   | `AUTO`       | See [Netmask filtering](../interfaces.md#netmask-filtering).                                                                       |
| [`allowlist`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor19interface_allowlistE)                                | `vector<pair<string, NetmaskFilterKind>>`                                             | Empty vector | List of allowed interfaces with<br/>netmask filter configuration.<br/>See [Allowlist](../interfaces.md#interfaces-allowlist).      |
| [`blocklist`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor19interface_blocklistE)                                | `vector<string>`                                                                      | Empty vector | List of blocked interfaces.<br/>See [Blocklist](../interfaces.md#interfaces-blocklist).                                            |
| [`interfaceWhiteList`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor18interfaceWhiteListE)                        | `vector<string>`                                                                      | Empty vector | List of allowed interfaces.<br/>See [Interface Whitelist](../whitelist.md#whitelist-interfaces).                                   |
| [`TTL`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor3TTLE)                                                       | `uint8_t`                                                                             | 1            | Time to live, in number of hops.                                                                                                   |
| [`m_output_udp_socket`](../../api_reference/transport/udp_transport/udp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22UDPTransportDescriptor19m_output_udp_socketE)                                           | `uint16_t`                                                                            | 0            | Port number for the outgoing messages.                                                                                             |
| [`non_blocking_send`](../../api_reference/transport/udp_transport/udp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22UDPTransportDescriptor17non_blocking_sendE)                                               | `bool`                                                                                | `false`      | Do not block on send operations (\*).                                                                                              |
| [`default_reception_threads`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/port_based_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28PortBasedTransportDescriptor25default_reception_threadsEv) | [ThreadSettings](../../dds_layer/core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#threadsettingsqos) |              | Default [ThreadSettings](../../dds_layer/core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#threadsettingsqos) for the reception threads.           |
| [`reception_threads`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/port_based_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28PortBasedTransportDescriptor17reception_threadsEv)                 | `std::map<uint32_t, ThreadSettings>`                                                  |              | [ThreadSettings](../../dds_layer/core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#threadsettingsqos) for the reception threads on specific ports. |

#### NOTE
When [`non_blocking_send`](../../api_reference/transport/udp_transport/udp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22UDPTransportDescriptor17non_blocking_sendE) is set to true, send operations will return immediately if the
buffer is full, but no error will be returned to the upper layer.
This means that the application will behave as if the datagram is sent and lost.
This value is specially useful on high-frequency best-effort writers.

When set to `false`, send operations will block until the network buffer has space for the
datagram.
This may hinder performance on high-frequency writers.

<a id="transport-udp-v4transportdescriptor"></a>

<a id="udpv4transportdescriptor"></a>

### UDPv4TransportDescriptor

[`UDPv4TransportDescriptor`](../../api_reference/transport/udp_transport/udpv4_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps24UDPv4TransportDescriptorE) has no additional data members from the common ones described in
[UDPTransportDescriptor](#transport-udp-transportdescriptor).

#### NOTE
The [`kind`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_interface.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds4rtps18TransportInterface4kindEv) value for a [`UDPv4TransportDescriptor`](../../api_reference/transport/udp_transport/udpv4_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps24UDPv4TransportDescriptorE) is given by the value
[`LOCATOR_KIND_UDPv4`](../../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/defines.md#c.LOCATOR_KIND_UDPv4).

<a id="transport-udp-v6transportdescriptor"></a>

<a id="udpv6transportdescriptor"></a>

### UDPv6TransportDescriptor

[`UDPv6TransportDescriptor`](../../api_reference/transport/udp_transport/udpv6_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps24UDPv6TransportDescriptorE) has no additional data members from the common ones described in
[UDPTransportDescriptor](#transport-udp-transportdescriptor).

#### NOTE
The [`kind`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_interface.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds4rtps18TransportInterface4kindEv) value for a [`UDPv6TransportDescriptor`](../../api_reference/transport/udp_transport/udpv6_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps24UDPv6TransportDescriptorE) is given by the value
[`LOCATOR_KIND_UDPv6`](../../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/defines.md#c.LOCATOR_KIND_UDPv6).

<a id="transport-udp-enabling"></a>

<a id="enabling-udp-transport"></a>

## Enabling UDP Transport

*Fast DDS* enables a UDPv4 transport by default.
Nevertheless, the application can enable other UDP transports if needed.
To enable a new UDP transport in a [DomainParticipant](../../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant), first
create an instance of [UDPv4TransportDescriptor](#transport-udp-v4transportdescriptor) (for UDPv4) or
[UDPv6TransportDescriptor](#transport-udp-v6transportdescriptor) (for UDPv6), and add it to the user transport list of the
[DomainParticipant](../../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant).

The examples below show this procedure in both C++ code and XML file.

### C++

```c++
DomainParticipantQos qos;

// Create a descriptor for the new transport.
auto udp_transport = std::make_shared<UDPv4TransportDescriptor>();
udp_transport->sendBufferSize = 9216;
udp_transport->receiveBufferSize = 9216;
udp_transport->non_blocking_send = true;

// [OPTIONAL] ThreadSettings configuration
udp_transport->default_reception_threads(eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ThreadSettings{2, 2, 2, 2});
udp_transport->set_thread_config_for_port(12345, eprosima::fastdds::rtps::ThreadSettings{3, 3, 3, 3});

// Link the Transport Layer to the Participant.
qos.transport().user_transports.push_back(udp_transport);

// Avoid using the default transport
qos.transport().use_builtin_transports = false;
```

### XML

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<dds>
    <profiles xmlns="http://www.eprosima.com">
        <transport_descriptors>
            <transport_descriptor>
                <transport_id>udp_transport</transport_id>
                <type>UDPv4</type>
                <sendBufferSize>9216</sendBufferSize>
                <receiveBufferSize>9216</receiveBufferSize>
                <non_blocking_send>true</non_blocking_send>
                <default_reception_threads>
                    <scheduling_policy>2</scheduling_policy>
                    <priority>2</priority>
                    <affinity>2</affinity>
                    <stack_size>2</stack_size>
                </default_reception_threads>
                <reception_threads>
                    <reception_thread port="12345">
                        <scheduling_policy>3</scheduling_policy>
                        <priority>3</priority>
                        <affinity>3</affinity>
                        <stack_size>3</stack_size>
                    </reception_thread>
                </reception_threads>
            </transport_descriptor>
        </transport_descriptors>

        <participant profile_name="UDPParticipant">
            <rtps>
                <userTransports>
                    <transport_id>udp_transport</transport_id>
                </userTransports>
                <useBuiltinTransports>false</useBuiltinTransports>
            </rtps>
        </participant>
    </profiles>
<dds>
```

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/transport/tcp/tcp.md -->

<a id="transport-tcp-tcp"></a>

<a id="tcp-transport"></a>

# TCP Transport

TCP is a connection oriented transport, so the [DomainParticipant](../../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) must establish a TCP connection
to the remote peer before sending data messages.
Therefore, one of the communicating DomainParticipants (the one acting as *server*) must open a TCP port listening for
incoming connections, and the other one (the one acting as *client*) must connect to this port.

#### NOTE
The *server* and *client* concepts are independent from the DDS concepts of
[Publisher](../../dds_layer/publisher/publisher.md#dds-layer-publisher), [Subscriber](../../dds_layer/subscriber/subscriber.md#dds-layer-subscriber),
[DataWriter](../../dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter), and [DataReader](../../dds_layer/subscriber/dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader).
Also, these concepts are independent from the *eProsima Discovery Server* *servers* and *clients*
([Discovery Server](../../discovery/discovery_server.md#discovery-server)).
Any of them can act as a *TCP Server* or *TCP Client* when establishing the connection,
and the DDS communication will work over this connection.

#### WARNING
This documentation assumes the reader has basic knowledge of TCP/IP concepts, since terms like
Time To Live (TTL), Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC), Transport Layer Security (TLS),
socket buffers, and port numbering are not explained in detail.
However, it is possible to configure a basic TCP transport on *Fast DDS* without this knowledge.

<a id="transport-tcp-transportdescriptor"></a>

<a id="tcptransportdescriptor"></a>

## TCPTransportDescriptor

*eProsima Fast DDS* implements TCP transport for both TCPv4 and TCPv6.
Each of these transports is independent from the other, and has its own [`TransportDescriptorInterface`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_descriptor_interface.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28TransportDescriptorInterfaceE).
However, they share many of their features, and most of the [`TransportDescriptorInterface`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_descriptor_interface.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28TransportDescriptorInterfaceE) data members are common.

The following table describes the common data members for both TCPv4 and TCPv6.

| Member                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Data type                                                                                                                                               | Default      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`sendBufferSize`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor14sendBufferSizeE)                                | `uint32_t`                                                                                                                                              | 0            | Size of the sending buffer of the socket (octets).<br/>**[Pro]** If 0, the operating system auto-tunes it (\*).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`receiveBufferSize`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor17receiveBufferSizeE)                          | `uint32_t`                                                                                                                                              | 0            | Size of the receiving buffer of the socket (octets).<br/>**[Pro]** If 0, the operating system auto-tunes it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`netmask_filter`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor14netmask_filterE)                                | `NetmaskFilterKind`                                                                                                                                     | `AUTO`       | See [Netmask filtering](../interfaces.md#netmask-filtering).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`allowlist`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor19interface_allowlistE)                                | `vector<pair<string, NetmaskFilterKind>>`                                                                                                               | Empty vector | List of allowed interfaces with<br/>netmask filter configuration.<br/>See [Allowlist](../interfaces.md#interfaces-allowlist).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`blocklist`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor19interface_blocklistE)                                | `vector<string>`                                                                                                                                        | Empty vector | List of blocked interfaces.<br/>See [Blocklist](../interfaces.md#interfaces-blocklist).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`interfaceWhiteList`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor18interfaceWhiteListE)                        | `vector<string>`                                                                                                                                        | Empty vector | List of allowed interfaces<br/>See [Interface Whitelist](../whitelist.md#whitelist-interfaces).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`TTL`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor3TTLE)                                                       | `uint8_t`                                                                                                                                               | 1            | Time to live, in number of hops.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [`listening_ports`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor15listening_portsE)                                                   | `vector<uint16_t>`                                                                                                                                      | Empty vector | List of ports to listen as *server*. If a port is set to 0, an available port will be automatically assigned.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`keep_alive_frequency_ms`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor23keep_alive_frequency_msE)                                   | `uint32_t`                                                                                                                                              | 0            | **[Pro]** Frequency of RTCP keep alive requests (in ms).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`keep_alive_timeout_ms`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor21keep_alive_timeout_msE)                                       | `uint32_t`                                                                                                                                              | 0            | **[Pro]** Time since sending the last keep alive request to consider a connection as broken (in ms).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [`max_logical_port`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor16max_logical_portE)                                                 | `uint16_t`                                                                                                                                              | 100          | Maximum number of logical ports to try during RTCP negotiation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`logical_port_range`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor18logical_port_rangeE)                                             | `uint16_t`                                                                                                                                              | 20           | Maximum number of logical ports per request to try during RTCP negotiation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [`logical_port_increment`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor22logical_port_incrementE)                                     | `uint16_t`                                                                                                                                              | 2            | Increment between logical ports to try during RTCP negotiation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [`enable_tcp_nodelay`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor18enable_tcp_nodelayE)                                             | `bool`                                                                                                                                                  | `false`      | Enables the TCP_NODELAY socket option.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [`non_blocking_send`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor17non_blocking_sendE)                                               | `bool`                                                                                                                                                  | `false`      | Do not block on send operations (\*).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [`calculate_crc`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor13calculate_crcE)                                                       | `bool`                                                                                                                                                  | `true`       | True to calculate and send CRC on message headers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`check_crc`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor9check_crcE)                                                                | `bool`                                                                                                                                                  | `true`       | True to check the CRC of incoming message headers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`apply_security`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor14apply_securityE)                                                     | `bool`                                                                                                                                                  | `false`      | True to use TLS. See [TLS over TCP](tls.md#transport-tcp-tls).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`tls_config`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor10tls_configE)                                                             | [`TLSConfig`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor9TLSConfigE) |              | Configuration for TLS. See [TLS over TCP](tls.md#transport-tcp-tls).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [`default_reception_threads`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/port_based_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28PortBasedTransportDescriptor25default_reception_threadsEv) | [ThreadSettings](../../dds_layer/core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#threadsettingsqos)                                                                   |              | Default [ThreadSettings](../../dds_layer/core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#threadsettingsqos) for the reception threads.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`reception_threads`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/port_based_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds4rtps28PortBasedTransportDescriptor17reception_threadsEv)                 | `std::map<uint32_t, ThreadSettings>`                                                                                                                    |              | [ThreadSettings](../../dds_layer/core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#threadsettingsqos) for the reception threads on specific ports.                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`keep_alive_thread`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor17keep_alive_threadE)                                               | [ThreadSettings](../../dds_layer/core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#threadsettingsqos)                                                                   |              | [ThreadSettings](../../dds_layer/core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#threadsettingsqos) for the thread keeping alive TCP connections.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`accept_thread`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor13accept_threadE)                                                       | [ThreadSettings](../../dds_layer/core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#threadsettingsqos)                                                                   |              | [ThreadSettings](../../dds_layer/core/policy/eprosimaExtensions.md#threadsettingsqos) for the threads processing incoming TCP connection requests.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`tcp_negotiation_timeout`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor23tcp_negotiation_timeoutE)                                   | `uint32_t`                                                                                                                                              | 0            | Time to wait for logical port negotiation (in ms). If a logical port is under negotiation, it waits for the<br/>negotiation to finish up to this timeout before trying to send a message to that port. Setting this option to<br/>non-zero values increases the discovery time. Setting it to zero means no wait but could lead to loss of first<br/>messages. |

#### WARNING
Although the member [`listening_ports`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor15listening_portsE) accepts multiple ports, only the first listening port
will be effectively used. The rest of the ports will be ignored.

#### NOTE
If [`listening_ports`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor15listening_portsE) is left empty, the participant will not be able to receive incoming
connections but will be able to connect to other participants that have configured their listening ports.

#### NOTE
When [`non_blocking_send`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor17non_blocking_sendE) is set to `true`, send operations will return immediately if the
send buffer might get full, but no error will be returned to the upper layer.
This means that the application will behave as if the packet is sent and lost.

When set to `false`, send operations will block until the network buffer has space for the
packet.

**[Pro]** As this check requires a fixed send buffer size, enabling [`non_blocking_send`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcp_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps22TCPTransportDescriptor17non_blocking_sendE) with
[`sendBufferSize`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/socket_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps25SocketTransportDescriptor14sendBufferSizeE) set to 0 disables the send buffer auto-tuning, and the system
default size is used instead.

<a id="transport-tcp-v4transportdescriptor"></a>

<a id="tcpv4transportdescriptor"></a>

### TCPv4TransportDescriptor

The following table describes the data members that are exclusive for [`TCPv4TransportDescriptor`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcpv4_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps24TCPv4TransportDescriptorE).

| Member                                                                                                                                                    | Data type   | Default      | Description                                                                                |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`wan_addr`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcpv4_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps24TCPv4TransportDescriptor8wan_addrE) | `octet[4]`  | [0, 0, 0, 0] | Configuration for WAN. See [WAN or Internet Communication over TCPv4](#transport-tcp-wan). |

#### NOTE
The [`kind`](../../api_reference/transport/transport_generic_interfaces/transport_interface.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds4rtps18TransportInterface4kindEv) value for a [`TCPv4TransportDescriptor`](../../api_reference/transport/tcp_transport/tcpv4_transport_descriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps24TCPv4TransportDescriptorE) is given by the value
[`LOCATOR_KIND_TCPv4`](../../api_reference/rtps/common/Locator/defines.md#c.LOCATOR_KIND_TCPv4).

<a id="transport-tcp-v6transportdescriptor"></a>
