`dds.sec.log.plugin` with the value `builtin.DDS_LogTopic`.
The following table outlines the properties used for the DDS:Logging:DDS_LogTopic plugin configuration.
For further information and examples follow the dedicated documentation: [Logging plugin: DDS:Logging:DDS_LogTopic](../security/logging_plugin/logging_plugin.md#logging-logtopic).

<a id="property-ignore-local-endpoints"></a>

<a id="ignore-local-endpoints"></a>

# Ignore Local Endpoints

By default, Fast DDS will automatically match all the endpoints (meaning [DataReaders](../dds_layer/subscriber/dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader) and [DataWriters](../dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter)) belonging to a
given [DomainParticipant](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) as soon as they share the same [Topic](../dds_layer/topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic) and have compatible Qos.
This however can result in undesired feedback whenever an application creates a [DataReader](../dds_layer/subscriber/dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader) and a [DataWriter](../dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter) under
the same [DomainParticipant](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) on a shared [Topic](../dds_layer/topic/topic.md#dds-layer-topic).
Although this feedback can be filtered out at the application level upon data reception by filtering out messages coming
from a [DataWriter](../dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter) belonging to the same [DomainParticipant](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) on the [DataReader](../dds_layer/subscriber/dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader) receiving the data (by looking at the
[`GuidPrefix_t`](../api_reference/rtps/common/GuidPrefix_t/GuidPrefix_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps12GuidPrefix_tE)), this entails for a data sample to go all the way to the [DataReaderListener](../dds_layer/subscriber/dataReaderListener/dataReaderListener.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareaderlistener) just to be discarded
by an overcomplicated application business logic.
For this reason, Fast DDS offers the possibility of instructing the [DomainParticipant](../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) to avoid the matching of local
endpoints through the following property:

| PropertyPolicyQos name             | PropertyPolicyQos value   | Default value   |
|------------------------------------|---------------------------|-----------------|
| `"fastdds.ignore_local_endpoints"` | `"true"`/`"false"`        | `"false"`       |

### C++

```c++
DomainParticipantQos participant_qos;

// Avoid local matching of this participant's endpoints
participant_qos.properties().properties().emplace_back(
    "fastdds.ignore_local_endpoints",
    "true");
```

### XML

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<dds xmlns="http://www.eprosima.com">
    <profiles>
        <participant profile_name="ignore_local_endpoints_domainparticipant_xml_profile">
            <rtps>
                <propertiesPolicy>
                    <properties>
                        <!-- Avoid local matching of this participant's endpoints -->
                        <property>
                            <name>fastdds.ignore_local_endpoints</name>
                            <value>true</value>
                        </property>
                    </properties>
                </propertiesPolicy>
            </rtps>
        </participant>
    </profiles>
</dds>
```

#### NOTE
An invalid value of `fastdds.ignore_local_endpoints` results in the default behaviour.

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/statistics/statistics.md -->

<!-- {{{ X-Types API -->
<!-- }}} -->

<a id="statistics"></a>

<a id="statistics-module"></a>

# Statistics Module

The *Fast DDS Statistics module* is an extension of Fast DDS that enables the recollection of data concerning the DDS
communication.
The collected data is published using DDS over dedicated topics using builtin DataWriters within the
*Statistics module*.
In *Fast DDS*, the *Statistics module* and the [Monitor Service](monitor_service/monitor_service.md#monitor-service) are compiled when the `FASTDDS_STATISTICS`
CMake option is enabled, which is the default (see [CMake options](../../installation/configuration/cmake_options.md#cmake-options)).
For more information about *Fast DDS* compilation, see [Linux installation from sources](../../installation/sources/sources_linux.md#linux-sources) and [Windows installation from sources](../../installation/sources/sources_windows.md#windows-sources).

**[Pro]** In *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**, the *Statistics module* and the [Monitor Service](monitor_service/monitor_service.md#monitor-service) are always available, so no
specific build configuration is required to use them.

Data is only collected and published for the statistics topics that are explicitly enabled, meaning that applications
that do not enable any of them are not affected.
Therefore, the user must enable those DataWriters that are publishing data on the topics of interest for the user’s
application.
To that end, the standard [DDS Layer](../dds_layer/dds_layer.md#dds-layer) has been extended with the statistics API (see
[Statistics Domain Participant](dds_layer/domainParticipant.md#statistics-domainparticipant)).
The following section explains it.

#### NOTE
Please refer to [Statistics QoS Troubleshooting](dds_layer/troubleshooting.md#statistics-troubleshooting) for any problems related to the statistics module.

* [Statistics Module DDS Layer](dds_layer/statistics_dds_layer.md)

In order to simplify its use, the API provides aliases for the different statistics topics (see
[Statistics topic names](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#api-statistics-topic-names)).
The following table shows the correlation between the topic name and the corresponding alias.

<a id="history-latency-topic"></a>

## [`HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics21HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPICE)

The `_fastdds_statistics_history2history_latency` statistics topic collects data related with the latency between any
two matched endpoints.
This measurement provides information about the DDS overall latency independent of the user’s application overhead.
Specifically, the measured latency corresponds to the time spent between the instant when the sample is written to the
DataWriter’s history and the time when the sample is added to the DataReader’s history and the notification is issued to
the corresponding user’s callback.

<a id="network-latency-topic"></a>

## [`NETWORK_LATENCY_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics21NETWORK_LATENCY_TOPICE)

#### NOTE
**[Pro]** This topic is not available in *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**, see [Statistics topics not available in Fast DDS](#statistics-topic-names-removed) .

The `_fastdds_statistics_network_latency` statistics topic collects data related with the network latency (expressed
in *ns*) between any two communicating locators.
This measurement provides information about the transport layer latency.
The measured latency corresponds to the time spent between the message being written until the message being received
in the `MessageReceiver`.

#### IMPORTANT
In the case of [TCP Transport](../../transport/tcp/tcp.md#transport-tcp-tcp), the reported latency also includes the time spent on the datagram’s CRC
related operations.
Mind that is possible to disable CRC operations when defining the [TCPTransportDescriptor](../../transport/tcp/tcp.md#transport-tcp-transportdescriptor).

<a id="publication-throughput-topic"></a>

## [`PUBLICATION_THROUGHPUT_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics28PUBLICATION_THROUGHPUT_TOPICE)

The `_fastdds_statistics_publication_throughput` statistics topic collects the amount of data (expressed in *B/s*)
that is being sent by each DataWriter.
This measurement provides information about the publication’s throughput.

<a id="subscription-throughput-topic"></a>

## [`SUBSCRIPTION_THROUGHPUT_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics29SUBSCRIPTION_THROUGHPUT_TOPICE)

The `_fastdds_statistics_subscription_throughput` statistics topic collects the amount of data (expressed in *B/s*)
that is being received by each DataReader.
This measurement provides information about the subscription’s throughput.

<a id="rtps-sent-topic"></a>

## [`RTPS_SENT_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics15RTPS_SENT_TOPICE)

#### NOTE
**[Pro]** This topic is not available in *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**, see [Statistics topics not available in Fast DDS](#statistics-topic-names-removed) .

The `_fastdds_statistics_rtps_sent` statistics topic collects the number of RTPS packets and bytes that are being sent
from each DDS entity to each locator.

<a id="rtps-lost-topic"></a>

## [`RTPS_LOST_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics15RTPS_LOST_TOPICE)

#### NOTE
**[Pro]** This topic is not available in *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**, see [Statistics topics not available in Fast DDS](#statistics-topic-names-removed) .

The `_fastdds_statistics_rtps_lost` statistics topic collects the number of RTPS packets and bytes that are being lost
in the transport layer (dropped somewhere in between) in the communication between each DDS entity and locator.

<a id="heartbeat-count-topic"></a>

## [`HEARTBEAT_COUNT_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics21HEARTBEAT_COUNT_TOPICE)

The `_fastdds_statistics_heartbeat_count` statistics topic collects the number of heartbeat messages sent by each
user’s DataWriter.
This topic does not apply to builtin (related to [Discovery](../../discovery/discovery.md#discovery)) and statistics DataWriters.
Heartbeat messages are only sent if the [ReliabilityQosPolicy](../../dds_layer/core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#reliabilityqospolicy) is set to [`RELIABLE_RELIABILITY_QOS`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/reliabilityqospolicykind.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24ReliabilityQosPolicyKind24RELIABLE_RELIABILITY_QOSE).
These messages report the DataWriter’s status.

<a id="acknack-count-topic"></a>

## [`ACKNACK_COUNT_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics19ACKNACK_COUNT_TOPICE)

The `_fastdds_statistics_acknack_count` statistics topic collects the number of acknack messages sent by each user’s
DataReader.
This topic does not apply to builtin DataReaders (related to [Discovery](../../discovery/discovery.md#discovery)).
Acknack messages are only sent if the [ReliabilityQosPolicy](../../dds_layer/core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#reliabilityqospolicy) is set to [`RELIABLE_RELIABILITY_QOS`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/reliabilityqospolicykind.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24ReliabilityQosPolicyKind24RELIABLE_RELIABILITY_QOSE).
These messages report the DataReader’s status.

<a id="nackfrag-count-topic"></a>

## [`NACKFRAG_COUNT_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics20NACKFRAG_COUNT_TOPICE)

The `_fastdds_statistics_nackfrag_count` statistics topic collects the number of nackfrag messages sent by each user’s
DataReader.
This topic does not apply to builtin DataReaders (related to [Discovery](../../discovery/discovery.md#discovery)).
Nackfrag messages are only sent if the [ReliabilityQosPolicy](../../dds_layer/core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#reliabilityqospolicy) is set to [`RELIABLE_RELIABILITY_QOS`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/reliabilityqospolicykind.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24ReliabilityQosPolicyKind24RELIABLE_RELIABILITY_QOSE).
These messages report the data fragments that have not been received yet by the DataReader.

<a id="gap-count-topic"></a>

## [`GAP_COUNT_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics15GAP_COUNT_TOPICE)

The `_fastdds_statistics_gap_count` statistics topic collects the number of gap messages sent by each user’s
DataWriter.
This topic does not apply to builtin (related to [Discovery](../../discovery/discovery.md#discovery)) and statistics DataWriters.
Gap messages are only sent if the [ReliabilityQosPolicy](../../dds_layer/core/policy/standardQosPolicies.md#reliabilityqospolicy) is set to [`RELIABLE_RELIABILITY_QOS`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/reliabilityqospolicykind.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24ReliabilityQosPolicyKind24RELIABLE_RELIABILITY_QOSE).
These messages report that some specific samples are not relevant to a specific DataReader.

<a id="data-count-topic"></a>

## [`DATA_COUNT_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics16DATA_COUNT_TOPICE)

The `_fastdds_statistics_data_count` statistics topic collects the total number of user’s data messages and data
fragments (in case that the message size is large enough to require RTPS fragmentation) that have been sent by each
user’s DataWriter.
This topic does not apply to builtin (related to [Discovery](../../discovery/discovery.md#discovery)) and statistics DataWriters.

<a id="resent-datas-topic"></a>

## [`RESENT_DATAS_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics18RESENT_DATAS_TOPICE)

The `_fastdds_statistics_resent_data` statistics topic collects the total number of user’s data messages and data
fragments (in case that the message size is large enough to require RTPS fragmentation) that have been necessary to
resend by each user’s DataWriter.
This topic does not apply to builtin (related to [Discovery](../../discovery/discovery.md#discovery)) and statistics DataWriters.

<a id="sample-datas-topic"></a>

## [`SAMPLE_DATAS_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics18SAMPLE_DATAS_TOPICE)

#### NOTE
**[Pro]** This topic is not available in *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**, see [Statistics topics not available in Fast DDS](#statistics-topic-names-removed) .

The `_fastdds_statistics_sample_datas` statistics topic collects the number of user’s data messages (or data fragments
in case that the message size is large enough to require RTPS fragmentation) that have been sent by the user’s
DataWriter to completely deliver a single sample.
This topic does not apply to builtin (related to [Discovery](../../discovery/discovery.md#discovery)) and statistics DataWriters.

<a id="pdp-packets-topic"></a>

## [`PDP_PACKETS_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics17PDP_PACKETS_TOPICE)

The `_fastdds_statistics_pdp_packets` statistics topic collects the number of PDP discovery traffic RTPS packets
transmitted by each DDS [`DomainParticipant`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipantE).
PDP packets are the data messages exchanged during the PDP discovery phase (see [Discovery phases](../../discovery/discovery.md#disc-phases) for more
information).

<a id="edp-packets-topic"></a>

## [`EDP_PACKETS_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics17EDP_PACKETS_TOPICE)

The `_fastdds_statistics_edp_packets` statistics topic collects the number of EDP discovery traffic RTPS packets
transmitted by each DDS [`DomainParticipant`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipantE).
EDP packets are the data messages exchanged during the EDP discovery phase (see [Discovery phases](../../discovery/discovery.md#disc-phases) for more
information).

<a id="statistics-topic-names-discovery"></a>

<a id="discovery-topic"></a>

## [`DISCOVERY_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics15DISCOVERY_TOPICE)

#### NOTE
**[Pro]** This topic is not available in *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**, see [Statistics topics not available in Fast DDS](#statistics-topic-names-removed) .

The `_fastdds_statistics_discovered_entity` statistics topic reports the time when each local [`DomainParticipant`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipantE)
discovers any remote DDS entity (with the exception of those DDS entities related with the *Fast DDS Statistics
module*).
This topic also carries the `PHYSICAL_DATA_TOPIC` information for the case of discovered [`DomainParticipant`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipantE); if the
discovered entity is either a [`DataReader`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/subscriber/datareader.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataReaderE) or [`DataWriter`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriter.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds10DataWriterE), then the physical information is empty (see
[Physical Data in Discovery Information](../../property_policies/non_consolidated_qos.md#property-policies-physical-data) for more information about how to configure the physical data conveyed on the
discovery messages).

<a id="statistics-topic-names-physical"></a>

<a id="physical-data-topic"></a>

## `PHYSICAL_DATA_TOPIC`

#### NOTE
**[Pro]** This topic is not available in *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**, see [Statistics topics not available in Fast DDS](#statistics-topic-names-removed) .

The `_fastdds_statistics_physical_data` statistics topic reports the host, user and process where the
*Fast DDS Statistics module* is running.

<a id="statistics-topic-names-removed"></a>

<a id="statistics-topics-not-available-in-fast-dds-pro"></a>

## Statistics topics not available in Fast DDS **[Pro]**

**[Pro]** The following statistics topics are published by *Fast DDS*, but they have been removed from *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**.
In *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**, enabling any of them has no effect, and a warning is logged.
Their names are still declared, and deprecated, so that applications referring to them keep building.

| **Topic name**                          | **Alias**               |
|-----------------------------------------|-------------------------|
| `_fastdds_statistics_network_latency`   | `NETWORK_LATENCY_TOPIC` |
| `_fastdds_statistics_rtps_sent`         | `RTPS_SENT_TOPIC`       |
| `_fastdds_statistics_rtps_lost`         | `RTPS_LOST_TOPIC`       |
| `_fastdds_statistics_discovered_entity` | `DISCOVERY_TOPIC`       |
| `_fastdds_statistics_sample_datas`      | `SAMPLE_DATAS_TOPIC`    |
| `_fastdds_statistics_physical_data`     | `PHYSICAL_DATA_TOPIC`   |

The Network Latency and RTPS Lost topics were derived from a dedicated submessage that *Fast DDS* appended to
every outgoing RTPS message.
*Fast DDS* **[Pro]** no longer sends that submessage, which reduces the size of every RTPS message.
The remaining topics were removed because no consumer used the data they reported.

In *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**, [`HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPIC`](../../api_reference/statistics/topic_names.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics21HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPICE) is the closest available latency measurement.
Mind that it is reported for each pair of DataWriter and DataReader, and that it covers the complete path
between both histories, which includes the network but is not limited to it.

The host, user and process where an application runs are still announced in the participant discovery message,
so in *Fast DDS* **[Pro]** they remain available without this topic (see [Physical Data in Discovery Information](../../property_policies/non_consolidated_qos.md#property-policies-physical-data)).

<a id="statistics-domainparticipant"></a>

<a id="statistics-domain-participant"></a>

# Statistics Domain Participant

In order to start collecting data in one of the statistics topics ([Statistics Topic names](topic_names.md#statistics-topic-names)), the corresponding
statistics DataWriter should be enabled.
In fact, *Fast DDS Statistics module* can be enabled and disabled at runtime.
For this purpose, *Fast DDS Statistics module* exposes an extended DDS `statistics::dds::DomainParticipant` API:

<a id="statistics-enable-datawriters"></a>

<a id="enable-statistics-datawriters"></a>

## Enable statistics DataWriters

Statistics DataWriters can be enabled in different ways.
It can be done automatically (see [Automatically enabling statistics DataWriters](#auto-enabling-statistics-datawriters)).
Alternatively, Statistics DataWriters can be enabled at run time using one of two methods:
[`enable_statistics_datawriter()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant28enable_statistics_datawriterERKNSt6stringERK13DataWriterQos) or [`enable_statistics_datawriter_with_profile()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant41enable_statistics_datawriter_with_profileERKNSt6stringERKNSt6stringE).

[`enable_statistics_datawriter()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant28enable_statistics_datawriterERKNSt6stringERK13DataWriterQos) method requires as parameters:

* Name of the statistics topic to be enabled (see [Statistics Topic names](topic_names.md#statistics-topic-names) for the statistics topic list).
* DataWriter QoS profile (see [Statistics DataWriter recommended QoS](qos.md#statistics-datawriter-qos) for the recommended profile).

It is possible to define specific desired QoS through DataWriter profile on the FASTDDS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE
(see [XML profiles](../../xml_configuration/xml_configuration.md#xml-profiles)).
[`enable_statistics_datawriter_with_profile()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant41enable_statistics_datawriter_with_profileERKNSt6stringERKNSt6stringE) method enables a DataWriter by searching a specific DataWriter XML profile.
On those profiles, specific QoS can be set.

[`enable_statistics_datawriter_with_profile()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant41enable_statistics_datawriter_with_profileERKNSt6stringERKNSt6stringE) method requires as parameters:

* Name of the XML profile to use to fill the QoS structure of the DataWriter.
* Name of the statistics topic name to be enabled. (see [Statistics Topic names](topic_names.md#statistics-topic-names) for the statistics topic list).

<a id="disable-statistics-datawriters"></a>

## Disable statistics DataWriters

Statistics DataWriters are disabled using the method [`disable_statistics_datawriter()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant29disable_statistics_datawriterERKNSt6stringE).
This method requires as parameter:

* Name of the statistics topic to be disabled (see [Statistics Topic names](topic_names.md#statistics-topic-names) for the statistics topic list).

<a id="example"></a>

## Example

<a id="obtain-pointer-to-the-extended-statisticsdomainparticipant-api-class"></a>

## Obtain pointer to the extended `statistics::dds::DomainParticipant` class

The [`DomainParticipant`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipantE) is created using the [`create_participant()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory18create_participantE10DomainId_tRK20DomainParticipantQosP25DomainParticipantListenerRK10StatusMask) provided by the
[`DomainParticipantFactory`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactoryE).
This method returns a pointer to the DDS standard DomainParticipant created.
In order to obtain the pointer to the child `statistics::dds::DomainParticipant` which extends the DDS API, the
`static` method [`narrow()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant6narrowEP17DomainParticipant) is provided.

#### NOTE
**[Pro]** In *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**, the statistics API is part of the [`DomainParticipant`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipantE) itself, so it can be called
directly on the pointer returned by [`create_participant()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory18create_participantE10DomainId_tRK20DomainParticipantQosP25DomainParticipantListenerRK10StatusMask).
`statistics::dds::DomainParticipant` is kept as an alias of [`DomainParticipant`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipantE), and [`narrow()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant6narrowEP17DomainParticipant) returns
the participant it is given, so code written for *Fast DDS* keeps working.

The following example shows how to use the Statistics module extended DDS API:

```c++
// Create a DomainParticipant
DomainParticipant* participant =
        DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0, PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);
if (nullptr == participant)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Enable statistics DataWriter
if (participant->enable_statistics_datawriter(eprosima::fastdds::statistics::GAP_COUNT_TOPIC,
        eprosima::fastdds::statistics::dds::STATISTICS_DATAWRITER_QOS) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Use the DomainParticipant to communicate
// (...)

// Disable statistics DataWriter
if (participant->disable_statistics_datawriter(eprosima::fastdds::statistics::GAP_COUNT_TOPIC) !=
        RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}

// Delete DomainParticipant
if (DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->delete_participant(participant) != RETCODE_OK)
{
    // Error
    return;
}
```

<a id="auto-enabling-statistics-datawriters"></a>

<a id="automatically-enabling-statistics-datawriters"></a>

## Automatically enabling statistics DataWriters

The statistics DataWriters can be directly enabled using the [DomainParticipantQos](../../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantqos)
[`properties()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantqos.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds20DomainParticipantQos10propertiesEv) `fastdds.statistics`.
The value of this property is a semicolon separated list containing the
[statistics topic name aliases](topic_names.md#statistics-topic-names) of those DataWriters that the user wants to enable.
The property can be set either programmatically or loading an XML file.
If the property is set in both ways, the priority would depend on the API and the QoS profile provided:

* XML settings have priority if [`create_participant_with_profile()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory31create_participant_with_profileE10DomainId_tRKNSt6stringEP25DomainParticipantListenerRK10StatusMask) is called with a valid
  participant profile.
* XML settings also have priority if [`create_participant()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory18create_participantE10DomainId_tRK20DomainParticipantQosP25DomainParticipantListenerRK10StatusMask) is called using
  [`PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds23PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULTE) and a participant profile exists in the XML file with the `is_default_profile` option
  set to `true` ([DomainParticipant XML attributes](../../xml_configuration/domainparticipant.md#domainparticipantattributes)).
* The property set programmatically is used only when [`create_participant()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds24DomainParticipantFactory18create_participantE10DomainId_tRK20DomainParticipantQosP25DomainParticipantListenerRK10StatusMask) is called with
  the specific QoS.

Another way of enabling statistics DataWriters, compatible with the previous one, is setting the
[FASTDDS_STATISTICS](../../env_vars/env_vars.md#env-vars-fastdds-statistics) environment variable.
The statistics DataWriters that will be enabled when the [`DomainParticipant`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipantE) is enabled would be the union between
those specified in the [`properties()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantqos.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds20DomainParticipantQos10propertiesEv) `fastdds.statistics` and those included with the
environment variable.

The following examples show how to use all the previous methods:

### C++

```c++
DomainParticipantQos pqos;

// Activate Fast DDS Statistics module
pqos.properties().properties().emplace_back("fastdds.statistics",
        "HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPIC;ACKNACK_COUNT_TOPIC;PDP_PACKETS_TOPIC");
```

### XML

```xml
<participant profile_name="statistics_domainparticipant_conf_xml_profile">
    <rtps>
        <propertiesPolicy>
            <properties>
                <!-- Activate Fast DDS Statistics Module -->
                <property>
                    <name>fastdds.statistics</name>
                    <value>HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPIC;ACKNACK_COUNT_TOPIC;PDP_PACKETS_TOPIC</value>
                </property>
            </properties>
        </propertiesPolicy>
    </rtps>
</participant>
```

### Environment Variable Linux

```bash
export FASTDDS_STATISTICS="HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPIC;ACKNACK_COUNT_TOPIC;PDP_PACKETS_TOPIC"
```

### Environment Variable Windows

```bash
set FASTDDS_STATISTICS=HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPIC;ACKNACK_COUNT_TOPIC;PDP_PACKETS_TOPIC
```

#### NOTE
These are all the statistics topics:

```bash
HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPIC;PUBLICATION_THROUGHPUT_TOPIC;SUBSCRIPTION_THROUGHPUT_TOPIC;HEARTBEAT_COUNT_TOPIC;ACKNACK_COUNT_TOPIC;NACKFRAG_COUNT_TOPIC;GAP_COUNT_TOPIC;DATA_COUNT_TOPIC;RESENT_DATAS_TOPIC;PDP_PACKETS_TOPIC;EDP_PACKETS_TOPIC
```

#### NOTE
Be aware that automatically enabling the statistics DataWriters using all these methods implies using the recommended
QoS profile [`STATISTICS_DATAWRITER_QOS`](../../api_reference/statistics/datawriter_qos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics3dds25STATISTICS_DATAWRITER_QOSE). For more information, please refer to [Statistics DataWriter recommended QoS](qos.md#statistics-datawriter-qos).
However, if an XML profile is defined, the QoS applied are those defined in the profile,
and for those QoS that are not specified in that profile, the default library QoS are applied
(see [DataWriterQos](../../dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriterqos) for the standard eProsima’s DataWriter QoS),
and not the recommended QoS for the Statistics DataWriters.

For the creation of an automatically enabled Datawriter, the priority for setting its QoS is the following:

* First, if a specific profile exists for the statistics topic, that one is applied.
* If that is not the case but a generic profile for statistics DataWriters exists, that one is applied.
* If no profile is defined in XML file, the recommended statistics QoS are applied.

#### NOTE
The generic DataWriter profile defined in the FASTDDS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE XML needs to be named as
GENERIC_STATISTICS_PROFILE.

The specific DataWriter profile defined in the FASTDDS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE XML needs to be named using the
same statistic topic alias or name (see [Statistics Topic names](topic_names.md#statistics-topic-names) for the alias corresponding to each statistic
topic) that has been used in the [DomainParticipantQos](../../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipantqos) [`properties()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipantqos.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds20DomainParticipantQos10propertiesEv) `fastdds.statistics`
(see [Statistics Module Settings](../../property_policies/non_consolidated_qos.md#property-policies-statistics)) or the [FASTDDS_STATISTICS](../../env_vars/env_vars.md#env-vars-fastdds-statistics) environment variable,
where the enabling of the corresponding statistics
topic has been set.

# Statistics recommended QoS

Although the statistics DataWriters can be enabled using any valid QoS profile, the recommended profile is presented
below.
Also, the DataReaders created by the user to receive the data being published by the statistics DataWriters can use any
compatible QoS profile.
However, a recommended DataReader QoS profile is also provided.

<a id="statistics-datawriter-qos"></a>

<a id="statistics-datawriter-recommended-qos"></a>

## Statistics DataWriter recommended QoS

The following table shows the recommended [`DataWriterQos`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/publisher/datawriterqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13DataWriterQosE) profile for enabling the statistics DataWriters.
This profile enables the `pull mode` [operating mode](../../property_policies/non_consolidated_qos.md#push-mode-qos-policy) on the statistics DataWriters.
This entails that the DataWriters will only send information upon the reception of acknack submessages sent by the
monitoring DataReader.
This QoS profile is always used when the statistics DataWriters are
[auto-enabled](domainParticipant.md#auto-enabling-statistics-datawriters).
The recommended profile can be accessed through the constant [`STATISTICS_DATAWRITER_QOS`](../../api_reference/statistics/datawriter_qos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds10statistics3dds25STATISTICS_DATAWRITER_QOSE).

<a id="statistics-troubleshooting"></a>

<a id="troubleshooting"></a>

# Troubleshooting

This section aims to give quick solutions to overcome the most common problems arising from the use of the statistics
module.

<a id="statistics-troubleshooting-notgettindata"></a>

<a id="monitoring-application-is-not-receiving-any-statistic-data"></a>

## Monitoring application is not receiving any statistic data

Sometimes, especially in the case of monitoring large applications with many DataWriters and DataReaders, it may happen
that the application monitoring Fast DDS statistics does not receive any data.
This is generally caused by the default configuration of the statistics DataWriters, which includes the
`push_mode` set to `false` (i.e. `pull_mode`), the History Kind set to `KEEP_LAST`, and the
History Depth set to `10`.
With this configuration, the following may happen:

1. Fast DDS adds new samples to one of the statistics DataWriters.
2. The DataWriter notifies the DataReader of the availability of said samples.
3. The DataReader sends a request to the DataWriter to “pull” those samples.
4. Before the request arrives to the DataWriter, some new statistics samples are added to that same DataWriter, which
   causes the previous samples to be overwritten.
5. Once the DataReader request arrives to the DataWriter, since the requested samples have been overwritten, they are
   not available any more, so the DataWriter send a notification to the DataReader informing of the presence of the
   newer samples instead.
6. The loop starts again.

The easiest fix to overcome this situation is to simply increase the History Depth of the DataWriter to create Some
buffer to answer to requests:

### Generic profile

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<dds xmlns="http://www.eprosima.com">
    <profiles>
        <participant profile_name="statistics_domainparticipant_conf_xml_general_profile">
            <rtps>
                <propertiesPolicy>
                    <properties>
                        <!-- Activate various Fast DDS Statistics Module DataWriters -->
                        <property>
                            <name>fastdds.statistics</name>
                            <value>HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPIC;PDP_PACKETS_TOPIC</value>
                        </property>
                    </properties>
                </propertiesPolicy>
            </rtps>
        </participant>

        <!-- Generic profile for all the statistics DataWriter -->
        <data_writer profile_name="GENERIC_STATISTICS_PROFILE">
            <!-- Configure History QoS as KEEP_LAST 20 -->
            <!-- History depth depends on the user application constraints (publication rate for instance) -->
            <topic>
                <historyQos>
                    <kind>KEEP_LAST</kind>
                    <depth>20</depth>
                </historyQos>
            </topic>
            <!-- Enable pull mode -->
            <propertiesPolicy>
                <properties>
                    <property>
                        <name>fastdds.push_mode</name>
                        <value>false</value>
                    </property>
                </properties>
            </propertiesPolicy>
            <!-- Set durability, reliability, and publication mode -->
            <qos>
                <durability>
                    <kind>TRANSIENT_LOCAL</kind>
                </durability>

                <reliability>
                    <kind>RELIABLE</kind>
                </reliability>

                <publishMode>
                    <kind>ASYNCHRONOUS</kind>
                </publishMode>
            </qos>
        </data_writer>
    </profiles>
</dds>
```

### Specific profile

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<dds xmlns="http://www.eprosima.com">
    <profiles>
        <participant profile_name="statistics_domainparticipant_conf_xml_specific_profile">
            <rtps>
                <propertiesPolicy>
                    <properties>
                        <!-- Activate various Fast DDS Statistics Module DataWriters -->
                        <property>
                            <name>fastdds.statistics</name>
                            <value>HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPIC</value>
                        </property>
                    </properties>
                </propertiesPolicy>
            </rtps>
        </participant>

        <!-- Generic profile for a specific statistics DataWriters -->
        <data_writer profile_name="HISTORY_LATENCY_TOPIC">
            <!-- Configure History QoS as KEEP_LAST 20 -->
            <!-- History depth depends on the user application constraints (publication rate for instance) -->
            <topic>
                <historyQos>
                    <kind>KEEP_LAST</kind>
                    <depth>20</depth>
                </historyQos>
            </topic>
            <!-- Enable pull mode -->
            <propertiesPolicy>
                <properties>
                    <property>
                        <name>fastdds.push_mode</name>
                        <value>false</value>
                    </property>
                </properties>
            </propertiesPolicy>
            <!-- Set durability, reliability, and publication mode -->
            <qos>
                <durability>
                    <kind>TRANSIENT_LOCAL</kind>
                </durability>

                <reliability>
                    <kind>RELIABLE</kind>
                </reliability>

                <publishMode>
                    <kind>ASYNCHRONOUS</kind>
                </publishMode>
            </qos>
        </data_writer>
    </profiles>
</dds>
```

#### WARNING
Mind that the specific profile only targets to the DataWriter which profile name matches with the alias of
the corresponding statistics topic.
Check the complete list of topics and their aliases in the [Statistics Topic names](topic_names.md#statistics-topic-names) section.

#### NOTE
Increasing the History Depth of the statistics DataWriters has an impact on memory usage, as sufficient space is
pre-allocated for each of the DataWriter’s histories to hold that number of samples per topic instance.

<a id="monitor-service"></a>

<a id="id1"></a>

# Monitor Service

The *Fast DDS* Monitor Service is a feature of Fast DDS that
grants the user the ability to collect data about the entities existing within
a particular [domain](../../dds_layer/domain/domain.md#dds-layer-domain) (i.e [DomainParticipants](../../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant), [DataReaders](../../dds_layer/subscriber/dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader), [DataWriters](../../dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter))
as well as the capability of detecting possible misconfigurations among them.

* [Introduction](intro.md)
  * [Keywords](intro.md#keywords)
  * [Description](intro.md#description)
  * [Use Cases](intro.md#use-cases)
* [Monitor Service Topics](monitor_service_topics.md)
  * [Monitor Service Status Topic](monitor_service_topics.md#monitor-service-status-topic)
* [Monitor Service Configuration](monitor_service_configuration.md)
  * [Endpoints QoS](monitor_service_configuration.md#endpoints-qos)

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/statistics/monitor_service/intro.md -->

<!-- {{{ X-Types API -->
<!-- }}} -->

<a id="monitor-intro"></a>

<a id="introduction"></a>

# Introduction

The `Monitor Service` targets any application implementing the subscription side of
the [Monitor Service Status Topic](monitor_service_topics.md#monitor-service-topics),
giving the possibility of retrieving the [Monitoring Information](#monitor-service-keywords)
of the local entities (incompatible QoS, deadlines missed,
active connections,…).

<a id="monitor-service-keywords"></a>

<a id="keywords"></a>

## Keywords

* **Proxy**: An entity that acts on behalf of another entity.
* **Proxy Data**: The way in which a Proxy can be described.
* **Monitoring Information**: The collection of different sources of information and statuses of an entity,
  including: the Proxy Data, incompatible QoS, connections, liveliness, deadlines missed, inconsistent
  topics and lost sample status.

<a id="description"></a>

## Description

Enabling the service makes each [DomainParticipant](../../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant) publish its local entities, each one with its related
`Monitoring Information`.

The [Monitor Service](monitor_service.md#monitor-service) is disabled by default, as it may entail a performance cost.
Further information on the [Monitor Service](monitor_service.md#monitor-service) topics and how to configure it is described
in the following sections.

The [Monitor Service](monitor_service.md#monitor-service) is available in both the [DDS Layer](../../dds_layer/dds_layer.md#dds-layer) and [RTPS Layer](../../rtps_layer/rtps_layer.md#rtps-layer).

<a id="monitor-service-in-rtps-note"></a>

#### NOTE
If the service is activated within a [RTPS](../../rtps_layer/rtps_layer.md#rtps-layer) context, not all the `Monitoring Information`
may be published by the service.

<a id="use-cases"></a>

## Use Cases

The [Monitor Service](monitor_service.md#monitor-service) can be particularly useful in the following scenarios:

* Collecting the `Monitoring Information` of any local entity of a remote [DomainParticipant](../../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant)
  in order to extend the default discovery information (see [Discovery](../../discovery/discovery.md#discovery)) about it.
* Troubleshooting issues regarding discovery or entity-matching, leveraging the information
  of the current locators in use, for example.
* Recreating an entity graph of a certain domain given that all participants are able to discover each other.

# Monitor Service Topics

The following table depicts the properties of the topics within the [Monitor Service](monitor_service.md#monitor-service):

| **Topic name**                   | **Topic Alias**       | **TopicDataType**                                           |
|----------------------------------|-----------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `fastdds_monitor_service_status` | MONITOR_SERVICE_TOPIC | [Monitor Service Status Data](#monitor-service-status-data) |

<a id="monitor-service-status-topic"></a>

<a id="id2"></a>

## Monitor Service Status Topic

The `Monitor Service Status Topic` carries information about the
[monitoring information](intro.md#monitor-service-keywords) of the local entities of a
particular [DomainParticipant](../../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant).
The [monitoring information](intro.md#monitor-service-keywords) can be divided into different statuses
identified by a `StatusKind`.
The possible values are described in the following table:

<a id="monitoring-statuses"></a>

|   **Value** | **Name**                  | **Description**                                                                                 |
|-------------|---------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|           0 | `ProxyInfo`               | Collection of Parameters describing the<br/>`Proxy Data` of that entity. Contains optional qos. |
|           1 | `ConnectionList`          | List of connections that this entity is<br/>using with its matched remote entities.             |
|           2 | `IncompatibleQoSInfo`     | Status of the Incompatible QoS<br/>of that entity.                                              |
|           3 | `InconsistentTopicInfo`   | Status of Inconsistent topics that the<br/>topic of that entity has.                            |
|           4 | `LivelinessLostInfo`      | Tracks the status of the number of times<br/>a writer lost liveliness.                          |
|           5 | `LivelinessChangedInfo`   | Tracks the status of the number of times<br/>the liveliness changed in a reader.                |
|           6 | `DeadlineMissedInfo`      | The Status of the number of deadlines<br/>missed of a sample for that entity.                   |
|           7 | `SampleLostInfo`          | Tracks the status of the number of times<br/>this entity lost samples.                          |
|           8 | `ExtendedIncompatibleQoS` | Stores the list of remote incompatible `GUIDs`<br/>and QoS policies for each local entity guid. |

#### NOTE
The `ProxyInfo` within the `Monitor Service Status Topic`
always includes the [optional qos](../../property_policies/non_consolidated_qos.md#property-serialize-optional-qos) independently of the
`fastdds.serialize_optional_qos` property.

#### NOTE
If the service is enabled in a [RTPS layer](../../rtps_layer/rtps_layer.md#rtps-layer) context, [not all
the statuses will be published](intro.md#monitor-service-in-rtps-note),
only the `ProxyInfo` and `ConnectionList`.

The `Monitor Service Status Topic` publishes new data when new updates are received from any
of the [DomainParticipant](../../dds_layer/domain/domainParticipant/domainParticipant.md#dds-layer-domainparticipant)’s local entities (on-event driven) with a minimum waiting time between
publications.
In addition, it is in charge of notifying about any disposal or liveliness lost.

<a id="monitor-service-status-data"></a>

<a id="id3"></a>

### Monitor Service Status Data

The `MonitorServiceStatusData` data structure comprises the following fields:

* *local_entity:* [`Guid_t`](../../api_reference/rtps/common/Guid/GUID_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds4rtps6GUID_tE) of the local entity.
* *status_kind:* [StatusKind](#monitoring-statuses) enumeration identifying the status.
* *value:* The value of the status.

```bash
MonitorServiceStatusData
  @Key GUID local_entity
  @Key StatusKind status_kind
  Data value
```

#### NOTE
The *local_entity* and *status_kind* are keyed fields, hence making use of instances (see [Topics, keys and instances](../../dds_layer/topic/instances.md#dds-layer-topic-instances)).
In this case, the pair <*local_entity, status_kind*> identifies a unique instance.

Each of the `StatusKind` enumeration values maps to a corresponding `Data` value.
The actual field names for the different values are described below:

* *entity_proxy:* Collection of the serialized Quality of Service Parameters in the form of a `ParameterList`.
* *connection_list:* Defines how is this entity communicating with its matched entities.
  Each of the elements is of Connection type (depicted below).

```bash
Connection
  uint32_t mode //INTRAPROCESS, DATASHARING, TRANSPORT
  LocatorList announced_locators
  LocatorList used_locators
```

* *incompatible_qos_status:* Status of the Incompatible QoS of that entity.
  * [DataWriter](../../dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter) Incompatible QoS Offered.
  * [DataReader](../../dds_layer/subscriber/dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader) Incompatible QoS Requested.
* *inconsistent_topic_status:* Status of Inconsistent topics of the topic of that entity.
  Asked to the topic of the requested entity.
* *liveliness_lost_status:* Tracks the status of the number of times that liveliness was lost by a
  [DataWriter](../../dds_layer/publisher/dataWriter/dataWriter.md#dds-layer-publisher-datawriter).
* *liveliness_changed_status:* Tracks the status of the number of times that liveliness was lost
  by a [DataReader](../../dds_layer/subscriber/dataReader/dataReader.md#dds-layer-subscriber-datareader).
* *deadline_status:* The Status of the number of deadlines missed that were registered in that entity.
* *sample_lost_status:* The number of samples that entity lost.
* *extended_incompatible_qos_status:* Details a list of remote GUIDs with incompatible QoS with
  a local entity and the particular [`QosPolicyId_t`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/qospolicyid_t.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds13QosPolicyId_tE) of those incompatible policies.

```bash
ExtendedIncompatibleQoSStatus_s
  GUID remote_guid
  sequence<unsigned long> current_incompatible_policies

ExtendedIncompatibleQoSStatusSeq = sequence<ExtendedIncompatibleQoSStatus>
```

The following table depicts the relation between each of the `StatusKind` values and the `Data` field:

|   **StatusKind** | **StatusKind Name**       | **Data field Name**              | **IDL Data field Type**          |
|------------------|---------------------------|----------------------------------|----------------------------------|
|                0 | `ProxyInfo`               | entity_proxy                     | sequence<octet>                  |
|                1 | `ConnectionList`          | connection_list                  | sequence<Connection>             |
|                2 | `IncompatibleQoSInfo`     | incompatible_qos_status          | IncompatibleQoSStatus            |
|                3 | `InconsistentTopicInfo`   | inconsistent_topic_status        | InconsistentTopicStatus          |
|                4 | `LivelinessLostInfo`      | liveliness_lost_status           | LivelinessLostStatus             |
|                5 | `LivelinessLostInfo`      | liveliness_changed_status        | LivelinessChangedStatus          |
|                6 | `DeadlineMissedInfo`      | deadline_missed_status           | DeadlineMissedStatus             |
|                7 | `SampleLostInfo`          | sample_lost_status               | SampleLostStatus                 |
|                8 | `ExtendedIncompatibleQoS` | extended_incompatible_qos_status | ExtendedIncompatibleQoSStatusSeq |

<!-- Source: https://fast-dds.docs.eprosima.com/en/latest/fastdds/statistics/monitor_service/monitor_service_configuration.md -->

<a id="monitor-service-configuration"></a>

<a id="id1"></a>

# Monitor Service Configuration

In *Fast DDS*, the [Monitor Service](monitor_service.md#monitor-service) can be activated using the `-DFASTDDS_STATISTICS=ON` at CMake
configuration step (for further information regarding the *Fast DDS* compilation, see [Linux installation from sources](../../../installation/sources/sources_linux.md#linux-sources) and
[Windows installation from sources](../../../installation/sources/sources_windows.md#windows-sources)).
**[Pro]** In *Fast DDS* **[Pro]**, it is always compiled in.
Once the [Monitor Service](monitor_service.md#monitor-service) feature is activated, it can be programmatically enabled in both [DDS Layer](../../dds_layer/dds_layer.md#dds-layer) and
[RTPS Layer](../../rtps_layer/rtps_layer.md#rtps-layer) through the [`enable_monitor_service()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant22enable_monitor_serviceEv) and
[`disable_monitor_service()`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant23disable_monitor_serviceEv) calls.
In addition, leveraging the [`PropertyPolicyQos`](../../api_reference/dds_pim/core/policy/propertypolicyqos.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17PropertyPolicyQosE) there is new `Property` defined
for the purpose: `fastdds.enable_monitor_service`.

The following table depicts the different ways in which the *Monitor Service* can be enabled or disabled:

### C++ API

```c++

DomainParticipant* participant = DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0,
                PARTICIPANT_QOS_DEFAULT);

// Enable Fast DDS Monitor Service through API
participant->enable_monitor_service();

// Disable Fast DDS Monitor Service through API
participant->disable_monitor_service();


```

### C++ Property

```c++
DomainParticipantQos pqos;

// Enable Fast DDS Monitor Service through properties
pqos.properties().properties().emplace_back("fastdds.enable_monitor_service",
        "true");

// Enable Fast DDS Monitor Service through statistics properties (other way)
pqos.properties().properties().emplace_back("fastdds.statistics",
        "MONITOR_SERVICE_TOPIC");

DomainParticipant* participant_with_mon_srv = DomainParticipantFactory::get_instance()->create_participant(0,
                pqos);

```

### XML

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
<profiles xmlns="http://www.eprosima.com">
<participant profile_name="monitor_service_participant_xml_profile">
    <rtps>
        <propertiesPolicy>
            <properties>
                <!-- Enable Monitor Service -->
                <property>
                    <name>fastdds.enable_monitor_service</name>
                    <value>true</value>
                </property>
                <!-- Include Monitor Service in the Fast DDS Statistics (other way to enable it) -->
                <property>
                    <name>fastdds.statistics</name>
                    <value>MONITOR_SERVICE_TOPIC</value>
                </property>
            </properties>
        </propertiesPolicy>
    </rtps>
</participant>
</profiles>
```

### Env. Variable Linux

```bash
export FASTDDS_STATISTICS="MONITOR_SERVICE_TOPIC"
```

### Env. Variable Windows

```bash
set FASTDDS_STATISTICS=MONITOR_SERVICE_TOPIC
```

# XTypes

*eProsima Fast DDS* supports the OMG [Extensible and Dynamic Topic Types for DDS](https://www.omg.org/spec/DDS-XTypes/1.3) specification (also known as XTypes).
This specification defines the following concepts:

* DDS supported type system, including the concept of extensible types that might evolve in time.
* Type representation, including [IDL](../../fastddsgen/dataTypes/dataTypes.md#fastddsgen-idl-datatypes) and [TypeObject](discovery_matching.md#xtypes-discovery-matching)
  representations.
* Data representation over the wire.
* Language binding, defining both a plain and a dynamic language binding.
  [eProsima Fast DDS-Gen](../../fastddsgen/introduction/introduction.md#fastddsgen-intro) generates the plain language binding given an IDL type representation.
  [Dynamic Language Binding](language_binding.md#xtypes-language-binding) section explains the required API to define and set/read the data types.
* DDS builtin mechanism to automatically discover remote data types.
  More information in [Remote Data Types Discovery](discovery_matching.md#xtypes-discovery-matching) section.

<a id="xtypes-discovery-matching"></a>

<a id="remote-data-types-discovery"></a>

# Remote Data Types Discovery

[DDS-XTypes specification](https://www.omg.org/spec/DDS-XTypes/1.3) defines an internal mechanism to discover the remote data types at runtime and match
depending on the extensible types compatibility rules configured using the [TypeConsistencyEnforcementQosPolicy](../dds_layer/core/policy/xtypesExtensions.md#typeconsistencyenforcementqospolicy).

#### NOTE
*eProsima Fast DDS* does not support XTypes compatibility check yet.

The remote data type discovery mechanism is based on the exchange of the data type information optimized in order to
reduce the required bandwidth.
On the one hand, `TypeInformation` structure defined in the IDL below (extracted from Annex B of the
[DDS-XTypes specification](https://www.omg.org/spec/DDS-XTypes/1.3)), is used to communicate the Topic Data Type and its dependencies.

```omg-idl
@extensibility(APPENDABLE) @nested
struct TypeIdentfierWithSize
{
    TypeIdentifier      type_id;
    unsigned long       typeobject_serialized_size;
};

@extensibility(APPENDABLE) @nested
struct TypeIdentifierWithDependencies
{
    TypeIdentfierWithSize           typeid_with_size;
    long                            dependent_type_id_count;
    sequence<TypeIdentfierWithSize> dependent_typeids;
};

@extensibility(MUTABLE) @nested
struct TypeInformation
{
    @id(0x1001) TypeIdentifierWithDependencies minimal;
    @id(0x1002) TypeIdentifierWithDependencies complete;
};
```

`TypeInformation` includes the `TypeIdentifier`, the data type information hashed which identifies almost
univocally the data type.
The data type information is contained in the `TypeObject` union:

```omg-idl
@extensibility(APPENDABLE) @nested
union TypeObject switch(octet)
{
    case EK_COMPLETE:
        CompleteTypeObject  complete;
    case EK_MINIMAL:
        MinimalTypeObject   minimal;
};
```

The `CompleteTypeObject` includes the data type full description.
On the other hand, `MinimalTypeObject` only includes the minimum required information in order to check type
compatibility.

#### IMPORTANT
Current TypeObject representation implementation does not support forward declarations or recursive data types
defined using the `@external` annotation.
Please, remember to disable TypeObject generation code using `-no-typeobjectsupport` option when generating
the code using Fast DDS-Gen.

<a id="prerequisites"></a>

## Prerequisites

The remote data type discovery feature only works if some requisites are met:

1. The local data types must be registered into the [`ITypeObjectRegistry`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/typeobjectregistry.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds6xtypes19ITypeObjectRegistryE).
   The types are automatically registered when calling [`register_type()`](../api_reference/dds_pim/domain/domainparticipant.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DomainParticipant13register_typeE11TypeSupportRKNSt6stringE) /
   [`register_type()`](../api_reference/dds_pim/topic/typesupport.md#_CPPv4NK8eprosima7fastdds3dds11TypeSupport13register_typeEP17DomainParticipant) if the code required for registration has been generated using
   [eProsima Fast DDS-Gen](../../fastddsgen/introduction/introduction.md#fastddsgen-intro).
   Fast DDS-Gen generates the required files ( *<IDLFileName>TypeObjectSupport.cxx/.hpp*) by default.

   #### NOTE
   `-no-typeobjectsupport` option disables the generation of these files and effectively disables the
   discovery of remote types.
2. `TypeInformation` should be received with the DomainParticipant’s endpoint discovery information.
   A DomainParticipant that does not inform about its `TypeInformation` would not trigger the remote data type
   discovery mechanism.

If the prerequisites are not met, endpoint matching relies on type name and topic name in order to match the discovered
endpoints.

<a id="xtypes-discovery-matching-config"></a>

## Configuration

The level of propagation of local data types can be configured as specified in [Type Propagation](../property_policies/non_consolidated_qos.md#property-type-propagation).

<a id="xtypes-language-binding"></a>

<a id="dynamic-language-binding"></a>

# Dynamic Language Binding

The Dynamic Language Binding API allows to define data types at runtime instead of having the types predefined as it is
required by the Plain Language Binding.
This API includes both the type definition and, the getters and setters required to use the defined types.
Type definition can also be done using a XML configuration file as explained in [Dynamic Types profiles](../xml_configuration/dynamic_types.md#xmldynamictypes) section or by
parsing an IDL file at runtime, as explained in [Dynamic Types IDL Parsing](idl_parsing.md#dynamic-types-idl-parsing) section.

This section presents first the Dynamic Language Binding API, and then the supported types and specific examples
defining and using those types.

<a id="xtypes-interfaces"></a>

<a id="dynamic-language-binding-interfaces"></a>

## Dynamic Language Binding Interfaces

This section briefly presents the Dynamic Language Binding API.
For more information, please refer both to the [DDS-XTypes specification](https://www.omg.org/spec/DDS-XTypes/1.3)
and the [API reference](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamic_types.md#dynamic-language-binding-api).

<a id="typedescriptor"></a>

### TypeDescriptor

[`TypeDescriptor`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/typedescriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds14TypeDescriptorE) is in charge of describing the state of a type.
Objects of this interface have value semantics allowing the TypeDescriptor data to be deeply copied and compared.

<a id="annotationdescriptor"></a>

### AnnotationDescriptor

[`AnnotationDescriptor`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/annotationdescriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds20AnnotationDescriptorE) is in charge of describing the user-defined applied annotation to a specific element.
Objects of this interface have value semantics allowing the AnnotationDescriptor data to be deeply copied and compared.

<a id="memberdescriptor"></a>

### MemberDescriptor

[`MemberDescriptor`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/memberdescriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds16MemberDescriptorE) is in charge of describing the state of a specific member of a type.
Objects of this interface have value semantics allowing the MemberDescriptor data to be deeply copied and compared.

<a id="verbatimtextdescriptor"></a>

### VerbatimTextDescriptor

[`VerbatimTextDescriptor`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/verbatimtextdescriptor.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds22VerbatimTextDescriptorE) is in charge of describing the `@verbatim` builtin annotation application.
Objects of this interface have value semantics allowing the VerbatimTextDescriptor data to be deeply copied and
compared.

<a id="dynamictypebuilderfactory"></a>

### DynamicTypeBuilderFactory

The [`DynamicTypeBuilderFactory`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamictypebuilderfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds25DynamicTypeBuilderFactoryE) serves as a singleton which instance is responsible for both creating and deleting
[`DynamicTypeBuilder`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamictypebuilder.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DynamicTypeBuilderE) objects.
This class provides the generic [`DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::create_type`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamictypebuilderfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds25DynamicTypeBuilderFactory11create_typeEN6traitsI14TypeDescriptorE8ref_typeE) API, and also specific APIs to define other
basic types such as strings, sequences, etc.
More information can be found in [Supported Types](#xtypes-supportedtypes) section.

<a id="dynamictype"></a>

### DynamicType

[`DynamicType`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamictype.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds11DynamicTypeE) objects represents a specific type definition.
Once the DynamicType has been built, it cannot be modified.
Objects of this interface have reference semantics, so the API receives a nil-reference which is then returned pointing
to the correct DynamicType address.

<a id="dynamictypemember"></a>

### DynamicTypeMember

[`DynamicTypeMember`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamictypemember.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds17DynamicTypeMemberE) represents a data member of a DynamicType.
Objects of this interface have reference semantics, so the API receives a nil-reference which is then returned pointing
to the correct DynamicTypeMember address.

<a id="dynamictypebuilder"></a>

### DynamicTypeBuilder

[`DynamicTypeBuilder`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamictypebuilder.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DynamicTypeBuilderE) interface allows the instantiation of concrete DynamicType objects and serves as a transitional
state for configuring the DynamicType before its creation.
Upon definition, DynamicTypeBuilderFactory leverages the information contained in the builder to create
the DynamicType.
[`DynamicTypeBuilder::build`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamictypebuilder.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DynamicTypeBuilder5buildEv) allows for creating the fully constructed DynamicType.
Builders remain reusable after DynamicType creation, ensuring changes to the builder do not affect previously
created types.

<a id="dynamicdatafactory"></a>

### DynamicDataFactory

[`DynamicDataFactory`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamicdatafactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds18DynamicDataFactoryE) serves as a singleton which instance is responsible for both creating and deleting
[`DynamicData`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamicdata.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds11DynamicDataE) objects from a given DynamicType instance.

<a id="dynamicdata"></a>

### DynamicData

[`DynamicData`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamicdata.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds11DynamicDataE) represents a data instance of a DynamicType, providing functionalities to access
and modify data values.
Each DynamicData object corresponds to an object of the type represented by its DynamicType.
Offering reflective getters and setters, DynamicData enables manipulation of individual data samples.

<a id="xtypes-supportedtypes"></a>

<a id="supported-types"></a>

## Supported Types

This section describes the supported Type System including examples of how to instantiate those specific types using the
Dynamic Language Binding API and the XML configuration file.
The C++ examples also include instantiating the corresponding DynamicData sample, and setting and reading a value.

The table below summarizes which types can be used with each of the ways of building a dynamic type at runtime.
Data types defined in an IDL file and processed with *Fast DDS-Gen* to generate code are covered by
[Supported IDL types](../../fastddsgen/dataTypes/dataTypes.md#fastddsgen-supported-idl-types) instead.

| Type                                                        | Dynamic Language Binding support                          | XML Dynamic Type profiles support                         | IDL Parsing Dynamic Type support                          |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| [Primitive Types](#xtypes-supportedtypes-primitive)         | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         |
| [String Types](#xtypes-supportedtypes-string)               | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         |
| [Enumeration Types](#xtypes-supportedtypes-enumeration)     | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         |
| [Alias Types](#xtypes-supportedtypes-alias)                 | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         |
| [Sequence types](#xtypes-supportedtypes-sequence)           | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         |
| [Array types](#xtypes-supportedtypes-array)                 | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         |
| [Map Types](#xtypes-supportedtypes-map)                     | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         | ❌                                                         |
| [Structure Types](#xtypes-supportedtypes-structure)         | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         |
| [Structure Inheritance](#xtypes-supportedtypes-inheritance) | ✅                                                         | ❌                                                         | ✅ **[Pro]**                                               |
| [Union Types](#xtypes-supportedtypes-union)                 | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         |
| [Bitmask Types](#xtypes-supportedtypes-bitmask)             | ✅                                                         | ✅                                                         | ✅ **[Pro]**                                               |
| [Bitset Types](#xtypes-supportedtypes-bitset)               | ✅                                                         | ⚠️ (inheritance not supported)                            | ✅ **[Pro]**                                               |
| [Annotations](#xtypes-annotations)                          | See the [annotations table](#xtypes-builtin-annotations). | See the [annotations table](#xtypes-builtin-annotations). | See the [annotations table](#xtypes-builtin-annotations). |

<a id="xtypes-supportedtypes-primitive"></a>

<a id="primitive-types"></a>

### Primitive Types

Primitive types are self-describing and can be created without configuration parameters.
The [`DynamicTypeBuilderFactory`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamictypebuilderfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds25DynamicTypeBuilderFactoryE) interface exposes the method [`DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_primitive_type`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamictypebuilderfactory.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds25DynamicTypeBuilderFactory18get_primitive_typeE8TypeKind)
to allow users to directly get the corresponding primitive DynamicType.
The [`DynamicData`](../api_reference/dds_pim/xtypes/dynamicdata.md#_CPPv4N8eprosima7fastdds3dds11DynamicDataE) class provides specific getters and setters for each primitive data type.

The following table shows the supported primitive types and their corresponding `TypeKind`.
The `TypeKind` is used to query the DynamicTypeBuilderFactory for the specific primitive DynamicType.

| C++ Type      | TypeKind               |
|---------------|------------------------|
| `bool`        | `TK_BOOLEAN`           |
| `char`        | `TK_CHAR8`             |
| `wchar_t`     | `TK_CHAR16`            |
| `uint8_t`     | `TK_BYTE` / `TK_UINT8` |
| `int8_t`      | `TK_INT8`              |
| `int16_t`     | `TK_INT16`             |
| `uint16_t`    | `TK_UINT16`            |
| `int32_t`     | `TK_INT32`             |
| `uint32_t`    | `TK_UINT32`            |
| `int64_t`     | `TK_INT64`             |
| `uint64_t`    | `TK_UINT64`            |
| `float`       | `TK_FLOAT32`           |
| `double`      | `TK_FLOAT64`           |
| `long double` | `TK_FLOAT128`          |

The example below shows how to create an structure with primitive members.

### OMG-IDL

```omg-idl
struct PrimitivesStruct
{
    boolean my_bool;
    octet my_octet;
    char my_char;
    wchar my_wchar;
    long my_long;
    unsigned long my_ulong;
    int8 my_int8;
    uint8 my_uint8;
    short my_short;
    unsigned short my_ushort;
    long long my_longlong;
    unsigned long long my_ulonglong;
    float my_float;
    double my_double;
    long double my_longdouble;
};
```

### XML

```xml
<struct name="PrimitivesStruct">
    <member name="my_bool" type="boolean"/>
    <member name="my_octet" type="byte"/>
    <member name="my_char" type="char8"/>
    <member name="my_wchar" type="char16"/>
    <member name="my_long" type="int32"/>
    <member name="my_ulong" type="uint32"/>
    <member name="my_int8" type="int8"/>
    <member name="my_uint8" type="uint8"/>
    <member name="my_short" type="int16"/>
    <member name="my_ushort" type="uint16"/>
    <member name="my_longlong" type="int64"/>
    <member name="my_ulonglong" type="uint64"/>
    <member name="my_float" type="float32"/>
    <member name="my_double" type="float64"/>
    <member name="my_longdouble" type="float128"/>
</struct>
```

### C++

```c++
// Define a struct type with various primitive members
TypeDescriptor::_ref_type type_descriptor {traits<TypeDescriptor>::make_shared()};
type_descriptor->kind(TK_STRUCTURE);
type_descriptor->name("PrimitivesStruct");
DynamicTypeBuilder::_ref_type struct_builder {DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->
                                                      create_type(type_descriptor)};

// Define and add primitive members to the struct
MemberDescriptor::_ref_type member_descriptor {traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared()};
member_descriptor->name("my_bool");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_BOOLEAN));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_octet");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_BYTE));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_char");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_CHAR8));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_wchar");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_CHAR16));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_long");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_INT32));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_ulong");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_UINT32));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_int8");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_INT8));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_uint8");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_UINT8));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_short");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_INT16));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_ushort");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_UINT16));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_longlong");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_INT64));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_ulonglong");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_UINT64));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_float");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_FLOAT32));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_double");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_FLOAT64));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);
member_descriptor = traits<MemberDescriptor>::make_shared();
member_descriptor->name("my_longdouble");
member_descriptor->type(DynamicTypeBuilderFactory::get_instance()->get_primitive_type(TK_FLOAT128));
struct_builder->add_member(member_descriptor);

// Build the struct type
DynamicType::_ref_type struct_type {struct_builder->build()};
// Create dynamic data based on the struct type
DynamicData::_ref_type data {DynamicDataFactory::get_instance()->create_data(struct_type)};

// Set and retrieve values for a member of type int32_t
int32_t in_value {2};
int32_t out_value {0};
data->set_int32_value(data->get_member_id_by_name("my_long"), in_value);
data->get_int32_value(out_value, data->get_member_id_by_name("my_long"));
```

For a detailed explanation about the XML definition of this type,
please refer to [XML Primitive Types](../xml_configuration/dynamic_types.md#xmldynamictypes-primivites).

<a id="type-promotions"></a>

#### Type promotions

The Dynamic Language Binding also supports type promotion, enabling implicit promotion of types during both `get()`
and `set()` operations.
This means that a smaller type can be implicitly promoted to a larger type, but not the other way around.

The following promotions are supported:

| TypeKind      | Allowed promotions                                                                                                                              |
|---------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `TK_INT8`     | `TK_INT16`, `TK_INT32`, `TK_INT64`, `TK_FLOAT32`, `TK_FLOAT64`, `TK_FLOAT128`                                                                   |
| `TK_INT16`    | `TK_INT32`, `TK_INT64`, `TK_FLOAT32`, `TK_FLOAT64`, `TK_FLOAT128`                                                                               |
| `TK_INT32`    | `TK_INT64`, `TK_FLOAT64`, `TK_FLOAT128`                                                                                                         |
